1: # c_3sat
2: 
3: C port of `knowledge/3sat` (the Rust `context-3sat` experiment): an incremental
4: stochastic local-search 3-SAT engine for `little.AI` context handling.
5: 
6: Dependency-free C11 (GNU extensions: GCC/Clang). It returns **SAT** (verified
7: against the input) or **UNKNOWN** when the budget runs out. It never claims
8: UNSAT: local search cannot prove it.
9: 
10: ## Build / test
11: 
12: ```sh
13: make -C knowledge/c_3sat build   # -> build/3sat
14: make -C knowledge/c_3sat test    # ASan + UBSan test run
15: make -C knowledge/c_3sat bench N=20000 RATIO=3.5 SEED=1
16: ```
17: 
18: ## Run
19: 
20: ```sh
21: knowledge/c_3sat/build/3sat input.cnf
22: knowledge/c_3sat/build/3sat input.cnf --steps 250000 --restarts 40 --noise 0.20 --seed 42
23: knowledge/c_3sat/build/3sat input.cnf --strategy greedy --progress 100000 --out out.json
24: ```
25: 
26: Default output: `./knowledge/c_3sat/results/latest.json` (relative to cwd), same
27: JSON shape as the Rust version. Exit codes: `0` SAT, `1` input/output/internal
28: error, `2` usage error, `3` budget exhausted (UNKNOWN).
29: 
30: ## Design
31: 
32: **Rust-like errors** (`src/result.h`). Fallible functions return a tagged
33: `Result` instead of using errno or sentinel values:
34: 
35: ```c
36: typedef RESULT(Cnf) ResultCnf;                 // { bool ok; union { Cnf val; Error err; } }
37: Cnf cnf = TRY_CTX(ResultInt, cnf_from_dimacs_file(path), "Failed to load CNF");  // like `?` + .context()
38: return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_PARSE, "line %zu: ...", n);                           // like Err(...)
39: ```
40: 
41: `TRY`, `TRY_CTX` (adds context) and `TRY0` (for `Result<()>`) early-return the
42: error from the enclosing function. Named typedefs are required per result type
43: (two anonymous structs are different types in C).
44: 
45: **Functions as variables.**
46: 
47: - `PickFn` chooses the variable to flip from the scored candidates. It is stored
48:   in `SolverConfig.pick`; built-ins are `ranked` (default, the original
49:   heuristic), `greedy`, `random`, selected by `--strategy` through the
50:   `STRATEGIES` name table.
51: - `ProgressFn` is an optional observer called every N flips (`--progress N`).
52: - CLI flags are a table of `{flag, handler}` function pointers (`OPTS` in `main.c`).
53: 
54: Adding a heuristic = write a `PickFn`, add one row to `STRATEGIES`.
55: 
56: **Speed / energy.**
57: 
58: - Flat CSR arrays for clauses and variable occurrences (no per-clause allocations).
59: - Variable states (prime/neutral, break/make counts) are derived *lazily*, only for
60:   the 2-3 variables of the clause actually examined, in one pass. A flip only
61:   updates clause counters and the rogue-clause index. On random 3-SAT this is
62:   ~10x faster than re-ranking every variable in every touched clause, with
63:   identical search decisions (same seed -> same steps).
64: 
65: ## Differences from the Rust version
66: 
67: - If the very last allowed flip satisfies the formula, C reports SAT. The Rust
68:   loop only checks at the top of a step, so it could report UNKNOWN with 0
69:   unsatisfied clauses.
70: - `make_count` equals `rogue_occurrences` (a rogue clause has no true literal),
71:   so both come from the same pass.
72: - Extra options: `--strategy`, `--progress`.
73: 
74: ## Layout
75: 
76: ```
77: src/result.h   Result/Error/TRY macros
78: src/sat.h      public API
79: src/sat.c      DIMACS parser, strategies, solver
80: src/main.c     CLI
81: tests/         test_sat.c + fixtures
82: tools/gen_cnf.py   random 3-CNF generator
83: ```

137:     TRY0(ResultUnit, ensure_parent_dir(path));
138:     FILE *f = fopen(path, "wb");
139:     if (!f) return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_IO, "Cannot write result %s: %s", path, strerror(errno));
140:     if (r->status == SOLVE_SAT) {
141:         fprintf(f, "{\n  \"status\": \"SAT\",\n  \"variables\": %zu,\n  \"clauses\": %zu,\n"
142:                    "  \"steps\": %zu,\n  \"restart\": %zu,\n  \"assignment\": [",
143:                 cnf->n_vars, cnf->n_clauses, r->steps, r->restart);
144:         for (size_t i = 0; i < r->n_vars; i++) fprintf(f, "%s%s", i ? ", " : "", r->assignment[i] ? "true" : "false");
145:         fprintf(f, "]\n}\n");
146:     } else {
147:         fprintf(f, "{\n  \"status\": \"UNKNOWN\",\n  \"variables\": %zu,\n  \"clauses\": %zu,\n"
148:                    "  \"steps\": %zu,\n  \"best_unsatisfied\": %zu\n}\n",
149:                 cnf->n_vars, cnf->n_clauses, r->steps, r->best_unsatisfied);
150:     }
151:     if (fclose(f) != 0) return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_IO, "Cannot write result %s: %s", path, strerror(errno));
152:     return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
153: }
154: 
155: /* ---- run --------------------------------------------------------------- */
156: 
157: static ResultInt solve_and_report(const Cnf *cnf, const Cli *cli) {
158:     if (!cnf_is_3sat(cnf))
159:         fprintf(stderr, "Warning: input contains clauses longer than 3 literals; solving general CNF instead of strict 3-SAT.\n");
160:     Solver *solver = TRY(ResultInt, solver_new(cnf, cli->cfg.seed));
161:     ResultSolve rs = solver_solve(solver, &cli->cfg);
162:     solver_free(solver);
163:     SolveResult res = TRY(ResultInt, rs);
164: 
165:     if (res.status == SOLVE_SAT && !verify(cnf, res.assignment, res.n_vars)) {
166:         solve_result_free(&res);
167:         return ERRF(ResultInt, ERR_VERIFY, "Internal verification failed");
168:     }
169:     ResultUnit w = write_json(cli->output, cnf, &res);
170:     if (!w.ok) { solve_result_free(&res); return ERR(ResultInt, w.err); }
171: 
172:     int code;
173:     if (res.status == SOLVE_SAT) {
174:         printf("SAT (%zu steps, restart %zu) \xe2\x80\x94 %s\n", res.steps, res.restart, cli->output);
175:         code = 0;
176:     } else {
177:         printf("UNKNOWN (%zu steps, best %zu unsatisfied) \xe2\x80\x94 %s\n", res.steps, res.best_unsatisfied, cli->output);
178:         code = 3;
179:     }
180:     solve_result_free(&res);
181:     return OK(ResultInt, code);
182: }
183: 
184: static ResultInt run(int argc, char **argv) {
185:     Cli cli = { .input = NULL, .output = DEFAULT_OUT, .cfg = solver_config_default() };
186:     TRY0(ResultInt, parse_args(argc, argv, &cli));
187:     Cnf cnf = TRY_CTX(ResultInt, cnf_from_dimacs_file(cli.input), "Failed to load CNF");
188:     ResultInt r = solve_and_report(&cnf, &cli);
189:     cnf_free(&cnf);
190:     return r;
191: }
192: 
193: int main(int argc, char **argv) {
194:     ResultInt r = run(argc, argv);
195:     if (r.ok) return r.val;
196:     fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", r.err.msg);
197:     if (r.err.kind == ERR_USAGE) { usage(); return 2; }
198:     return 1;
199: }

1: # sound_detector — notes
2: 
3: Two time-domain ideas, no FFT, no scipy: **fading** and **bands**.
4: 
5: - `bands.py` — ~230 lines: biquad bandpass bank (10 bands, 100 Hz–6.3 kHz),
6:   rectified envelope followers, per-band release-edge measurement, 5 rules.
7:   Self-check on synthetic signals + CLI for wav files.
8: - `mod.py` — modulation clocks per band (syllable 3–8 Hz, beat 0.3–2.5 Hz)
9:   by autocorrelation of a detrended decimated envelope. No FFT.
10: - `sound_detector.cpp` — the two above ported to C-style C++17 with
11:   `std::variant` errors: `--selftest` + wav CLI, zero dependencies.
12: 
13: ## The core idea
14: 
15: A voice is **n frequencies that fade in unison** — a handful of harmonics
16: share one 30–80 ms release. A song is many frequencies fading at *staggered*
17: times. Hiss fades all at once; a drone never fades. The biquad bank gives us
18: a per-band envelope, and `_fades` finds every 20 dB descent in each band.
19: The discriminator is `short_fades / fades` (per-band descents < 150 ms over
20: all): voice high, music ≈ 0.
21: 
22: ## What is measured
23: 
24: | feature | how |
25: |---|---|
26: | `rms_db` | silence gate at -50 dBFS |
27: | `fades_per_band` | every 20 dB descent per band, in ms |
28: | `short_fades` | descents < 150 ms, summed over all bands |
29: | `fades` | descents on the summed envelope (total activity) |
30: | `spread_hz` | energy-weighted width of the band profile |
31: | `band_std` | flatness of the band profile in dB (hiss = flat) |
32: 
33: ## Rules
34: 
35: ```
36: silence      rms < -50 dBFS
37: no fades     -> noise if band_std < 4.5, else music   (hiss vs drone/pad)
38: short_fades > 33% of fades -> voice
39: >= 2 fades   -> music
40: 1 fade       -> voice if spread > 700 Hz, else music   (short clips)
41: ```
42: 
43: ## Measured (16 kHz mono, 1–2 s windows)
44: 
45: | input | truth | got | short/fades | spread | flat |
46: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
47: | synth voice (4 Hz syllables) | voice | voice | 76/11 | 541 Hz | 6.9 dB |
48: | synth chord, 120 ms decay | music | music | 0/3 | 340 Hz | 9.4 dB |
49: | synth pad (sustained) | music | music | 0/0 | 282 Hz | 10.9 dB |
50: | synth white noise | noise | noise | 0/0 | 1949 Hz | 4.1 dB |
51: | `alsa/Front_Center.wav` (real speech) | voice | voice | 37/3 | 554 Hz | 6.7 dB |
52: | `speech-dispatcher/test.wav` (TTS, 0.5 s) | voice | voice | 7/1 | 990 Hz | 5.7 dB |
53: | KDE chime | music | music | 0/5 | 647 Hz | 7.4 dB |
54: | `alsa/Noise.wav` | noise | noise | 0/0 | 1171 Hz | 3.5 dB |
55: 
56: ## Confirmed
57: 
58: - Voice is n harmonics fading in unison; short fade ratio is high.
59: - Music is many freqs fading at staggered times; short fade ratio ≈ 0.
60: - Noise has no release edges at all, and a flat band profile (< 4.5 dB std).
61: - 10 biquads per band, ~0.6 s of numpy per 1 s of audio. C++ will be
62:   realtime with no dependency.
63: 
64: ## Open / known weak spots
65: 
66: - Short clip (<1 s) has ≤2 total fades, so the ratio test is skipped and
67:   `spread` decides; the threshold needs device data, not 8 files.
68: - Dense music mixes have both fades and a flat spectrum; `band_std` is only
69:   trusted in the no-fade branch for this reason.
70: - TTS sample released in 200 ms (above the 150 ms cutoff); the ratio
71:   test still passed it.
72: - `n_bands_fading` is *not* the discriminator (voice and music both have all
73:   10 bands active). The right discriminator is `short_fades / fades`.
74: - Next step: 20–30 one-second clips per class from the actual device, tune
75:   3 thresholds (band_std 4.5, fade cutoff 150, spread 700) and nothing else.
76: 
77: ## Dense-mix collapse (the headline failure)
78: 
79: Scan of `02. Lost Yo Mind.mp3` (227 s, 45×5 s windows) through `bands.classify`:
80: **voice=45, music=0**. Every section, including instrumental, reads voice.

80:     for (size_t i = 0; i < cnf->n_clauses; i++)
81:         if (cnf_clause_len(cnf, i) > 3) return false;
82:     return true;
83: }
84: 
85: ResultCnf cnf_from_dimacs_str(const char *input) {
86:     Error err = {0};
87:     int64_t *tok = NULL; size_t ntok = 0, captok = 0;
88:     Lit *cur = NULL; size_t ncur = 0, capcur = 0;
89:     size_t capoff = 0, caplit = 0, nlit = 0;
90:     Cnf cnf = {0};
91:     size_t n_vars = 0, expected = 0;
92:     bool have_header = false;
93: 
94: #define FAIL(kind, ...) do { err = error_make((kind), __VA_ARGS__); goto fail; } while (0)
95: 
96:     /* Pass 1: header + raw integer tokens. */
97:     size_t line_no = 0;
98:     const char *p = input;
99:     while (*p) {
100:         line_no++;
101:         const char *eol = strchr(p, '\n');
102:         size_t llen = eol ? (size_t)(eol - p) : strlen(p);
103:         const char *line = p;
104:         p = eol ? eol + 1 : p + llen;
105:         while (llen && is_ws(*line)) { line++; llen--; }
106:         while (llen && is_ws(line[llen - 1])) llen--;
107:         if (llen == 0 || line[0] == 'c') continue;
108: 
109:         if (line[0] == 'p') {
110:             struct { const char *s; size_t n; } f[5];
111:             size_t nf = 0, i = 0;
112:             while (i < llen) {
113:                 while (i < llen && is_ws(line[i])) i++;
114:                 if (i >= llen) break;
115:                 size_t st = i;
116:                 while (i < llen && !is_ws(line[i])) i++;
117:                 if (nf < 5) { f[nf].s = line + st; f[nf].n = i - st; }
118:                 nf++;
119:             }
120:             if (nf != 4 || f[1].n != 3 || memcmp(f[1].s, "cnf", 3) != 0)
121:                 FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "line %zu: expected `p cnf VARS CLAUSES`", line_no);
122:             if (!parse_usize(f[2].s, f[2].n, &n_vars))
123:                 FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "line %zu: invalid variable count", line_no);
124:             if (!parse_usize(f[3].s, f[3].n, &expected))
125:                 FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "line %zu: invalid clause count", line_no);
126:             have_header = true;
127:             continue;
128:         }
129: 
130:         size_t i = 0;
131:         while (i < llen) {
132:             while (i < llen && is_ws(line[i])) i++;
133:             if (i >= llen) break;
134:             size_t st = i;
135:             while (i < llen && !is_ws(line[i])) i++;
136:             int64_t v;
137:             if (!parse_i64(line + st, i - st, &v))
138:                 FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "line %zu: invalid DIMACS token `%.*s`", line_no, (int)(i - st), line + st);
139:             if (!vec_reserve((void **)&tok, &captok, sizeof *tok, ntok + 1)) FAIL(ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
140:             tok[ntok++] = v;
141:         }
142:     }
143:     if (!have_header) FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "missing `p cnf` header");
144:     if (n_vars > UINT32_MAX) FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "variable count %zu is too large", n_vars);
145: 
146:     /* Pass 2: build clauses; drop duplicate literals and tautologies. */
147:     cnf.n_vars = n_vars;
148:     if (!vec_reserve((void **)&cnf.off, &capoff, sizeof *cnf.off, 1)) FAIL(ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
149:     cnf.off[0] = 0;
150: 
151:     for (size_t t = 0; t < ntok; t++) {
152:         int64_t value = tok[t];
153:         if (value != 0) {
154:             if (value == INT64_MIN) FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "literal integer overflow");
155:             uint64_t abs = value < 0 ? (uint64_t)(-value) : (uint64_t)value;
156:             if (abs > n_vars) FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "literal %lld is outside 1..=%zu", (long long)value, n_vars);
157:             if (!vec_reserve((void **)&cur, &capcur, sizeof *cur, ncur + 1)) FAIL(ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
158:             cur[ncur++] = (Lit){ (uint32_t)(abs - 1), value > 0 };
159:             continue;
160:         }
161:         size_t start = cnf.off[cnf.n_clauses], appended = 0;
162:         bool taut = false;
163:         for (size_t c = 0; c < ncur && !taut; c++) {
164:             bool dup = false;
165:             for (size_t k = 0; k < appended; k++) {
166:                 Lit e = cnf.lits[start + k];
167:                 if (e.var != cur[c].var) continue;
168:                 if (e.positive != cur[c].positive) taut = true; else dup = true;
169:                 break;
170:             }
171:             if (taut || dup) continue;
172:             if (!vec_reserve((void **)&cnf.lits, &caplit, sizeof *cnf.lits, start + appended + 1)) FAIL(ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
173:             cnf.lits[start + appended++] = cur[c];
174:         }
175:         ncur = 0;
176:         if (taut) continue;
177:         if (!vec_reserve((void **)&cnf.off, &capoff, sizeof *cnf.off, cnf.n_clauses + 2)) FAIL(ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
178:         cnf.off[++cnf.n_clauses] = start + appended;
179:         nlit = start + appended;
180:     }
181:     (void)nlit;
182:     if (ncur != 0) FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "unterminated clause: missing 0");
183:     if (cnf.n_clauses > expected)
184:         FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "header declares %zu clauses, parsed %zu", expected, cnf.n_clauses);
185: 
186:     free(tok);
187:     free(cur);
188:     if (!cnf.lits) cnf.lits = malloc(sizeof *cnf.lits); /* keep non-NULL for empty formulas */
189:     return OK(ResultCnf, cnf);
190: 
191: fail:
192:     free(tok);
193:     free(cur);
194:     cnf_free(&cnf);
195:     return ERR(ResultCnf, err);
196: #undef FAIL
197: }
198: 
199: ResultCnf cnf_from_dimacs_file(const char *path) {
200:     FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
201:     if (!f) return ERRF(ResultCnf, ERR_IO, "cannot open %s: %s", path, strerror(errno));
202:     char *buf = NULL;
203:     size_t len = 0, cap = 0;
204:     for (;;) {
205:         if (!vec_reserve((void **)&buf, &cap, 1, len + 4097)) { free(buf); fclose(f); return ERRF(ResultCnf, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory"); }
206:         size_t n = fread(buf + len, 1, 4096, f);
207:         len += n;
208:         if (n < 4096) break;
209:     }
210:     bool bad = ferror(f);
211:     fclose(f);
212:     if (bad) { free(buf); return ERRF(ResultCnf, ERR_IO, "cannot read %s", path); }
213:     buf[len] = '\0';
214:     ResultCnf r = cnf_from_dimacs_str(buf);
215:     free(buf);
216:     return r;
217: }
218: 
219: bool verify(const Cnf *cnf, const bool *assignment, size_t len) {
220:     if (len < cnf->n_vars) return false;
221:     for (size_t i = 0; i < cnf->n_clauses; i++) {
222:         const Lit *c = cnf_clause(cnf, i);
223:         size_t n = cnf_clause_len(cnf, i);
224:         bool any = false;
225:         for (size_t k = 0; k < n && !any; k++) any = lit_value(c[k], assignment[c[k].var]);
226:         if (!any) return false;
227:     }
228:     return true;
229: }
230: 
231: /* ======================================================================== */
232: /* pick strategies (the function-as-variable part)                          */
233: /* ======================================================================== */
234: 
235: size_t pick_ranked(Rng *rng, const Candidate *c, size_t n, double noise) {
236:     size_t neutral = 0;
237:     while (neutral < n && c[neutral].cls == 0) neutral++;
238:     size_t pool = neutral > 0 ? neutral : n;
239:     if (rng_f64(rng) < noise) return c[rng_index(rng, pool)].var;
240:     return c[0].var;
241: }
242: 
243: size_t pick_greedy(Rng *rng, const Candidate *c, size_t n, double noise) {
244:     (void)rng; (void)n; (void)noise;
245:     return c[0].var;
246: }
247: 
248: size_t pick_random(Rng *rng, const Candidate *c, size_t n, double noise) {
249:     (void)noise;
250:     return c[rng_index(rng, n)].var;
251: }
252: 
253: const Strategy STRATEGIES[] = {
254:     { "ranked", pick_ranked },
255:     { "greedy", pick_greedy },
256:     { "random", pick_random },
257: };
258: const size_t N_STRATEGIES = sizeof STRATEGIES / sizeof STRATEGIES[0];
259: 
260: PickFn pick_fn_by_name(const char *name) {
261:     for (size_t i = 0; i < N_STRATEGIES; i++)
262:         if (strcmp(STRATEGIES[i].name, name) == 0) return STRATEGIES[i].fn;
263:     return NULL;
264: }
265: 
266: SolverConfig solver_config_default(void) {
267:     return (SolverConfig){
268:         .max_steps = 100000, .restarts = 20, .noise = 0.22,
269:         .seed = 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL, .pick = pick_ranked,
270:         .on_progress = NULL, .progress_ctx = NULL, .progress_every = 0,
271:     };
272: }
273: 
274: /* ======================================================================== */
275: /* solver                                                                   */
276: /* ======================================================================== */
277: 
278: typedef struct { uint32_t clause; bool positive; } Occ;
279: 
280: struct Solver {
281:     const Cnf *cnf;
282:     bool *assignment;
283:     uint32_t *sat;          /* currently-true literal count per clause (0 == rogue) */
284:     size_t *occ_off;        /* CSR occurrence index, n_vars + 1 entries */
285:     Occ *occ;
286:     size_t *rogue;          /* clause ids currently rogue, for O(1) selection */
287:     size_t n_rogue;
288:     size_t *rogue_pos;      /* SIZE_MAX when not rogue */
289:     VarStats *stats;
290:     bool stats_dirty;       /* variable states are derived lazily */
291:     Candidate *cands;
292:     size_t max_len;
293:     Rng rng;
294: };
295: 
296: static size_t occ_count(const Solver *s, size_t v) { return s->occ_off[v + 1] - s->occ_off[v]; }
297: 
298: void solver_free(Solver *s) {
299:     if (!s) return;
300:     free(s->assignment); free(s->sat); free(s->occ_off); free(s->occ);
301:     free(s->rogue); free(s->rogue_pos); free(s->stats); free(s->cands);
302:     free(s);
303: }
304: 
305: static void add_rogue(Solver *s, size_t c) {
306:     if (s->rogue_pos[c] != SIZE_MAX) return;
307:     s->rogue_pos[c] = s->n_rogue;
308:     s->rogue[s->n_rogue++] = c;
309: }
310: 
311: static void remove_rogue(Solver *s, size_t c) {
312:     size_t pos = s->rogue_pos[c];
313:     if (pos == SIZE_MAX) return;
314:     size_t last = s->rogue[--s->n_rogue];
315:     if (pos < s->n_rogue) { s->rogue[pos] = last; s->rogue_pos[last] = pos; }
316:     s->rogue_pos[c] = SIZE_MAX;
317: }
318: 
319: static void rebuild_counts(Solver *s) {
320:     const Cnf *cnf = s->cnf;
321:     s->n_rogue = 0;
322:     for (size_t ci = 0; ci < cnf->n_clauses; ci++) {
323:         const Lit *c = cnf_clause(cnf, ci);
324:         size_t n = cnf_clause_len(cnf, ci), count = 0;
325:         for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) count += lit_value(c[k], s->assignment[c[k].var]);
326:         s->sat[ci] = (uint32_t)count;
327:         s->rogue_pos[ci] = SIZE_MAX;
328:     }
329:     for (size_t ci = 0; ci < cnf->n_clauses; ci++)
330:         if (s->sat[ci] == 0) add_rogue(s, ci);
331:     s->stats_dirty = true;
332: }
333: 
334: ResultSolver solver_new(const Cnf *cnf, uint64_t seed) {
335:     if (cnf->n_clauses > UINT32_MAX) return ERRF(ResultSolver, ERR_PARSE, "too many clauses (%zu)", cnf->n_clauses);
336:     Solver *s = calloc(1, sizeof *s);
337:     if (!s) return ERRF(ResultSolver, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
338:     size_t nv = cnf->n_vars, nc = cnf->n_clauses;
339:     size_t total = cnf->off[nc];
340:     s->cnf = cnf;
341:     s->rng = rng_new(seed);
342:     s->assignment = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *s->assignment);
343:     s->sat = calloc(nc ? nc : 1, sizeof *s->sat);
344:     s->occ_off = calloc(nv + 1, sizeof *s->occ_off);
345:     s->occ = malloc((total ? total : 1) * sizeof *s->occ);
346:     s->rogue = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *s->rogue);
347:     s->rogue_pos = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *s->rogue_pos);
348:     s->stats = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *s->stats);
349:     if (!s->assignment || !s->sat || !s->occ_off || !s->occ || !s->rogue || !s->rogue_pos || !s->stats) {
350:         solver_free(s);
351:         return ERRF(ResultSolver, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
352:     }
353:     for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++) {
354:         size_t n = cnf_clause_len(cnf, ci);
355:         if (n > s->max_len) s->max_len = n;
356:         for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) s->occ_off[cnf_clause(cnf, ci)[k].var + 1]++;
357:     }
358:     for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) s->occ_off[v + 1] += s->occ_off[v];
359:     size_t *fill = malloc((nv ? nv : 1) * sizeof *fill);
360:     s->cands = malloc((s->max_len ? s->max_len : 1) * sizeof *s->cands);
361:     if (!fill || !s->cands) { free(fill); solver_free(s); return ERRF(ResultSolver, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory"); }
362:     memcpy(fill, s->occ_off, nv * sizeof *fill);
363:     for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++) {
364:         size_t n = cnf_clause_len(cnf, ci);
365:         for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) {
366:             Lit l = cnf_clause(cnf, ci)[k];
367:             s->occ[fill[l.var]++] = (Occ){ (uint32_t)ci, l.positive };
368:         }
369:     }
370:     free(fill);
371:     for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) s->stats[v].rank = SIZE_MAX;
372:     rebuild_counts(s);
373:     return OK(ResultSolver, s);
374: }
375: 
376: /* Re-derive one variable's state, break and make counts from the current
377:  * assignment in a single pass over its occurrences. */
378: static void refresh_var(Solver *s, size_t v) {
379:     size_t satisfied = 0, rogue_occ = 0, breaks = 0, min_support = SIZE_MAX;
380:     bool prime = false;
381:     bool val = s->assignment[v];
382:     for (size_t i = s->occ_off[v]; i < s->occ_off[v + 1]; i++) {
383:         Occ o = s->occ[i];
384:         uint32_t c = s->sat[o.clause];
385:         if (c == 0) { rogue_occ++; continue; }
386:         if (val == o.positive) {
387:             satisfied++;
388:             if (c < min_support) min_support = c;
389:             if (c == 1) { prime = true; breaks++; }
390:         }
391:     }
392:     VarStats *st = &s->stats[v];
393:     st->satisfied_occurrences = satisfied;
394:     st->rogue_occurrences = rogue_occ;
395:     st->break_count = breaks;
396:     st->make_count = rogue_occ;  /* a rogue clause has no true literal, so every incidence is a "make" */
397:     st->rank = SIZE_MAX;
398:     if (occ_count(s, v) == 0) { st->state = VAR_UNUSED; st->min_support = 0; }
399:     else if (prime) { st->state = VAR_PRIME; st->min_support = 1; }
400:     else { st->state = VAR_NEUTRAL; st->min_support = satisfied == 0 ? 0 : min_support; }
401: }
402: 
403: static void refresh_all(Solver *s) {
404:     for (size_t v = 0; v < s->cnf->n_vars; v++) refresh_var(s, v);
405:     s->stats_dirty = false;
406: }
407: 
408: void solver_flip(Solver *s, size_t var) {
409:     s->assignment[var] = !s->assignment[var];
410:     s->stats_dirty = true;  /* states are re-derived lazily, only for candidates actually examined */
411:     for (size_t i = s->occ_off[var]; i < s->occ_off[var + 1]; i++) {
412:         Occ o = s->occ[i];
413:         uint32_t old = s->sat[o.clause];
414:         bool now_true = s->assignment[var] == o.positive;
415:         uint32_t nw = now_true ? old + 1 : old - 1;
416:         s->sat[o.clause] = nw;
417:         if (old == 0 && nw > 0) remove_rogue(s, o.clause);
418:         else if (old > 0 && nw == 0) add_rogue(s, o.clause);
419:     }
420: }
421: 
422: static int cand_cmp(const Candidate *a, const Candidate *b) {
423:     if (a->cls != b->cls) return a->cls < b->cls ? -1 : 1;                 /* neutral before prime */
424:     if (a->support != b->support) return a->support > b->support ? -1 : 1; /* stronger support first */
425:     if (a->breaks != b->breaks) return a->breaks < b->breaks ? -1 : 1;     /* fewer breaks */
426:     if (a->makes != b->makes) return a->makes > b->makes ? -1 : 1;         /* more makes */
427:     return a->var < b->var ? -1 : (a->var > b->var);
428: }
429: 
430: /* Score the variables of one rogue clause and sort them best-first. */
431: static size_t rank_candidates(Solver *s, size_t clause) {
432:     const Lit *c = cnf_clause(s->cnf, clause);
433:     size_t n = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, clause);
434:     for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) {
435:         size_t v = c[k].var;
436:         refresh_var(s, v);
437:         const VarStats *st = &s->stats[v];
438:         Candidate cd = { v, 0, 0, st->break_count, st->make_count };
439:         switch (st->state) {
440:             case VAR_NEUTRAL: cd.cls = 0; cd.support = st->min_support; break;
441:             case VAR_PRIME:   cd.cls = 1; cd.support = 1; break;
442:             case VAR_UNUSED:  cd.cls = 2; cd.support = SIZE_MAX; break;
443:         }
444:         size_t j = k;  /* insertion sort: clauses are tiny */
445:         while (j > 0 && cand_cmp(&cd, &s->cands[j - 1]) < 0) { s->cands[j] = s->cands[j - 1]; j--; }
446:         s->cands[j] = cd;
447:     }
448:     for (size_t r = 0; r < n; r++) s->stats[s->cands[r].var].rank = r;
449:     return n;
450: }
451: 
452: static void random_assignment(Solver *s, bool majority) {
453:     for (size_t v = 0; v < s->cnf->n_vars; v++) {
454:         size_t pos = 0, total = occ_count(s, v);
455:         for (size_t i = s->occ_off[v]; i < s->occ_off[v + 1]; i++) pos += s->occ[i].positive;
456:         size_t neg = total - pos;
457:         s->assignment[v] = (majority && pos != neg) ? pos > neg : rng_bool(&s->rng);
458:     }
459:     rebuild_counts(s);
460: }
461: 
462: static ResultSolve make_sat(const Solver *s, size_t steps, size_t restart) {
463:     size_t nv = s->cnf->n_vars;
464:     bool *a = malloc(nv ? nv : 1);
465:     if (!a) return ERRF(ResultSolve, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
466:     if (nv) memcpy(a, s->assignment, nv);
467:     return OK(ResultSolve, ((SolveResult){ SOLVE_SAT, a, nv, steps, restart, 0 }));
468: }
469: 
470: ResultSolve solver_solve(Solver *s, const SolverConfig *cfg) {
471:     const Cnf *cnf = s->cnf;
472:     for (size_t i = 0; i < cnf->n_clauses; i++)
473:         if (cnf_clause_len(cnf, i) == 0)
474:             return OK(ResultSolve, ((SolveResult){ SOLVE_UNKNOWN, NULL, cnf->n_vars, 0, 0, cnf->n_clauses }));
475:     if (cnf->n_clauses == 0) {
476:         memset(s->assignment, 0, cnf->n_vars);
477:         return make_sat(s, 0, 0);
478:     }
479:     PickFn pick = cfg->pick ? cfg->pick : pick_ranked;
480:     size_t total = 0, best = SIZE_MAX;
481:     for (size_t restart = 0; restart <= cfg->restarts; restart++) {
482:         random_assignment(s, restart == 0);
483:         for (size_t step = 0; step < cfg->max_steps; step++) {
484:             if (s->n_rogue == 0) return make_sat(s, total, restart);
485:             if (s->n_rogue < best) best = s->n_rogue;
486:             size_t clause = s->rogue[rng_index(&s->rng, s->n_rogue)];
487:             size_t n = rank_candidates(s, clause);
488:             if (n == 0) break;
489:             solver_flip(s, pick(&s->rng, s->cands, n, cfg->noise));
490:             total++;
491:             if (cfg->on_progress && cfg->progress_every && total % cfg->progress_every == 0)
492:                 cfg->on_progress(cfg->progress_ctx, total, s->n_rogue);
493:         }
494:         if (s->n_rogue == 0) return make_sat(s, total, restart);  /* last flip solved it */
495:     }
496:     if (s->n_rogue < best) best = s->n_rogue;
497:     return OK(ResultSolve, ((SolveResult){ SOLVE_UNKNOWN, NULL, cnf->n_vars, total, 0, best }));
498: }
499: 
500: void solve_result_free(SolveResult *r) {
501:     free(r->assignment);
502:     r->assignment = NULL;
503: }
504: 
505: /* ---- introspection ---------------------------------------------------- */
506: 
507: const bool *solver_assignment(const Solver *s) { return s->assignment; }
508: size_t solver_unsatisfied_count(const Solver *s) { return s->n_rogue; }
509: bool solver_clause_is_rogue(const Solver *s, size_t c) { return s->sat[c] == 0; }
510: size_t solver_clause_support(const Solver *s, size_t c) { return s->sat[c]; }
511: 
512: const VarStats *solver_var_stats(Solver *s) {
513:     if (s->stats_dirty) refresh_all(s);
514:     return s->stats;
515: }
516: 
517: void solver_set_assignment(Solver *s, const bool *a) {
518:     if (s->cnf->n_vars) memcpy(s->assignment, a, s->cnf->n_vars);
519:     rebuild_counts(s);
520: }

165: static void test_random_instances_and_strategies(void) {
166:     enum { N = 150, M = 570 };  /* ratio 3.8: comfortably satisfiable */
167:     static char text[M * 40 + 64];
168:     Rng g = rng_new(2024);
169:     int len = snprintf(text, sizeof text, "p cnf %d %d\n", N, M);
170:     for (int i = 0; i < M; i++) {
171:         int v[3];
172:         for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) {
173:             int x, dup;
174:             do { x = 1 + (int)rng_index(&g, N); dup = 0; for (int j = 0; j < k; j++) dup |= (v[j] == x); } while (dup);
175:             v[k] = x;
176:         }
177:         for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) len += snprintf(text + len, sizeof text - (size_t)len, "%d ", rng_bool(&g) ? v[k] : -v[k]);
178:         len += snprintf(text + len, sizeof text - (size_t)len, "0\n");
179:     }
180:     Cnf c = must_parse(text);
181:     CHECK(cnf_is_3sat(&c));
182:     for (size_t k = 0; k < N_STRATEGIES; k++) {
183:         CHECK(pick_fn_by_name(STRATEGIES[k].name) == STRATEGIES[k].fn);
184:         Solver *s = must_solver(&c, 77);
185:         SolverConfig cfg = solver_config_default();
186:         cfg.pick = STRATEGIES[k].fn;   /* function stored in a variable */
187:         cfg.max_steps = 200000; cfg.restarts = 10;
188:         cfg.on_progress = count_progress; cfg.progress_ctx = &progress_calls; cfg.progress_every = 1000;
189:         ResultSolve r = solver_solve(s, &cfg);
190:         if (strcmp(STRATEGIES[k].name, "ranked") == 0) {
191:             CHECK(r.ok && r.val.status == SOLVE_SAT && verify(&c, r.val.assignment, r.val.n_vars));
192:         } else if (r.ok && r.val.status == SOLVE_SAT) {
193:             CHECK(verify(&c, r.val.assignment, r.val.n_vars));   /* if it claims SAT it must be right */
194:         }
195:         if (r.ok) solve_result_free(&r.val);
196:         solver_free(s);
197:     }
198:     CHECK(pick_fn_by_name("nope") == NULL);
199:     CHECK(progress_calls > 0);
200:     cnf_free(&c);
201: }

//! Variable-centric 3-SAT search with incremental clause counters.
//!
//! This is a stochastic local-search solver: it returns SAT when it finds a
//! satisfying assignment, and UNKNOWN when its configured search budget ends.
//! It deliberately never reports UNSAT (local search cannot prove it).

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::error::Error;
use std::fmt;
use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct Lit {
    pub var: usize,
    pub positive: bool,
}

impl Lit {
    #[inline]
    pub fn value(self, assignment: bool) -> bool {
        assignment == self.positive
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Cnf {
    pub n_vars: usize,
    pub clauses: Vec<Vec<Lit>>,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ParseError(pub String);
impl fmt::Display for ParseError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result { f.write_str(&self.0) }
}
impl Error for ParseError {}

impl Cnf {
    pub fn from_dimacs_str(input: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError> {
        let mut declared_vars = None;
        let mut declared_clauses = None;
        let mut tokens: Vec<i64> = Vec::new();
        for (line_no, line) in input.lines().enumerate() {
            let line = line.trim();
            if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with('c') { continue; }
            if line.starts_with('p') {
                let fields: Vec<_> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
                if fields.len() != 4 || fields[1] != "cnf" {
                    return Err(ParseError(format!("line {}: expected `p cnf VARS CLAUSES`", line_no + 1)));
                }
                declared_vars = Some(fields[2].parse::<usize>().map_err(|_| ParseError(format!("line {}: invalid variable count", line_no + 1)))?);
                declared_clauses = Some(fields[3].parse::<usize>().map_err(|_| ParseError(format!("line {}: invalid clause count", line_no + 1)))?);
                continue;
            }
            for field in line.split_whitespace() {
                let value = field.parse::<i64>().map_err(|_| ParseError(format!("line {}: invalid DIMACS token `{field}`", line_no + 1)))?;
                tokens.push(value);
            }
        }
        let n_vars = declared_vars.ok_or_else(|| ParseError("missing `p cnf` header".into()))?;
        let expected_clauses = declared_clauses.unwrap();
        let mut clauses = Vec::new();
        let mut current = Vec::new();
        for value in tokens {
            if value == 0 {
                // Remove duplicate literals. Tautologies can never constrain a model.
                let mut seen = HashSet::new();
                let mut normalized = Vec::new();
                let mut tautology = false;
                for lit in current.drain(..) {
                    let key = (lit.var, lit.positive);
                    if seen.contains(&(lit.var, !lit.positive)) { tautology = true; break; }
                    if seen.insert(key) { normalized.push(lit); }
                }
                if !tautology { clauses.push(normalized); }
            } else {
                let abs = value.checked_abs().ok_or_else(|| ParseError("literal integer overflow".into()))? as usize;
                if abs == 0 || abs > n_vars {
                    return Err(ParseError(format!("literal {value} is outside 1..={n_vars}")));
                }
                current.push(Lit { var: abs - 1, positive: value > 0 });
            }
        }
        if !current.is_empty() { return Err(ParseError("unterminated clause: missing 0".into())); }
        // Tautologies are omitted, so compare declared count before normalization only
        // when no tautologies were present. DIMACS generators sometimes include them.
        if clauses.len() > expected_clauses {
            return Err(ParseError(format!("header declares {expected_clauses} clauses, parsed {}", clauses.len())));
        }
        Ok(Self { n_vars, clauses })
    }

    pub fn from_dimacs_file(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self, Box<dyn Error>> {
        Ok(Self::from_dimacs_str(&fs::read_to_string(path)?)?)
    }

    pub fn is_3sat(&self) -> bool { self.clauses.iter().all(|c| c.len() <= 3) }
}

/// Variable classification. Rogue is deliberately NOT a variable state:
/// only clauses can be rogue.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum VarState {
    Unused,
    Prime,
    Neutral { min_support: usize },
}

/// Satisfaction state belongs to a clause, never to a variable.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ClauseState {
    Rogue,
    Solved,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct ClauseStats {
    /// Number of currently true literals in this clause.
    pub satisfying_literals: usize,

}

# c_3sat

C port of `knowledge/3sat` (the Rust `context-3sat` experiment): an incremental
stochastic local-search 3-SAT engine for `little.AI` context handling.

Dependency-free C11 (GNU extensions: GCC/Clang). It returns **SAT** (verified
against the input) or **UNKNOWN** when the budget runs out. Local search cannot
prove UNSAT, so the only UNSAT it reports is structural: a unit clause `(x)` and
its negation `(-x)` are detected up front and returned as **UNSAT** with the list
of contradictory clause pairs. A pair of longer negated clauses is *not*
contradictory (`(1 2 3)` and `(-1 -2 -3)` are both true at `x1=1, x2=0, x3=0`).

## Build / test

```sh
make -C knowledge/c_3sat build   # -> build/3sat
make -C knowledge/c_3sat test    # ASan + UBSan test run
make -C knowledge/c_3sat bench N=20000 RATIO=3.5 SEED=1
```

## Run

```sh
knowledge/c_3sat/build/3sat input.cnf
knowledge/c_3sat/build/3sat input.cnf --steps 250000 --restarts 40 --noise 0.20 --seed 42
knowledge/c_3sat/build/3sat input.cnf --strategy greedy --progress 100000 --out out.json
```

Default output: `./knowledge/c_3sat/results/latest.json` (relative to cwd), same

```json
**Functions as variables.**

- `PickFn` chooses the variable to flip from the scored candidates. It is stored
  in `SolverConfig.pick`; built-ins are `ranked` (default, the original
  heuristic), `greedy`, `random`, selected by `--strategy` through the
  `STRATEGIES` name table.
- `ProgressFn` is an optional observer called every N flips (`--progress N`).
- CLI flags are a table of `{flag, handler}` function pointers (`OPTS` in `main.c`).

Adding a heuristic = write a `PickFn`, add one row to `STRATEGIES`.

**Speed / energy.**

- Flat CSR arrays for clauses and variable occurrences (no per-clause allocations).
- Variable states (prime/neutral, break/make counts) are derived *lazily*, only for
  the 2-3 variables of the clause actually examined, in one pass. A flip only
  updates clause counters and the rogue-clause index. On random 3-SAT this is
  ~10x faster than re-ranking every variable in every touched clause, with
  identical search decisions (same seed -> same steps).

from other domains, for example, encodings of problems available from
CSPLIB.


At the moment, we provide mainly satisfiable instances, as 
many popular SAT algorithms are incomplete. However, we will
extend our collection of unsatisfiable benchmark instances
in the near future, to further facilitate comparative studies
of complete algorithms.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u
BIN=/home/evg/i_C_u/little.AI/knowledge/c_3sat/build/3sat

      *) err=$((err+1));;

}

{
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# One-off batch run of the C solver over downloaded SATLIB/DIMACS CNFs.\n# No Python: only the C binary, exit codes, and shell counting.\nset -u\nBIN=/home/evg/i_C_u/little.AI/knowledge/c_3sat/build/3sat\nBASE=/tmp/opencode/cnf/ex\nTMP=/tmp/opencode/cnf/last.json\nLOG=/tmp/opencode/cnf/runs.log\n: > \"$LOG\"\n\nrun_family() {\n    local name=$1 expect=$2 limit=$3; shift 3\n    local sat=0 unk=0 unsat=0 err=0 n=0 f code\n    for f in \"$@\"; do\n        [ -n \"$f\" ] || continue\n        if [ \"$limit\" -gt 0 ] && [ \"$n\" -ge \"$limit\" ]; then break; fi\n        n=$((n + 1))\n        \"$BIN\" \"$f\" --out \"$TMP\" >/dev/null 2>&1\n        code=$?\n        case $code in\n            0) sat=$((sat + 1)) ;;\n            3) unk=$((unk + 1)) ;;\n            4) unsat=$((unsat + 1)) ;;\n            *) err=$((err + 1)) ;;\n        esac\n        printf '%d %s\\n' \"$code\" \"$f\" >> \"$LOG\"\n        [ \"$limit\" -gt 0 ] && [ \"$limit\" -le 5 ] && printf '  exit=%d  %s\\n' \"$code\" \"$(basename \"$f\")\"\n    done\n    printf '%-27s n=%-3d SAT=%-3d UNKNOWN=%-3d UNSAT=%-3d ERR=%-3d  expect=%s\\n' \\\n        \"$name\" \"$n\" \"$sat\" \"$unk\" \"$unsat\" \"$err\" \"$expect\"\n}\n\nfiles() { find \"$1\" -name '*.cnf' | sort; }\n\nrun_family \"uf20-91\"   SAT   20 $(files \"$BASE/uf20-91\")\nrun_family \"uf50-218\"  SAT   20 $(files \"$BASE/uf50-218\")\nrun_family \"uuf50-218\" UNSAT 20 $(files \"$BASE/uuf50-218\")\nrun_family \"uf100-430\" SAT   20 $(files \"$BASE/uf100-430\")\nrun_family \"uuf100-430\" UNSAT 20 $(files \"$BASE/uuf100-430\")\nrun_family \"DUBOIS\"    UNSAT  0 $(files \"$BASE/dubois\")\nrun_family \"PHOLE\"     UNSAT  0 $(files \"$BASE/pigeon-hole\")\nrun_family \"AIM-no\"    UNSAT 20 $(find \"$BASE/aim\" -name '*-no-*.cnf' | sort)\nrun_family \"AIM-yes\"   SAT   20 $(find \"$BASE/aim\" -name '*-yes*.cnf' | sort)\necho \"per-file exit codes: $LOG\"\n",

}

- **No false SAT**: the C solver calls `verify()` against the parsed formula before it reports SAT.

1. SATLIB files end with the DIMACS `%` marker; the parser rejected it. Fixed in `src/sat.c` (+ test). Without this, every downloaded file failed to load. **76 checks, 0 failures**.
2. `dubois100.cnf` in the SATLIB tarball is malformed: header says 800 clauses, but only 598 `0` terminators exist, so pairs of 3-clauses merge into 6-literal clauses. Not a solver bug, but the parser only rejects *more* clauses than declared, never fewer (tautologies can legitimately reduce the count).

- `BF` — circuit fault analysis, all UNSAT. 4/4 UNKNOWN.
- `SSA` — circuit fault analysis, mixed: 4 SAT, 4 UNSAT. Solver found 1 SAT and returned UNKNOWN for the other 7 — so it missed 3 satisfiable instances; the 4 UNSAT ones are expected UNKNOWN.
- `JNH` — random, mixed: 16 SAT, 34 UNSAT. Solver found exactly the 16 SAT and left all 34 UNSAT as UNKNOWN — the cleanest row.

**Totals**

- 220 runs = 100 truly SAT + 120 truly UNSAT.
- 85/100 satisfiable instances found and verified.
- 0/120 unsatisfiable instances proven — all UNKNOWN, as designed.
- 0 wrong answers: no SAT on an UNSAT instance, no false UNSAT.

The table therefore measures two separate things: **soundness** (never claim the wrong answer — 0 violations) and **coverage** (how much SAT it finds within the default budget — 85%). UNKNOWN is the honest "I didn't finish", not a failure claim.

SATLIB - Benchmark Problems





Instances from circuit fault analysis

The following description is based on the description given by Allen van
Gelder and Yumi
Tsuji. The original description can be found here.

The instances given here are selected formulas from those generated by
Nemesis. Nemesis is a test-pattern generation program described in
[LF91,Lar92].

These formulas are in CNF, and contain clauses of lengths 1-6.
Usually, more than half the clauses are Krom-clauses (2-clauses), so
the number of clauses is not as formidable as it first appears.

The given instances include only a subset of the formulas generated by
Nemesis because there are a large number of them, which could cause
disk space problems.  Also, the large majority are objectively very
easy, and would not provide significant tests of algorithms.

Nemesis applys random (but repeatable) simulation process to the
circuits to identify some detectable faults, then
generates cnf formulas only for those that were not found to be
detectable by this simulation.

Further deterministic polynomial time tests on the formulas generated
by Nemesis were done to eliminate those that can be easily processed.
This screening eliminates both satisfiable and unsatisfiable formulas.
For example, a formula that is unsatisfiable based on the Krom clauses
alone is screened out.

Each selected formula is "squeezed" (Nemesis generates formula that
has many gaps in the variable id's; so we rename the variables to make
them consecutive without gaps while maintaining the relative order).
The program "cnfsqueeze" is available here.


Formulas are in DIMACS Challenge cnf format.  A separate directory,
Cnfparse, has a parser and example programs using the parser.

Benchmark instances

There are four benchmark instances which test for bridge faults
and eight instances which test for single-at-stuck faults. The
instances are of rather large size (most of them have more than 1000
variables). Yet, it should be noted that the instances contain unit
clauses and, hence, can still be simplified by unit propagation.  The
instances are described in Table 1.

Instances hardness

Most of these instances are, despite their size, quite easily
solved. For example, all the satisfiable instances are solved with at
most backtrack by SATZ (version41). Also, WalkSAT, a stochastic local
search algorithm, quite easily solves these instances (for example,
using the option -noise 70 100 these instance are solved, on average,
in approx.\ 20.000 to 60.000 variable flips, with
ssa7552-038.cnf being the hardest.

Of the unsatisfiable instances only instances ssa2670-130.cnf
and ssa2670-141.cnf may be considered as hard, at least when
compared to the other unsatisfiable instances. For example, on the
first instance SATZ (version41) takes 17632 Backtracks, on the second
one 131352 Backtracks. Yet, with polynomial preprocessing techniques
(using the binary failed literal option in Jimmy Crawford's compact)
this latter instance becomes very easy for SATZ. The other instances
are all solved within at most 216 backtracks, instance
ssa6288-047.cnf, the largest of these instances, even in the
preprocessing steps of SATZ.

```bash
run_family() {
    local name=$1 expect=$2 limit=$3; shift 3
    local sat=0 unk=0 unsat=0 err=0 n=0 f code
    for f in "$@"; do
        [ -n "$f" ] || continue
        if [ "$limit" -gt 0 ] && [ "$n" -ge "$limit" ]; then break; fi
        n=$((n + 1))
        "$BIN" "$f" --out "$TMP" >/dev/null 2>&1
        code=$?
        case $code in
            0) sat=$((sat + 1)) ;;
            3) unk=$((unk + 1)) ;;
            4) unsat=$((unsat + 1)) ;;
            *) err=$((err + 1)) ;;
        esac
        ...
    done
    printf ... "$sat" "$unk" ...
}
```

Code:

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "sat.h"

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc < 2) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: inspect CNF [steps [restarts [seed]]]\n"); return 2; }
    ResultCnf rc = cnf_from_dimacs_file(argv[1]);
    if (!rc.ok) { fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", rc.err.msg); return 1; }
    Cnf cnf = rc.val;
    SolverConfig cfg = solver_config_default();
    if (argc > 2) cfg.max_steps = strtoull(argv[2], NULL, 10);
    if (argc > 3) cfg.restarts = strtoull(argv[3], NULL, 10);
    if (argc > 4) { cfg.seed = strtoull(argv[4], NULL, 10); }
    ResultSolver rs = solver_new(&cnf, cfg.seed);
    if (!rs.ok) { fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", rs.err.msg); cnf_free(&cnf); return 1; }
    Solver *s = rs.val;
    ResultSolve r = solver_solve(s, &cfg);
    if (!r.ok) { fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", r.err.msg); solver_free(s); cnf_free(&cnf); return 1; }
    const VarStats *st = solver_var_stats(s);
    size_t vu=0, vp=0, vn=0;
    for (size_t v=0; v<cnf.n_vars; v++) {
        switch (st[v].state) { case VAR_UNUSED: vu++; break; case VAR_PRIME: vp++; break; case VAR_NEUTRAL: vn++; break; }
    }
    size_t rogue=0, cn=0, cp=0, cu=0;
    for (size_t ci=0; ci<cnf.n_clauses; ci++) {
        if (!solver_clause_is_rogue(s, ci)) continue;
        rogue++;
        const Lit *c = cnf_clause(&cnf, ci);
        size_t n = cnf_clause_len(&cnf, ci);
        for (size_t k=0;k<n;k++) {
            switch (st[c[k].var].state) {
                case VAR_NEUTRAL: cn++; break;
                case VAR_PRIME: cp++; break;
                default: cu++; break;
            }
        }
    }
    printf("%s\t%s\t%zu\t%zu\t%zu\t%zu\t%zu\t%zu\t%zu\t%zu\t%zu\n",
        argv[1], r.val.status==SOLVE_SAT?"SAT":r.val.status==SOLVE_UNSAT?"UNSAT":"UNKNOWN",
        r.val.steps, r.val.best_unsatisfied, vu, vp, vn, rogue, cn, cp, cu);
    solve_result_free(&r.val);
    solver_free(s); cnf_free(&cnf);
    return 0;
}
```

## What that means

`VAR_NEUTRAL` = the variable is not the sole support of any satisfied clause. `VAR_PRIME` = it is the only true literal in at least one satisfied clause.

- There **are** neutrals — 8 to 63 of them in the failed AIM instances — so the formula is not "all variables critical".
- There are **zero neutrals inside the remaining unsat clause**. Every candidate there is prime.
- Flipping a prime candidate fixes the unsat clause but breaks the clause it uniquely supports, so `n_rogue` stays 1 — a one-flip plateau. It needs a **double flip** to make progress.
- A neutral candidate would be the only single flip that strictly lowers `n_rogue` (`breaks = 0`), and it never appears there.

So the failures are not caused by lack of neutrals globally; they are caused by the **local neighborhood of the near-solution containing none**. That is why raising the budget to 51M steps changed nothing.

Two supporting observations:
- The failures are exactly the low-density series `1_6` (ratio 1.6) and `2_0` (ratio 2.0). The `3_4` and `6_0` series never fail.
- At the SAT states, every variable is prime (neutral = 0) for all 27 solved AIM files, i.e. at a solution this generator's clauses each have exactly one true literal. So "zero neutral" is normal at a solution and not itself the failure signal.

## But the last rogue clause is always all-prime

Conditioned on states where exactly **one** clause is unsatisfied:

| instance | % of sampled states at n_rogue=1 | of those, all-prime |
|---|---:|---:|
| aim-50-1_6-yes1-1 | 96.5% | 100% |
| aim-100-1_6-yes1-1 | 96.2% | 100% |
| aim-200-2_0-yes1-1 | 57.8% | 100% |
| aim-50-3_4-yes1-1 (SAT) | 21.4% | 100% |
| ssa0432-003 | 42.3% | 100% |
| ssa7552-038/158, ssa6288-047 | 0% | not sampled |

Two different failure shapes, not one:

1. **AIM / ssa0432: stuck at 1.** They spend most of the budget at `n_rogue = 1`, and that lone clause is 100% prime-literal. Every flip of it just moves the violation somewhere else. This is the plateau I described.
2. **SSA 038/158/6288: not stuck at 1.** The `n_rogue = 1` state is too brief to sample at all — they fail at much higher counts (6288 bottoms out at 157). Neutrals are abundant there, yet it still fails, so availability of neutrals is not sufficient; the *choice* of which rogue clause to attack matters.

## What that implies for exploiting neutrals

The picker already ranks neutral candidates first (`cand_cmp`), and a neutral flip in the rogue clause provably reduces `n_rogue` by 1 without breaking anything. The waste is **upstream**: the rogue clause itself is chosen uniformly at random. With 20 rogue clauses, ~⅔ of which contain a neutral on SSA-038, most steps are spent plateau-walking in an all-prime clause while an improving clause sits unvisited.

Cheapest useful change, in order:
1. When `n_rogue` is small, scan all rogue clauses for one that has a neutral candidate and pick it, instead of a random clause. This is `O(n_rogue × 3)` per step and directly converts the SSA neutral supply into progress.
2. For AIM nothing in the neutral story helps — there are no neutral candidates at `best=1`. That needs a 2-flip escape (flip two prime vars in the clause and the clause they mutually support), or clause weighting.

Say the word and I'll implement (1) behind the existing config, with a test that the scan only fires when a neutral is actually present, and re-run the benchmark to see if SSA improves.

105: So rarest-first leaves 2-6x fewer broken clauses but is **worse** at scale. Why: it
106: satisfies each clause with the first literal it can and never adds redundancy, so almost
107: every satisfied clause hangs on a single variable. On the 20000-var / ratio 3.5 instance
108: 77% of variables are prime after rarest-first (62% after majority), only 23% are neutral
109: (38%), and 63% of the broken clauses contain no neutral variable at all, i.e. no free flip
110: (26% after majority). Fewer problems, but most of the remaining ones cannot be fixed
111: without breaking something. Group mode's merge, which only fires neutrals, is hit the same
112: way: its leftover barely changed (e.g. 105.7 -> 95.0 unmerged at ratio 4.2).
113: `majority` stays the default.

115: ## Group mode (`--mode groups`)
116: 
117: Sequential rogue groups with a neutral-driven merge, layered on the same solver
118: (`src/groups.c`). Ranking is unchanged: a variable is **neutral** iff flipping it
119: breaks no solved clause (`break_count == 0`), **prime** iff it is the sole
120: support of at least one (`break_count >= 1`). Neutrality belongs to the *current*
121: assignment, so it changes as flips happen. This invariant is pinned by a test.

Implementation:

```c
typedef struct { size_t key, var; } Rare;

static bool rare_before(Rare a, Rare b) {
    if (a.key != b.key) return a.key < b.key;
    return a.var < b.var;
}

static void rare_push(Rare *h, size_t *n, Rare x) {
    size_t i = (*n)++;
    while (i > 0) {
        size_t p = (i - 1) / 2;
        if (!rare_before(x, h[p])) break;
        h[i] = h[p];
        i = p;
    }
    h[i] = x;
}

static Rare rare_pop(Rare *h, size_t *n) {
    Rare top = h[0], last = h[--(*n)];
    size_t i = 0;
    for (;;) {
        size_t l = 2 * i + 1, r = l + 1, m = i;
        Rare best = last;
        if (l < *n && rare_before(h[l], best)) { m = l; best = h[l]; }
        if (r < *n && rare_before(h[r], best)) { m = r; best = h[r]; }
        if (m == i) break;
        h[i] = h[m];
        i = m;
    }
    if (*n) h[i] = last;
    return top;
}
```

```

Cleaner canonical:
```c
static void rare_sift_down(Rare *h, size_t n, size_t i, Rare x) {
    for (;;) {
        size_t l = 2*i+1;
        if (l >= n) break;
        size_t c = l;
        if (l+1 < n && rare_before(h[l+1], h[l])) c = l+1;
        if (!rare_before(h[c], x)) break;
        h[i] = h[c];
        i = c;
    }
    h[i] = x;
}
static Rare rare_pop(Rare *h, size_t *n) {
    Rare top = h[0];
    Rare last = h[--(*n)];
    if (*n) rare_sift_down(h, *n, 0, last);
    return top;
}
```

```c
typedef struct { size_t key, var; } Rare;

static bool rare_before(Rare a, Rare b) {
    if (a.key != b.key) return a.key < b.key;
    return a.var < b.var;
}

static void rare_push(Rare *h, size_t *n, Rare x) {
    size_t i = (*n)++;
    while (i > 0) {
        size_t p = (i - 1) / 2;
        if (!rare_before(x, h[p])) break;
        h[i] = h[p];
        i = p;
    }
    h[i] = x;
}

static void rare_sift_down(Rare *h, size_t n, size_t i, Rare x) {
    for (;;) {
        size_t l = 2 * i + 1;
        if (l >= n) break;
        size_t c = l;
        if (l + 1 < n && rare_before(h[l + 1], h[l])) c = l + 1;
        if (!rare_before(h[c], x)) break;
        h[i] = h[c];
        i = c;
    }
    h[i] = x;
}

static Rare rare_pop(Rare *h, size_t *n) {
    Rare top = h[0];
    Rare last = h[--(*n)];
    if (*n) rare_sift_down(h, *n, 0, last);
    return top;
}
```

And key helper:
```c
static size_t rare_key(const uint32_t *pos, const uint32_t *neg, size_t v) {
    return pos[v] > neg[v] ? pos[v] : neg[v];
}
```

Full function:

```c
bool solver_init_rarest(Solver *s) {
    const Cnf *cnf = s->cnf;
    size_t nv = cnf->n_vars, nc = cnf->n_clauses;
    size_t occ_total = s->occ_off[nv];
    uint32_t *unset = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *unset);
    unsigned char *done = calloc(nc ? nc : 1, 1);
    uint32_t *pos = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *pos);
    uint32_t *neg = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *neg);
    unsigned char *assigned = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1);
    Rare *heap = malloc((nv + occ_total + 1) * sizeof *heap);
    if (!unset || !done || !pos || !neg || !assigned || !heap) {
        free(unset); free(done); free(pos); free(neg); free(assigned); free(heap);
        return false;
    }
    for (size_t c = 0; c < nc; c++) unset[c] = (uint32_t)cnf_clause_len(cnf, c);
    size_t hn = 0;
    for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) {
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++)
            if (s->occ[k].positive) pos[v]++; else neg[v]++;
        rare_push(heap, &hn, (Rare){ rare_key(pos, neg, v), v });
    }

    for (size_t step = 0; step < nv; step++) {
        Rare top;
        do {
            top = rare_pop(heap, &hn);
        } while (assigned[top.var] || top.key != rare_key(pos, neg, top.var));
        size_t v = top.var;
        size_t fp = 0, fn = 0, op = 0, on = 0, tp = 0, tn = 0;
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++) {
            Occ o = s->occ[k];
            if (o.positive) tp++; else tn++;
            if (done[o.clause]) continue;
            if (unset[o.clause] == 1) { if (o.positive) fp++; else fn++; }
            else                      { if (o.positive) op++; else on++; }
        }
        bool val;
        if (fp != fn) val = fp > fn;
        else if (op != on) val = op > on;
        else if (tp != tn) val = tp > tn;
        else val = false;
        s->assignment[v] = val;
        assigned[v] = 1;
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++) {
            Occ o = s->occ[k];
            unset[o.clause]--;
            if (done[o.clause] || o.positive != val) continue;
            done[o.clause] = 1;
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(cnf, o.clause);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(cnf, o.clause);
            for (size_t j = 0; j < len; j++) {
                size_t u = cl[j].var;
                if (assigned[u]) continue;
                if (cl[j].positive) pos[u]--; else neg[u]--;
                rare_push(heap, &hn, (Rare){ rare_key(pos, neg, u), u });
            }
        }
    }
    free(unset); free(done); free(pos); free(neg); free(assigned); free(heap);
    rebuild_counts(s);
    return true;
}
```

Hmm: `rare_pop` on empty heap → UB. Could heap become empty before assigning all vars? Each unassigned var has at least one entry unless all its entries were popped as stale. A stale entry is popped when its key != current key. Current key changes only via decrement, and we push a fresh entry immediately after each decrement. If an entry is popped as stale, the fresh one exists (pushed after). Could the fresh one be popped as stale later? Only if key decreases again → another push. So invariant: for each unassigned var, the number of valid entries ≥1 minus... Let's reason: every decrement pushes an entry with the *current* key. Popping removes an entry; if it's stale, current key < entry key, meaning a newer entry exists (from the decrement). If it's valid, we use it and assign the var. So heap never empties while unassigned vars remain.

Implemented. `solver_init_rarest` no longer sorts once by total occurrences.

**New rule** (`src/sat.c`):
- Key for a variable = `max(#clauses containing x, #clauses containing !x)`, counting **only clauses not yet satisfied**.
- Take the smallest key next ("rarest"), ties by variable id.
- After each assignment, every clause that just became satisfied drops its occurrences from all still-unassigned variables, and those variables are re-keyed. So the order is recomputed per step, not fixed up front.
- Lazy min-heap (`key, var`) instead of `qsort`: counts only decrease, stale entries are skipped on pop. Pushes are bounded by `n_vars + total literal occurrences`, so it stays `O((n+m) log n)` — no per-step rescan of all variables.
- The value-choice logic (forced → open → total polarity → false) is untouched; it already used the satisfied/unset clause state.

Docs: `src/sat.h` comment and the README "Initial assignment" section now describe the max-of-polarities, recomputed-overlap rule. The old benchmark table is annotated as measured under the previous total-occurrence order — those numbers are stale, not re-run.

**Tests**: `112999 checks, 0 failures` under ASan/UBSan. The hand-checked test had to change: order is now `x2, x3, x1` instead of `x1, x2, x3`, and the result is `[true, false, true]` — the old expectation `[true, false, false]` is what total-order produced, so that test now pins the new rule.

**Effect on the failed SATs** (the reason for the change): with `--init rarest`, 4 of the 21 AIM instances that never solved with majority init now solve within the default budget:

} R;\nstatic uint64_t nx(R *r) { uint64_t x = r->s; x ^= x << 13; x ^= x >> 7; x ^= x << 17; return r->s = x; }\nstatic size_t idx(R *r, size_t n) { return (size_t)(nx(r) % n); }\n\ntypedef struct { size_t nv, nc, *off; int *lits; } Gen;\n\nstatic void gen_free(Gen *g) { free(g->off); free(g->lits); }\n\n/* random 3-SAT, distinct vars per clause */\nstatic Gen gen3(size_t nv, size_t nc, uint64_t seed) {\n    Gen g = { nv, nc, malloc((nc + 1) * sizeof *g.off), malloc(nc * 3 * sizeof *g.lits) };\n    R r = { seed ? seed : 1 };\n    g.off[0] = 0;\n    for (size_t c = 0; c < nc; c++) {\n        size_t a = idx(&r, nv), b = idx(&r, nv - 1), d = idx(&r, nv - 2);\n        if (b >= a) b++;\n        if (d >= a) d++;\n        if (d >= b) d++;\n        int s[3];\n        for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) s[k] = (nx(&r) & 1) ? 1 : -1;\n        g.lits[3*c+0] = s[0] * (int)(a + 1);\n        g.lits[3*c+1] = s[1] * (int)(b + 1);\n        g.lits[3*c+2] = s[2] * (int)(d + 1);\n        g.off[c+1] = g.off[c] + 3;\n    }\n    return g;\n}\n\nstatic char *to_dimacs(const Gen *g) {\n    size_t cap = g->nc * 32 + 64;\n    char *s = malloc(cap), *p = s;\n    p += sprintf(p, \"p cnf %zu %zu\\n\", g->nv, g->nc);\n    for (size_t c = 0; c < nc; c++)\n        for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(cnf, c); k++) cnt[cnf_clause(cnf, c)[k].var]++;\n    for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) order[v] = v;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < nv; i++)\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < nv; j++)\n            if (cnt[order[j]] < cnt[order[i]]) { size_t t = order[i]; order[i] = order[j]; order[j] = t; }\n    uint32_t *unset = malloc(nc * sizeof *unset);\n    unsigned char *done = calloc(nc, 1);\n    for (size_t c = 0; c < nc; c++) unset[c] = (uint32_t)cnf_clause_len(cnf, c);\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < nv; i++) {\n        size_t v = order[i], fp = 0, fn = 0, op = 0, on = 0, tp = 0, tn = 0;\n        for (size_t c = 0; c < nc; c++)\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(cnf, c); k++) {\n                const Lit l = cnf_clause(cnf, c)[k];\n                if (l.var != v) continue;\n                unset[c]--;\n                if (!done[c] && l.positive == val) done[c] = 1;\n            }\n    }\n    free(cnt); free(order); free(unset); free(done);\n}\n\ntypedef struct { const char *name; size_t init_unsat, solved, sum_steps, max_steps_run; double sec; } Row;\n\nint main(int argc, char **argv) {\n    if (argc < 6) { fprintf(stderr, \"usage: bench_rarest N RATIO SEEDS STEPS RESTARTS\\n\"); return 2; }\n    size_t nv = strtoull(argv[1], 0, 10);\n    double ratio = atof(argv[2]);\n    size_t seeds = strtoull(argv[3], 0, 10);\n    SolverConfig cfg = solver_config_default();\n    cfg.max_steps = strtoull(argv[4], 0, 10);\n    cfg.restarts = strtoull(argv[5], 0, 10);\n    size_t nc = (size_t)(nv * ratio + 0.5);\n\n    Row rows[3] = { { \"majority\", 0 }, { \"rarest-old\", 0 }, { \"rarest-new\", 0 } };\n    for (size_t sd = 1; return 1; }\n        Cnf cnf = rc.val;\n\n        for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {\n            ResultSolver rs = solver_new(&cnf, 5);\n            if (!rs.ok) { fprintf(stderr, \"solver: %s\\n\", rs.err.msg); return 1; }\n            Solver *s = rs.val;\n            if (i == 0) solver_init_majority(s);\n            else if (i == 1) {\n                bool *a = calloc(nv, sizeof *a);\n                old_rarest(&cnf, a);\n                solver_set_assignment(s, a);\n                free(a);\n            } else if (!solver_init_rarest(s)) { fprintf(stderr, \"init: oom\\n\"); return 1; }\n\n            rows[i].init_unsat += solver_unsatisfied_count(s);\n            if (cfg.max_steps) {\n                bool *start = malloc(nv * sizeof *start);\n                memcpy(start, solver_assignment(s), nv * sizeof *start);\n                SolverConfig c = cfg;\n                c.initial = start;\n                clock_t t0 = clock();\n                ResultSolve r = solver_solve(s, &c);\n                rows[i].sec += (double)(clock() - t0) / CLOCKS_PER_SEC;\n                if (!r.ok) { fprintf(stderr, \"solve: %s\\n\", r.err.msg); return 1; }\n                if (r.val.status == SOLVE_SAT) {\n                    rows[i].solved++;\n                    rows[i].sum_steps += r.val.steps;\n                    if (r.val.steps > rows[i].max_steps_run) rows[i].max_steps_run = r.val.steps;\n                    if (!verify(&cnf, r.val.assignment, r.val.n_vars)) { fprintf(stderr, \"BAD ASSIGNMENT\\n\"); ## Random 3-SAT

10 seeds per row (3 for the 5000-var row), 20 restarts.

| instance | broken after init (majority / old / new) | solved | mean flips (majority / old / new) |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 1000 vars, r=2.0 | 76 / 15 / 27 | 10/10 each | 85 / 32 / 42 |
| 1000 vars, r=3.5 | 187 / 77 / 98 | 10/10 each | 11.1k / 16.1k / 12.0k |

| 5000 vars, r=3.9 (10M budget) | 1098 / 482 / 631 | 2/3 each | 3.06M / 0.76M / 1.84M |
| 1000 vars, r=4.2 (2M) | 248 / 119 / 142 | 0/10 each | — |
| 20000 vars, r=3.8 (2M, then 10M on 3 seeds) | 4277 / 1858 / 2388 | 0/10, 0/3 each | — |

**Init quality.** The new key (`max(#x, #!x)`, only unsatisfied clauses) leaves **~40% more broken clauses than the old total-occurrence order** and **~45% fewer than majority**. That is expected: it prefers balanced-polarity variables, so the first assignments satisfy fewer clauses at once. Still, 2–3x fewer broken clauses than majority.

**Search.** Mixed:
- 1000/r2.0: new is slower than old (42 vs 32 flips) but 2x faster than majority.
- 1000/r3.5: new **beats old** (12.0k vs 16.1k) and is close to majority (11.1k).
- 20000/r3.5: new 162k vs old 169k vs majority 123k.
- 5000/r3.9: new **worse than old** (1.84M vs 0.76M), both beat majority (3.06M).
- 20000/r3.8 and 1000/r4.2: all inits fail identically at the tested budgets.

## AIM yes-set (48 instances, default budget 100k × 21)

| init | mean broken after init | solved |
|---|---:|---:|
| majority | 44.1 | 27/48 |
| rarest old | 18.2 | 31/48 |
| rarest new | 21.2 | 31/48 |

Old and new rarest fail the **exact same 17 files**; they just solve the same 4 extras that majority misses. So on the hard AIM series the new rule buys nothing over the old one — the earlier 4/21 result was a property of rarest in general, not of the new key.

## Verdict

The new ordering is not a clear win: it improves 1000-var/3.5 and ties/slightly improves 20000-var/3.5, but loses badly at 5000-var/3.9, and on AIM it is identical to the old rule. Its real effect is *which* near-solutions the search reaches, not overall coverage. `majority` is still the better default at scale.

The user asks to explain "tested budget" — likely referring to the benchmark output line: `budget=0 steps x 1 attempts` or in my tables "(2M)", "(10M)". Let me explain the budget concept precisely for this solver.

The solver's budget: for each restart, up to max_steps flips; total attempts = restarts+1. So total flips bound = max_steps × (restarts+1). "Tested budget" = that product, e.g. 100k × 21 = 2.1M flips.

Note: `steps` reported in SolveResult is the total across restarts, and means "flips", not "tested budget".

Explain: budget is a cap, not a target; UNKNOWN doesn't mean UNSAT; the "solved" counts are "found within the tested budget". Also my benchmark rows: 200k×10 = 2M; 1M×10 = 10M.

Where does "tested budget" appear? In my message: "5000 vars, r=3.9 (10M budget)" and the output prints `budget=200000 steps x 10 attempts`. Maybe the user refers to the harness output line. Let me explain that line, and the semantics.

Keep concise.

"Tested budget" is how far the search was allowed to run before the harness stopped it and recorded `UNKNOWN`. It is a cap, not a target.

The solver gets two knobs (`SolverConfig`):

| knob | meaning |
|---|---|
| `max_steps` | flips allowed in **one** restart |
| `restarts` | number of restarts after the first, so attempts = `restarts + 1` |

Total work cap = `max_steps × (restarts + 1)`. That product is what I called the tested budget.

In the harness output it is printed as:

```
budget=200000 steps x 10 attempts
```

= 200 000 flips per attempt × 10 attempts = **2 000 000 flips maximum** per init per instance. The table rows used:

| table row | command | tested budget |
|---|---|---:|
| 1000/r2.0, 1000/r3.5, 20000/r3.5 | `200000 9` | 2 M |
| 5000/r3.9 | `1000000 9` | 10 M |
| 20000/r3.8 first pass | `200000 9` | 2 M |
| 20000/r3.8 second pass | `1000000 9`, 3 seeds | 10 M |
| AIM (all 48, and the CLI runs) | default `100000 20` | 2.1 M |

Important details:

- **`steps` in the output is not the budget.** `SolveResult.steps` counts flips actually performed, summed over restarts. A solved run can report far fewer than the cap (e.g. `85` at 1000/r2.0 with a 2 M budget); an unsolved run reports close to the cap (e.g. `2 100 000` for 100k×21).
- **`UNKNOWN` means "budget exhausted", not "unsatisfiable".** A bigger budget can turn UNKNOWN into SAT, as `ssa7552-038` showed (default seed UNKNOWN, seed 3 SAT in 95 633 flips).
- **Budgets are per init, per instance.** Each of the three inits gets its own fresh cap, so `solved`/`mean_steps` are comparable across them.
- **`steps=0`** disables search entirely — the harness then only reports broken clauses right after init. That is the init-quality mode.
- Restarts matter because the cap is split: 10 attempts of 200k is not the same run as 1 attempt of 2M. A restart throws the assignment away and starts fresh (restart 0 from the init under test, later ones random), so more attempts = more independent tries, less depth per try.

When I wrote "(2M)" or "(10M)" in the benchmark tables, that's exactly this product — the maximum flips each init was allowed before being scored as a failure.

/* ---- Likho: majority first, then a one-pass repair ---------------- */

static bool likho_twin_flip(Solver *s, size_t a, const bool *flipped) {
    /* partner must lie in every sole-support clause of a; the first one bounds the search */
    for (size_t i = s->occ_off[a]; i < s->occ_off[a+1]; i++) {
        Occ o = s->occ[i];
        if (s->sat[o.clause] != 1 || s->assignment[a] != o.positive) continue;
        /* found a sole-support clause: candidates are its currently-false literals */
        const Lit *c = cnf_clause(s->cnf, o.clause);
        size_t n = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, o.clause);
        for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) {
            size_t b = c[k].var;
            if (b == a || flipped[b]) continue;
            refresh_var(s, b);
            if (s->stats[b].state != VAR_PRIME) continue;
            size_t before = s->n_rogue;
            solver_flip(s, a);
            solver_flip(s, b);
            bool ok = s->n_rogue < before;
            solver_flip(s, b);
            solver_flip(s, a);
            if (ok) { solver_flip(s, a); solver_flip(s, b); return true; }
        }
        return false;   /* first sole-support clause bounds the partners */
    }
    return false;
}

/* context-3sat (C port): incremental 3-SAT stochastic local search.
 *
 * Returns SAT when it finds a verified satisfying assignment and UNKNOWN when
 * the budget ends. Local search cannot prove UNSAT, but a contradictory unit
 * pair -- `(x)` and `(-x)` -- is checked up front and reported as UNSAT.
 */
#ifndef C3SAT_SAT_H
#define C3SAT_SAT_H

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include "result.h"

/* ---- CNF -------------------------------------------------------------- */

typedef struct {
    uint32_t var;   /* 0-based */
    bool positive;
} Lit;

/* Flat (CSR) layout: clause i is lits[off[i] .. off[i+1]). Owns its memory. */
typedef struct {
    size_t n_vars;
    size_t n_clauses;
    size_t *off;    /* n_clauses + 1 entries */
    Lit *lits;
} Cnf;

typedef RESULT(Cnf) ResultCnf;

ResultCnf cnf_from_dimacs_str(const char *input);
ResultCnf cnf_from_dimacs_file(const char *path);
void cnf_free(Cnf *cnf);
bool cnf_is_3sat(const Cnf *cnf);
static inline size_t cnf_clause_len(const Cnf *c, size_t i) { return c->off[i + 1] - c->off[i]; }
static inline const Lit *cnf_clause(const Cnf *c, size_t i) { return c->lits + c->off[i]; }
static inline bool lit_value(Lit l, bool assignment) { return assignment == l.positive; }

bool verify(const Cnf *cnf, const bool *assignment, size_t len);

/* ---- RNG (xorshift64) ------------------------------------------------- */

typedef struct { uint64_t state; } Rng;

static inline Rng rng_new(uint64_t seed) {
    return (Rng){ seed ? seed : 0xa0761d6478bd642fULL };
}
static inline uint64_t rng_next_u64(Rng *r) {
    uint64_t x = r->state;
    x ^= x << 13; x ^= x >> 7; x ^= x << 17;
    return r->state = x;
}
static inline bool rng_bool(Rng *r) { return rng_next_u64(r) & 1; }
static inline double rng_f64(Rng *r) { return (double)(rng_next_u64(r) >> 11) / 9007199254740992.0; }
static inline size_t rng_index(Rng *r, size_t upper) { return (size_t)rng_next_u64(r) % upper; }

/* ---- states ----------------------------------------------------------- */

/* Rogue is deliberately NOT a variable state: only clauses can be rogue. */
typedef enum { VAR_UNUSED, VAR_PRIME, VAR_NEUTRAL } VarState;

typedef struct {
    VarState state;
    size_t min_support;            /* meaningful for VAR_NEUTRAL */
    size_t satisfied_occurrences;  /* clauses where this var's literal is true */
    size_t rogue_occurrences;      /* incidence count only; never makes the var rogue */
    size_t break_count;
    size_t make_count;
    size_t rank;                   /* position among the last ranked candidates */
} VarStats;

/* One flip candidate from a rogue clause, already scored. */
typedef struct {
    size_t var;
    uint8_t cls;      /* 0 neutral, 1 prime, 2 unused */
    size_t support;
    size_t breaks;
    size_t makes;
} Candidate;

/* ---- function-as-variable hooks --------------------------------------- */

/* Choose which variable to flip from n >= 1 candidates sorted best-first. */
typedef size_t (*PickFn)(Rng *rng, const Candidate *cands, size_t n, double noise);
/* Optional observer, called every `progress_every` flips. */
typedef void (*ProgressFn)(void *ctx, size_t steps, size_t unsatisfied);

size_t pick_ranked(Rng *rng, const Candidate *c, size_t n, double noise); /* default */
size_t pick_greedy(Rng *rng, const Candidate *c, size_t n, double noise); /* noise-free */
size_t pick_random(Rng *rng, const Candidate *c, size_t n, double noise); /* uniform */

typedef struct { const char *name; PickFn fn; } Strategy;
extern const Strategy STRATEGIES[];
extern const size_t N_STRATEGIES;
PickFn pick_fn_by_name(const char *name); /* NULL if unknown */

/* Where restart 0 starts from (later restarts are random). */
typedef enum {
    INIT_MAJORITY,  /* every variable takes its majority polarity (default) */
    INIT_RAREST     /* constructive: rarest variables first, see solver_init_rarest() */
} InitMode;

typedef struct {
    size_t max_steps;
    size_t restarts;
    double noise;     /* probability of a random pick among top candidates */
    uint64_t seed;
    PickFn pick;      /* NULL => pick_ranked */
    const bool *initial;  /* optional start for restart 0 (n_vars entries); NULL => use `init` */
    InitMode init;
    ProgressFn on_progress;
    void *progress_ctx;
    size_t progress_every;
} SolverConfig;

SolverConfig solver_config_default(void);

/* ---- solver ----------------------------------------------------------- */

typedef struct Solver Solver;   /* borrows the Cnf: keep it alive */
typedef RESULT(Solver *) ResultSolver;

/* Two unit clauses with opposite signs: clause b == not clause a. */
typedef struct { size_t a, b; } Contradiction;

typedef enum { SOLVE_SAT, SOLVE_UNKNOWN, SOLVE_UNSAT } SolveStatus;
typedef struct {
    SolveStatus status;
    bool *assignment;        /* owned; SAT only (else NULL) */
    size_t n_vars;

static void add_rogue(Solver *s, size_t c) {
    if (s->rogue_pos[c] != SIZE_MAX) return;
    s->rogue_pos[c] = s->n_rogue;
    s->rogue[s->n_rogue++] = c;
}

static void remove_rogue(Solver *s, size_t c) {
    size_t pos = s->rogue_pos[c];
    if (pos == SIZE_MAX) return;
    size_t last = s->rogue[--s->n_rogue];
    if (pos < s->n_rogue) { s->rogue[pos] = last; s->rogue_pos[last] = pos; }
    s->rogue_pos[c] = SIZE_MAX;
}

static void rebuild_counts(Solver *s) {
    const Cnf *cnf = s->cnf;
    s->n_rogue = 0;
    for (size_t ci = 0; ci < cnf->n_clauses; ci++) {
        const Lit *c = cnf_clause(cnf, ci);
        size_t n = cnf_clause_len(cnf, ci), count = 0;
        for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) count += lit_value(c[k], s->assignment[c[k].var]);
        s->sat[ci] = (uint32_t)count;
        s->rogue_pos[ci] = SIZE_MAX;
    }
    for (size_t ci = 0; ci < cnf->n_clauses; ci++)
        if (s->sat[ci] == 0) add_rogue(s, ci);
    s->stats_dirty = true;
}

    if (cnf->n_clauses > UINT32_MAX) return ERRF(ResultSolver, ERR_PARSE, "too many clauses (%zu)", cnf->n_clauses);

    size_t nv = cnf->n_vars, nc = cnf->n_clauses;

    s->cnf = cnf;

    s->assignment = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *s->assignment);
    s->sat = calloc(nc ? nc : 1, sizeof *s->sat);
    s->occ_off = calloc(nv + 1, sizeof *s->occ_off);
    s->occ = malloc((total ? total : 1) * sizeof *s->occ);
    s->rogue = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *s->rogue);
    s->rogue_pos = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *s->rogue_pos);
    s->stats = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *s->stats);
    if (!s->assignment || !s->sat || !s->occ_off || !s->occ || !s->rogue || !s->rogue_pos || !s->stats) {
        solver_free(s);
        return ERRF(ResultSolver, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
    }
    for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++) {
        size_t n = cnf_clause_len(cnf, ci);
        if (n > s->max_len) s->max_len = n;
        for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) s->occ_off[cnf_clause(cnf, ci)[k].var + 1]++;
    }
    for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) s->occ_off[v + 1] += s->occ_off[v];
    size_t *fill = malloc((nv ? nv : 1) * sizeof *fill);
    s->cands = malloc((s->max_len ? s->max_len : 1) * sizeof *s->cands);
