/* Re-derive one variable's state, break and make counts from the current
 * assignment in a single pass over its occurrences.
 *
 * Ranking invariant (relied on by the group merge):
 *   VAR_PRIME   <=> break_count >= 1   (sole support of at least one solved clause)
 *   VAR_NEUTRAL <=> break_count == 0   (flipping can never un-solve a clause)
 * Neutrality is a property of the *current* assignment, not of the variable. */
static void refresh_var(Solver *s, size_t v) {
    size_t satisfied = 0, rogue_occ = 0, breaks = 0, min_support = SIZE_MAX;
    bool prime = false;
    bool val = s->assignment[v];
    for (size_t i = s->occ_off[v]; i < s->occ_off[v + 1]; i++) {
        Occ o = s->occ[i];
        uint32_t c = s->sat[o.clause];
        if (c == 0) { rogue_occ++; continue; }
        if (val == o.positive) {
            satisfied++;
            if (c < min_support) min_support = c;
            if (c == 1) { prime = true; breaks++; }
        }
    }
    VarStats *st = &s->stats[v];
    st->satisfied_occurrences = satisfied;
    st->rogue_occurrences = rogue_occ;
    st->break_count = breaks;
    st->make_count = rogue_occ;  /* a rogue clause has no true literal, so every incidence is a "make" */
    st->rank = SIZE_MAX;
    if (occ_count(s, v) == 0) { st->state = VAR_UNUSED; st->min_support = 0; }
    else if (prime) { st->state = VAR_PRIME; st->min_support = 1; }
    else { st->state = VAR_NEUTRAL; st->min_support = satisfied == 0 ? 0 : min_support; }
}

static void refresh_all(Solver *s) {
    for (size_t v = 0; v < s->cnf->n_vars; v++) refresh_var(s, v);
    s->stats_dirty = false;
}

static int cand_cmp(const Candidate *a, const Candidate *b) {
    if (a->cls != b->cls) return a->cls < b->cls ? -1 : 1;                 /* neutral before prime */
    if (a->support != b->support) return a->support > b->support ? -1 : 1; /* stronger support first */
    if (a->breaks != b->breaks) return a->breaks < b->breaks ? -1 : 1;     /* fewer breaks */
    if (a->makes != b->makes) return a->makes > b->makes ? -1 : 1;         /* more makes */
    return a->var < b->var ? -1 : (a->var > b->var);
}

/* Score the variables of one rogue clause and sort them best-first. */
static size_t rank_candidates(Solver *s, size_t clause) {
    const Lit *c = cnf_clause(s->cnf, clause);
    size_t n = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, clause);
    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) {
        size_t v = c[k].var;
        refresh_var(s, v);
        const VarStats *st = &s->stats[v];
        Candidate cd = { v, 0, 0, st->break_count, st->make_count };
        switch (st->state) {
            case VAR_NEUTRAL: cd.cls = 0; cd.support = st->min_support; break;
            case VAR_PRIME:   cd.cls = 1; cd.support = 1; break;
            case VAR_UNUSED:  cd.cls = 2; cd.support = SIZE_MAX; break;
        }
        size_t j = k;  /* insertion sort: clauses are tiny */
        while (j > 0 && cand_cmp(&cd, &s->cands[j - 1]) < 0) { s->cands[j] = s->cands[j - 1]; j--; }
        s->cands[j] = cd;
    }
    for (size_t r = 0; r < n; r++) s->stats[s->cands[r].var].rank = r;
    return n;
}

static void random_assignment(Solver *s, bool majority) {
    for (size_t v = 0; v < s->cnf->n_vars; v++) {
        size_t pos = 0, total = occ_count(s, v);
        for (size_t i = s->occ_off[v]; i < s->occ_off[v + 1]; i++) pos += s->occ[i].positive;
        size_t neg = total - pos;
        s->assignment[v] = (majority && pos != neg) ? pos > neg : rng_bool(&s->rng);
    }
    rebuild_counts(s);
}

typedef struct { size_t key, var; } Rare;

static bool rare_before(Rare a, Rare b) {
    if (a.key != b.key) return a.key < b.key;
    return a.var < b.var;
}

static void rare_push(Rare *h, size_t *n, Rare x) {
    size_t i = (*n)++;
    while (i > 0) {
        size_t p = (i - 1) / 2;
        if (!rare_before(x, h[p])) break;
        h[i] = h[p];
        i = p;
    }
    h[i] = x;
}

static void rare_sift_down(Rare *h, size_t n, size_t i, Rare x) {
    for (;;) {
        size_t l = 2 * i + 1;
        if (l >= n) break;
        size_t c = l;
        if (l + 1 < n && rare_before(h[l + 1], h[l])) c = l + 1;
        if (!rare_before(h[c], x)) break;
        h[i] = h[c];
        i = c;
    }
    h[i] = x;
}

static Rare rare_pop(Rare *h, size_t *n) {
    Rare top = h[0], last = h[--(*n)];
    if (*n) rare_sift_down(h, *n, 0, last);
    return top;
}

/* Rarest = fewest clauses holding x or !x, whichever is larger. Only clauses
 * that are still unsatisfied count, so satisfying a clause removes the
 * overlapping occurrences of every variable it contains. */
static size_t rare_key(const uint32_t *pos, const uint32_t *neg, size_t v) {
    return pos[v] > neg[v] ? pos[v] : neg[v];
}

bool solver_init_rarest(Solver *s) {
    const Cnf *cnf = s->cnf;
    size_t nv = cnf->n_vars, nc = cnf->n_clauses;
    uint32_t *unset = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *unset);   /* unassigned variables left in each clause */
    unsigned char *done = calloc(nc ? nc : 1, 1);              /* clause already has a true literal */
    uint32_t *pos = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *pos);          /* effective: satisfied clauses dropped */
    uint32_t *neg = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *neg);
    unsigned char *assigned = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1);
    Rare *heap = malloc((nv + s->occ_off[nv] + 1) * sizeof *heap);
    if (!unset || !done || !pos || !neg || !assigned || !heap) {
        free(unset); free(done); free(pos); free(neg); free(assigned); free(heap);
        return false;
    }
    for (size_t c = 0; c < nc; c++) unset[c] = (uint32_t)cnf_clause_len(cnf, c);
    size_t hn = 0;
    for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) {
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++)
            if (s->occ[k].positive) pos[v]++; else neg[v]++;
        rare_push(heap, &hn, (Rare){ rare_key(pos, neg, v), v });
    }

    for (size_t step = 0; step < nv; step++) {
        Rare top;
        do {
            top = rare_pop(heap, &hn);
        } while (assigned[top.var] || top.key != rare_key(pos, neg, top.var));
        size_t v = top.var;
        size_t fp = 0, fn = 0, op = 0, on = 0, tp = 0, tn = 0;
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++) {
            Occ o = s->occ[k];
            if (o.positive) tp++; else tn++;
            if (done[o.clause]) continue;
            if (unset[o.clause] == 1) { if (o.positive) fp++; else fn++; }
            else                      { if (o.positive) op++; else on++; }
        }
        bool val;
        if (fp != fn) val = fp > fn;
        else if (op != on) val = op > on;
        else if (tp != tn) val = tp > tn;
        else val = false;
        s->assignment[v] = val;
        assigned[v] = 1;
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++) {
            Occ o = s->occ[k];
            unset[o.clause]--;
            if (done[o.clause] || o.positive != val) continue;
            done[o.clause] = 1;
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(cnf, o.clause);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(cnf, o.clause);
            for (size_t j = 0; j < len; j++) {
                size_t u = cl[j].var;
                if (assigned[u]) continue;
                if (cl[j].positive) pos[u]--; else neg[u]--;
                rare_push(heap, &hn, (Rare){ rare_key(pos, neg, u), u });
            }
        }
    }
    free(unset); free(done); free(pos); free(neg); free(assigned); free(heap);
    rebuild_counts(s);
    return true;
}

static ResultSolve make_sat(const Solver *s, size_t steps, size_t restart) {
    size_t nv = s->cnf->n_vars;
    bool *a = malloc(nv ? nv : 1);
    if (!a) return ERRF(ResultSolve, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
    if (nv) memcpy(a, s->assignment, nv);
    return OK(ResultSolve, ((SolveResult){ SOLVE_SAT, a, nv, steps, restart, 0, NULL, 0 }));
}

/* Sound UNSAT pre-check: only a unit clause and its negation are contradictory.
 * For length >= 2, a clause and its pointwise negation are satisfiable, e.g.
 * (1 2 3) and (-1 -2 -3) are both true at x1=1, x2=0, x3=0. */
bool cnf_find_contradictions(const Cnf *cnf, Contradiction **out, size_t *out_n) {
    size_t nv = cnf->n_vars;
    size_t *pos = malloc((nv ? nv : 1) * sizeof *pos);
    size_t *neg = malloc((nv ? nv : 1) * sizeof *neg);
    *out = NULL;
    *out_n = 0;
    if (!pos || !neg) { free(pos); free(neg); return false; }
    for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) pos[v] = neg[v] = SIZE_MAX;
    size_t n = 0, cap = 0;
    Contradiction *list = NULL;
    for (size_t ci = 0; ci < cnf->n_clauses; ci++) {
        if (cnf_clause_len(cnf, ci) != 1) continue;
        Lit l = cnf_clause(cnf, ci)[0];
        size_t *same = l.positive ? &pos[l.var] : &neg[l.var];
        size_t *opp = l.positive ? &neg[l.var] : &pos[l.var];
        if (*opp != SIZE_MAX) {
            if (n == cap) {
                size_t ncap = cap ? cap * 2 : 8;
                Contradiction *p = realloc(list, ncap * sizeof *p);
                if (!p) { free(pos); free(neg); free(list); return false; }
                list = p; cap = ncap;
            }
            list[n++] = l.positive ? (Contradiction){ ci, *opp }
                                   : (Contradiction){ *opp, ci };
        }
        *same = ci;
    }
    free(pos); free(neg);
    *out = list;
    *out_n = n;
    return true;
}

ResultSolve solver_solve(Solver *s, const SolverConfig *cfg) {
    const Cnf *cnf = s->cnf;
    Contradiction *contradictions = NULL;
    size_t n_contradictions = 0;
    if (!cnf_find_contradictions(cnf, &contradictions, &n_contradictions))
        return ERRF(ResultSolve, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
    if (n_contradictions)
        return OK(ResultSolve, ((SolveResult){ SOLVE_UNSAT, NULL, cnf->n_vars, 0, 0, 0,
                                               contradictions, n_contradictions }));
    for (size_t i = 0; i < cnf->n_clauses; i++)
        if (cnf_clause_len(cnf, i) == 0)
            return OK(ResultSolve, ((SolveResult){ SOLVE_UNKNOWN, NULL, cnf->n_vars, 0, 0, cnf->n_clauses, NULL, 0 }));
    if (cnf->n_clauses == 0) {
        memset(s->assignment, 0, cnf->n_vars);
        return make_sat(s, 0, 0);
    }
    PickFn pick = cfg->pick ? cfg->pick : pick_ranked;
    size_t total = 0, best = SIZE_MAX;
    for (size_t restart = 0; restart <= cfg->restarts; restart++) {
        if (restart == 0 && cfg->initial) {
            if (cnf->n_vars) memcpy(s->assignment, cfg->initial, cnf->n_vars);
            rebuild_counts(s);
        } else if (restart == 0 && cfg->init == INIT_RAREST) {
            if (!solver_init_rarest(s)) return ERRF(ResultSolve, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
        } else {
            random_assignment(s, restart == 0);
        }
        for (size_t step = 0; step < cfg->max_steps; step++) {
            if (s->n_rogue == 0) return make_sat(s, total, restart);
            if (s->n_rogue < best) best = s->n_rogue;
            size_t clause = s->rogue[rng_index(&s->rng, s->n_rogue)];
            size_t n = rank_candidates(s, clause);
            if (n == 0) break;
            solver_flip(s, pick(&s->rng, s->cands, n, cfg->noise));
            total++;
            if (cfg->on_progress && cfg->progress_every && total % cfg->progress_every == 0)
                cfg->on_progress(cfg->progress_ctx, total, s->n_rogue);
        }
        if (s->n_rogue == 0) return make_sat(s, total, restart);  /* last flip solved it */
    }
    if (s->n_rogue < best) best = s->n_rogue;
    return OK(ResultSolve, ((SolveResult){ SOLVE_UNKNOWN, NULL, cnf->n_vars, total, 0, best, NULL, 0 }));
}

void solve_result_free(SolveResult *r) {
    free(r->assignment);
    free(r->contradictions);
    r->assignment = NULL;
    r->contradictions = NULL;
}

/* ---- introspection ---------------------------------------------------- */

const bool *solver_assignment(const Solver *s) { return s->assignment; }
size_t solver_unsatisfied_count(const Solver *s) { return s->n_rogue; }
bool solver_clause_is_rogue(const Solver *s, size_t c) { return s->sat[c] == 0; }
size_t solver_clause_support(const Solver *s, size_t c) { return s->sat[c]; }

const VarStats *solver_var_stats(Solver *s) {
    if (s->stats_dirty) refresh_all(s);
    return s->stats;
}

void solver_init_majority(Solver *s) { random_assignment(s, true); }
const size_t *solver_rogue_list(const Solver *s) { return s->rogue; }
VarStats solver_refresh_var(Solver *s, size_t v) { refresh_var(s, v); return s->stats[v]; }
size_t solver_occ_count(const Solver *s, size_t v) { return occ_count(s, v); }
size_t solver_occ_clause(const Solver *s, size_t v, size_t i) { return s->occ[s->occ_off[v] + i].clause; }

void solver_set_assignment(Solver *s, const bool *a) {
    if (s->cnf->n_vars) memcpy(s->assignment, a, s->cnf->n_vars);
    rebuild_counts(s);
}

static ResultUnit opt_merge(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    if (strcmp(value, "free") == 0) cli->gcfg.directed_only = false;
    else if (strcmp(value, "directed") == 0) cli->gcfg.directed_only = true;
    else return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Invalid value for %s: `%s` (expected free|directed)", flag, value);
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
}

static ResultUnit opt_init(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    if (strcmp(value, "majority") == 0) cli->cfg.init = INIT_MAJORITY;
    else if (strcmp(value, "rarest") == 0) cli->cfg.init = INIT_RAREST;
    else return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Invalid value for %s: `%s` (expected majority|rarest)", flag, value);
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
}
static ResultUnit opt_group_len(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    return parse_size(flag, value, &cli->gcfg.group_len);
}
static ResultUnit opt_diversify(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    return parse_size(flag, value, &cli->gcfg.diversify);
}

static void print_progress(void *ctx, size_t steps, size_t unsat) {
    (void)ctx;
    fprintf(stderr, "[%zu steps] %zu unsatisfied\n", steps, unsat);
}
static ResultUnit opt_progress(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    TRY0(ResultUnit, parse_size(flag, value, &cli->cfg.progress_every));
    cli->cfg.on_progress = cli->cfg.progress_every ? print_progress : NULL;
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
}

typedef struct { const char *flag; OptApply apply; } OptSpec;
static const OptSpec OPTS[] = {
    { "--steps", opt_steps },     { "--restarts", opt_restarts },
    { "--noise", opt_noise },     { "--seed", opt_seed },
    { "--out", opt_out },         { "--strategy", opt_strategy },
    { "--progress", opt_progress },
    { "--mode", opt_mode },       { "--max-groups", opt_max_groups },
    { "--merge", opt_merge },     { "--diversify", opt_diversify },
    { "--group-len", opt_group_len }, { "-group-len", opt_group_len },
    { "--init", opt_init },
};

static void usage(void) {
    fprintf(stderr,
        "Usage: 3sat INPUT.cnf [--steps N] [--restarts N] [--noise 0..1] [--seed N]\n"
        "                      [--strategy ranked|greedy|random] [--progress N] [--out FILE]\n"
        "                      [--mode plain|groups] [--max-groups 1..1024] [--merge free|directed]\n"
        "                      [--diversify N] [--group-len N]\n"
        "                      [--init majority|rarest]\n");
}

static ResultUnit parse_args(int argc, char **argv, Cli *cli) {
    if (argc < 2) return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Missing INPUT.cnf");
    cli->input = argv[1];
    for (int i = 2; i < argc; i += 2) {
        const OptSpec *spec = NULL;
        for (size_t k = 0; k < sizeof OPTS / sizeof OPTS[0]; k++)
            if (strcmp(OPTS[k].flag, argv[i]) == 0) { spec = &OPTS[k]; break; }
        if (!spec) return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Unknown option: %s", argv[i]);
        if (i + 1 >= argc) return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Missing value for %s", argv[i]);
        TRY0(ResultUnit, spec->apply(cli, argv[i], argv[i + 1]));
    }
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
}

/* ---- output ------------------------------------------------------------ */

static ResultUnit ensure_parent_dir(const char *path) {
    char *tmp = strdup(path);
    if (!tmp) return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
    char *slash = strrchr(tmp, '/');
    if (slash && slash != tmp) {
        *slash = '\0';
        for (char *p = tmp + 1; *p; p++) {
            if (*p != '/') continue;
            *p = '\0';
            if (mkdir(tmp, 0777) != 0 && errno != EEXIST) goto fail;
            *p = '/';
        }
        if (mkdir(tmp, 0777) != 0 && errno != EEXIST) goto fail;
    }
    free(tmp);
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
fail:;
    Error e = error_make(ERR_IO, "Cannot create output directory %s: %s", tmp, strerror(errno));

static bool likho_try_twin(Solver *s, size_t a, unsigned char *flipped) {
    if (stats[a].state != VAR_PRIME || flipped[a]) return false;
    // find first sole-support clause of a
    size_t sole = SIZE_MAX;
    bool aval = s->assignment[a];
    for occurrences o of a:
        if (o.positive == aval && s->sat[o.clause] == 1) { sole = o.clause; break; }
    if (sole == SIZE_MAX) return false;
    size_t before = s->n_rogue;
    // candidates: false literals in sole clause, excluding a
    for each literal l in sole clause:
        b = l.var; if b==a continue;
        if (s->assignment[b] == l.positive) continue; // currently true, not a candidate
        // refresh b
        refresh_var(s,b);
        if (stats[b].state != VAR_PRIME || flipped[b]) continue;
        // simulate
        solver_flip(s, a); solver_flip(s, b);
        bool ok = s->n_rogue < before;
        if (!ok) { solver_flip(s, b); solver_flip(s, a); }
        else return true; // both flipped
    }
    return false;
}

/* More than 64 groups (the old membership-mask limit) must work end to end. */
static void test_more_than_64_groups(void) {
    Cnf c = random_cnf(1000, 3000, 31337);
    SolverConfig cfg = solver_config_default();
    cfg.max_steps = 5000; cfg.restarts = 2;
    GroupConfig gc = group_config_default();
    gc.max_groups = 400;
    gc.group_len = 10;
    ResultGroup r = group_solve(&c, &cfg, &gc);
    CHECK(r.ok);
    if (r.ok) {
        CHECK(r.val.n_groups > 64 && r.val.n_groups <= 400);
        for (size_t k = 0; k < r.val.n_groups; k++) CHECK(r.val.group_sizes[k] <= 10);
        check_group_result(&c, &r.val);
        group_result_free(&r.val);
    }
    cnf_free(&c);
}

/* ---- rarest-first constructive start ------------------------------------ */

static size_t brute_unsat(const Cnf *c, const bool *a) {
    size_t n = 0;
    for (size_t ci = 0; ci < c->n_clauses; ci++) {
        bool any = false;
        for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(c, ci); k++) any |= lit_value(cnf_clause(c, ci)[k], a[cnf_clause(c, ci)[k].var]);
        n += !any;
    }
    return n;
}

static void test_init_rarest_hand_checked(void) {
    /* Rarest by max(#x,#!x): x2 and x3 have 1, x1 has 2, so x2 goes first.
     * x2 false satisfies (-2 -3), which drops x3's negative occurrence; x3 then
     * takes (1 3) as an open clause and goes true. x1 last: both clauses forced. */
    Cnf c = must_parse("p cnf 3 3\n1 2 0\n1 3 0\n-2 -3 0\n");
    Solver *s = must_solver(&c, 1);
    CHECK(solver_init_rarest(s));
    const bool *a = solver_assignment(s);
    CHECK(a[0] && !a[1] && a[2]);
    CHECK(solver_unsatisfied_count(s) == 0);
    solver_free(s); cnf_free(&c);

    /* x2 occurs once, x1 twice. x2 goes first: (-1 2) open -> true. x1: unit (1) is forced -> true. */
    Cnf d = must_parse("p cnf 2 2\n1 0\n-1 2 0\n");
    s = must_solver(&d, 1);
    CHECK(solver_init_rarest(s));
    a = solver_assignment(s);
    CHECK(a[0] && a[1] && solver_unsatisfied_count(s) == 0);
    solver_free(s); cnf_free(&d);

    /* variable that occurs nowhere is set false */
    Cnf e = must_parse("p cnf 3 1\n1 2 0\n");
    s = must_solver(&e, 1);
    CHECK(solver_init_rarest(s));
    CHECK(!solver_assignment(s)[2]);
    solver_free(s); cnf_free(&e);
}

static void test_init_rarest_properties(void) {
    SolverConfig cfg = solver_config_default();
    cfg.init = INIT_RAREST;
    cfg.max_steps = 20000; cfg.restarts = 2;
    for (int i = 0; i < 25; i++) {
        Cnf c = random_cnf(60 + 20 * (i % 4), (int)((60 + 20 * (i % 4)) * (2.0 + 0.4 * (i % 5))), 500 + (uint64_t)i);
        Solver *a = must_solver(&c, 1), *b = must_solver(&c, 99);   /* different RNG seeds: no randomness used */
        CHECK(solver_init_rarest(a) && solver_init_rarest(b));
        CHECK(memcmp(solver_assignment(a), solver_assignment(b), c.n_vars) == 0);   /* deterministic */
        CHECK(solver_unsatisfied_count(a) == brute_unsat(&c, solver_assignment(a))); /* counters consistent */
        solver_free(a); solver_free(b);

        Solver *s = must_solver(&c, 5);                       /* plain solver started from the rarest-first state */
        ResultSolve r = solver_solve(s, &cfg);
        CHECK(r.ok);
        if (r.ok && r.val.status == SOLVE_SAT) CHECK(verify(&c, r.val.assignment, r.val.n_vars));
        if (r.ok) solve_result_free(&r.val);
        solver_free(s);

        GroupConfig gc = group_config_default();               /* and the group solver */
        gc.max_groups = 64;
        ResultGroup g = group_solve(&c, &cfg, &gc);
        CHECK(g.ok);
        if (g.ok) { check_group_result(&c, &g.val); group_result_free(&g.val); }
        cnf_free(&c);
    }
}

    for (int i = 0; i < M; i++) {

        for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) {

            do { x = 1 + (int)rng_index(&g, N); dup = 0; for (int j = 0; j < k; j++) dup |= (v[j] == x); } while (dup);
            v[k] = x;
        }
        for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) len += snprintf(text + len, sizeof text - (size_t)len, "%d ", rng_bool(&g) ? v[k] : -v[k]);

/* ======================================================================== */

typedef struct { uint32_t clause; bool positive; } Occ;

struct Solver {
    const Cnf *cnf;
    bool *assignment;
    uint32_t *sat;          /* currently-true literal count per clause (0 == rogue) */
    size_t *occ_off;        /* CSR occurrence index, n_vars + 1 entries */
    Occ *occ;
    size_t *rogue;          /* clause ids currently rogue, for O(1) selection */
    size_t n_rogue;
    size_t *rogue_pos;      /* SIZE_MAX when not rogue */
    VarStats *stats;
    bool stats_dirty;       /* variable states are derived lazily */
    Candidate *cands;
    size_t max_len;
    Rng rng;
};

static size_t occ_count(const Solver *s, size_t v) { return s->occ_off[v + 1] - s->occ_off[v]; }

void solver_free(Solver *s) {
    if (!s) return;
    free(s->assignment); free(s->sat); free(s->occ_off); free(s->occ);
    free(s->rogue); free(s->rogue_pos); free(s->stats); free(s->cands);
    free(s);
}

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "groups.h"
#include "sat.h"

static int failures = 0, checks = 0;
#define CHECK(cond) do { checks++; if (!(cond)) { failures++; \
    fprintf(stderr, "FAIL %s:%d: %s\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); } } while (0)

static Cnf must_parse(const char *s) {
    ResultCnf r = cnf_from_dimacs_str(s);
    if (!r.ok) { fprintf(stderr, "unexpected parse error: %s\n", r.err.msg); exit(1); }
    return r.val;
}
static Solver *must_solver(const Cnf *c, uint64_t seed) {
    ResultSolver r = solver_new(c, seed);
    if (!r.ok) { fprintf(stderr, "solver_new: %s\n", r.err.msg); exit(1); }
    return r.val;
}

static void test_dimacs_multiline_and_comments(void) {
    Cnf c = must_parse("c demo\np cnf 3 2\n1 -2\n0\n3 0\n");
    CHECK(c.n_vars == 3 && c.n_clauses == 2);
    CHECK(cnf_clause_len(&c, 0) == 2 && cnf_clause_len(&c, 1) == 1);
    cnf_free(&c);
}

static void test_dimacs_percent_eof(void) {
    Cnf c = must_parse("p cnf 2 1\n1 2 0\n%\n0\n");
    CHECK(c.n_clauses == 1 && cnf_clause_len(&c, 0) == 2);
    cnf_free(&c);
}

static void test_normalization(void) {
    Cnf c = must_parse("p cnf 3 3\n1 1 2 0\n1 -1 2 0\n-3 0\n");
    CHECK(c.n_clauses == 2);                 /* tautology dropped */
    CHECK(cnf_clause_len(&c, 0) == 2);       /* duplicate literal removed */
    cnf_free(&c);
}

static void test_parse_errors(void) {
    ResultCnf r;
    r = cnf_from_dimacs_str("1 2 0\n");                 CHECK(!r.ok && r.err.kind == ERR_PARSE);
    r = cnf_from_dimacs_str("p cnf 2 1\n1 2\n");        CHECK(!r.ok && strstr(r.err.msg, "unterminated"));
    r = cnf_from_dimacs_str("p cnf 2 1\n3 0\n");        CHECK(!r.ok && strstr(r.err.msg, "outside"));
    r = cnf_from_dimacs_str("p cnf 2 1\n1 x 0\n");      CHECK(!r.ok && strstr(r.err.msg, "invalid DIMACS token"));
    r = cnf_from_dimacs_str("p cnf 2 1\n1 0\n2 0\n");   CHECK(!r.ok && strstr(r.err.msg, "declares"));
    r = cnf_from_dimacs_str("p dnf 2 1\n");             CHECK(!r.ok);
    r = cnf_from_dimacs_file("/definitely/not/here");   CHECK(!r.ok && r.err.kind == ERR_IO);
}

static void test_verify(void) {
    Cnf c = must_parse("p cnf 2 2\n1 2 0\n-1 2 0\n");
    bool good[] = { false, true }, bad[] = { true, false };
    CHECK(verify(&c, good, 2));
    CHECK(!verify(&c, bad, 2));
    CHECK(!verify(&c, good, 1));
    cnf_free(&c);
}
}
static void test_try_macros(void) {
    ResultInt r = outer();
    CHECK(!r.ok && r.err.kind == ERR_PARSE && strcmp(r.err.msg, "while testing: boom") == 0);
}

int main(void) {
    test_dimacs_multiline_and_comments();
    test_dimacs_percent_eof();
    test_normalization();
    test_parse_errors();
    test_verify();
    test_solves_simple();
    test_empty_clause_and_empty_formula();
    test_unsat_is_unknown_never_unsat();
    test_contradictory_units_are_unsat();
    test_contradiction_lives_in_extras();
    test_negated_3clauses_are_not_unsat();
    test_rogue_is_a_clause_state();
    test_neutral_can_occur_in_rogue_clause();
    test_prime_precedence();
    test_flip_updates_state();
    test_incremental_matches_rebuild();
    test_random_instances_and_strategies();
    test_try_macros();
    test_ranking_invariant_neutral_means_zero_breaks();
    test_groups_small_and_edge_cases();
    test_groups_contracts_on_random_instances();
    test_group_len_limits_group_size();
    test_more_than_64_groups();
    test_init_rarest_hand_checked();
    test_init_rarest_properties();
    printf("%d checks, %d failures\n", checks, failures);
    return failures ? 1 : 0;
}

/* ---- ranking invariant: neutral <=> zero breaks, prime <=> at least one --- */

static void test_ranking_invariant_neutral_means_zero_breaks(void) {
    Cnf c = random_cnf(80, 300, 99);
    Solver *s = must_solver(&c, 5);
    Rng rng = rng_new(4242);
    for (int round = 0; round < 40; round++) {
        for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++) solver_flip(s, rng_index(&rng, c.n_vars));
        const VarStats *st = solver_var_stats(s);
        for (size_t v = 0; v < c.n_vars; v++) {
            /* independent recount: clauses where v's literal is true and is the only true literal */
            size_t breaks = 0;
            for (size_t i = 0, n = solver_occ_count(s, v); i < n; i++) {
                size_t ci = solver_occ_clause(s, v, i);
                const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(&c, ci);
                for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(&c, ci); k++)
                    if (cl[k].var == v && lit_value(cl[k], solver_assignment(s)[v]) && solver_clause_support(s, ci) == 1) breaks++;
            }
            CHECK(st[v].break_count == breaks);
            CHECK((st[v].state == VAR_PRIME) == (breaks >= 1));
            if (st[v].state == VAR_NEUTRAL) CHECK(st[v].break_count == 0);
            CHECK(solver_refresh_var(s, v).state == st[v].state);   /* single-var refresh agrees */
        }
    }
    solver_free(s); cnf_free(&c);
}

/* ---- groups ------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* Everything a GroupResult reports must be recomputable from its assignment. */
static void check_group_result(const Cnf *c, const GroupResult *r) {
    size_t nv = c->n_vars, nc = c->n_clauses;
    unsigned char *is_rogue = calloc(nc ? nc : 1, 1), *in_rogue = calloc(nc ? nc : 1, 1);
    size_t unsat = 0;
    for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++) {
        bool any = false;
        for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(c, ci); k++) {
            Lit l = cnf_clause(c, ci)[k];
            any |= lit_value(l, r->assignment[l.var]);
        }
        if (!any) { is_rogue[ci] = 1; unsat++; }
    }
    CHECK(r->n_rogue == unsat);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < r->n_rogue; i++) { CHECK(r->rogue[i] < nc && is_rogue[r->rogue[i]]); in_rogue[r->rogue[i]] = 1; }
    for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++) CHECK(is_rogue[ci] == in_rogue[ci]);

```c
/* ---- Likho: majority start, then a one-flip-per-variable repair pass ---- */

/* A twin pair (a,b) is two primes whose joint flip strictly lowers the rogue
 * count. b must be a currently-false literal of a's first sole-support clause:
 * that clause is what a's flip breaks, so only a literal in it can restore it.
 * The pair is verified by actually flipping both and reverting on no progress. */
static bool likho_twin(Solver *s, size_t a, unsigned char *flipped, size_t *partner) {
    if (flipped[a]) return false;
    if (solver_refresh_var(s, a).state != VAR_PRIME) return false;
    bool aval = s->assignment[a];
    size_t sole = SIZE_MAX;
    for (size_t i = s->occ_off[a]; i < s->occ_off[a + 1]; i++) {
        Occ o = s->occ[i];
        if (o.positive == aval && s->sat[o.clause] == 1) { sole = o.clause; break; }
    }
    if (sole == SIZE_MAX) return false;
    const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, sole);
    size_t n = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, sole);
    size_t before = s->n_rogue;
    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) {
        size_t b = cl[k].var;
        if (b == a || flipped[b]) continue;
        if (lit_value(cl[k], s->assignment[b])) continue;  /* must be false now */
        if (solver_refresh_var(s, b).state != VAR_PRIME) continue;
        solver_flip(s, a);
        solver_flip(s, b);
        if (s->n_rogue < before) {
            s->stats[a].state = VAR_TWIN;
            s->stats[b].state = VAR_TWIN;
            *partner = b;
            return true;
        }
        solver_flip(s, b);
        solver_flip(s, a);
    }
    return false;
}

bool solver_likho(Solver *s) {
    solver_init_majority(s);
    size_t nv = s->cnf->n_vars;
    unsigned char *flipped = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1);
    size_t *snap = malloc((s->cnf->n_clauses ? s->cnf->n_clauses : 1) * sizeof *snap);
    if (!flipped || !snap) { free(flipped); free(snap); return false; }
    while (s->n_rogue > 0) {
        size_t nr = s->n_rogue;
        memcpy(snap, s->rogue, nr * sizeof *snap);
        bool moved = false;
        /* 2a: one neutral flip per rogue clause, all in one pass */
        for (size_t i = 0; i < nr && s->n_rogue > 0; i++) {
            size_t c = snap[i];
            if (!solver_clause_is_rogue(s, c)) continue;
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, c);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, c);
            for (size_t k = 0; k < len; k++) {
                size_t v = cl[k].var;
                if (flipped[v]) continue;
                if (solver_refresh_var(s, v).state == VAR_NEUTRAL) {
                    solver_flip(s, v);
                    flipped[v] = 1;
                    moved = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        if (moved) continue;
        /* 2b: twin double flips, one per pass (rogue set changes) */
        for (size_t i = 0; i < nr && s->n_rogue > 0; i++) {
            size_t c = snap[i];
            if (!solver_clause_is_rogue(s, c)) continue;
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, c);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, c);
            for (size_t k = 0; k < len; k++) {
                size_t v = cl[k].var;
                if (flipped[v]) continue;
                if (solver_refresh_var(s, v).state != VAR_PRIME) continue;
                size_t partner;
                if (likho_twin(s, v, flipped, &partner)) {
                    flipped[v] = 1;
                    flipped[partner] = 1;
                    moved = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (moved) break;
        }
        if (!moved) break;  /* no neutral, no twin: stuck */
    }
    free(flipped); free(snap);
    return true;
}
```

static bool parse_usize(const char *s, size_t len, size_t *out) {
    uint64_t mag; bool neg;
    if (!parse_u64(s, len, &mag, false, &neg) || mag > SIZE_MAX) return false;
    *out = (size_t)mag;
    return true;
}

/* ======================================================================== */
/* CNF                                                                      */
/* ======================================================================== */

void cnf_free(Cnf *cnf) {
    free(cnf->off);
    free(cnf->lits);
    cnf->off = NULL;
    cnf->lits = NULL;
    cnf->n_vars = cnf->n_clauses = 0;
}

bool cnf_is_3sat(const Cnf *cnf) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < cnf->n_clauses; i++)
        if (cnf_clause_len(cnf, i) > 3) return false;
    return true;
}

ResultCnf cnf_from_dimacs_str(const char *input) {
    Error err = {0};
    int64_t *tok = NULL; size_t ntok = 0, captok = 0;
    Lit *cur = NULL; size_t ncur = 0, capcur = 0;
    size_t capoff = 0, caplit = 0, nlit = 0;
    Cnf cnf = {0};
    size_t n_vars = 0, expected = 0;
    bool have_header = false;

#define FAIL(kind, ...) do { err = error_make((kind), __VA_ARGS__); goto fail; } while (0)

    /* Pass 1: header + raw integer tokens. */
    size_t line_no = 0;
    const char *p = input;
    while (*p) {
        line_no++;
        const char *eol = strchr(p, '\n');
        size_t llen = eol ? (size_t)(eol - p) : strlen(p);
        const char *line = p;
        p = eol ? eol + 1 : p + llen;
        while (llen && is_ws(*line)) { line++; llen--; }
        while (llen && is_ws(line[llen - 1])) llen--;
        if (llen == 0 || line[0] == 'c') continue;
        if (line[0] == '%') break;   /* DIMACS end-of-file marker; trailing tokens are ignored */

        if (line[0] == 'p') {
            struct { const char *s; size_t n; } f[5];
            size_t nf = 0, i = 0;
            while (i < llen) {
                while (i < llen && is_ws(line[i])) i++;
                if (i >= llen) break;
                size_t st = i;
                while (i < llen && !is_ws(line[i])) i++;
                if (nf < 5) { f[nf].s = line + st; f[nf].n = i - st; }
                nf++;
            }
            if (nf != 4 || f[1].n != 3 || memcmp(f[1].s, "cnf", 3) != 0)
                FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "line %zu: expected `p cnf VARS CLAUSES`", line_no);
            if (!parse_usize(f[2].s, f[2].n, &n_vars))
                FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "line %zu: invalid variable count", line_no);
            if (!parse_usize(f[3].s, f[3].n, &expected))
                FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "line %zu: invalid clause count", line_no);
            have_header = true;
            continue;
        }

        size_t i = 0;
        while (i < llen) {
            while (i < llen && is_ws(line[i])) i++;
            if (i >= llen) break;
            size_t st = i;
            while (i < llen && !is_ws(line[i])) i++;
            int64_t v;
            if (!parse_i64(line + st, i - st, &v))
                FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "line %zu: invalid DIMACS token `%.*s`", line_no, (int)(i - st), line + st);
            if (!vec_reserve((void **)&tok, &captok, sizeof *tok, ntok + 1)) FAIL(ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
            tok[ntok++] = v;
        }
    }
    if (!have_header) FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "missing `p cnf` header");
    if (n_vars > UINT32_MAX) FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "variable count %zu is too large", n_vars);

    /* Pass 2: build clauses; drop duplicate literals and tautologies. */
    cnf.n_vars = n_vars;
    if (!vec_reserve((void **)&cnf.off, &capoff, sizeof *cnf.off, 1)) FAIL(ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
    cnf.off[0] = 0;

    for (size_t t = 0; t < ntok; t++) {
        int64_t value = tok[t];
        if (value != 0) {
            if (value == INT64_MIN) FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "literal integer overflow");
            uint64_t abs = value < 0 ? (uint64_t)(-value) : (uint64_t)value;
            if (abs > n_vars) FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "literal %lld is outside 1..=%zu", (long long)value, n_vars);
            if (!vec_reserve((void **)&cur, &capcur, sizeof *cur, ncur + 1)) FAIL(ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
            cur[ncur++] = (Lit){ (uint32_t)(abs - 1), value > 0 };
            continue;
        }
        size_t start = cnf.off[cnf.n_clauses], appended = 0;
        bool taut = false;
        for (size_t c = 0; c < ncur && !taut; c++) {
            bool dup = false;
            for (size_t k = 0; k < appended; k++) {
                Lit e = cnf.lits[start + k];
                if (e.var != cur[c].var) continue;
                if (e.positive != cur[c].positive) taut = true; else dup = true;
                break;
            }
            if (taut || dup) continue;
            if (!vec_reserve((void **)&cnf.lits, &caplit, sizeof *cnf.lits, start + appended + 1)) FAIL(ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
            cnf.lits[start + appended++] = cur[c];
        }
        ncur = 0;
        if (taut) continue;
        if (!vec_reserve((void **)&cnf.off, &capoff, sizeof *cnf.off, cnf.n_clauses + 2)) FAIL(ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
        cnf.off[++cnf.n_clauses] = start + appended;
        nlit = start + appended;
    }
    (void)nlit;
    if (ncur != 0) FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "unterminated clause: missing 0");
    if (cnf.n_clauses > expected)
        FAIL(ERR_PARSE, "header declares %zu clauses, parsed %zu", expected, cnf.n_clauses);

    free(tok);
    free(cur);
    if (!cnf.lits) cnf.lits = malloc(sizeof *cnf.lits); /* keep non-NULL for empty formulas */
    return OK(ResultCnf, cnf);

/* ---- Likho: majority start + one-flip-per-variable repair pass ---------- */

/* a is a prime in a rogue clause. Its flip breaks every clause where it is the
 * sole true literal; take the first one and try its other (false) literals as
 * partners. A partner b is a twin iff b is an unflipped prime and flipping both
 * leaves every clause containing a or b satisfied. Flipping toggles the literal
 * in each such clause, so a clause that is rogue after the pair flip was
 * satisfied before it -- exactly the breakage we must avoid. */
static bool likho_twin(Solver *s, size_t a, const unsigned char *flipped, size_t *partner) {
    if (flipped[a] || solver_refresh_var(s, a).state != VAR_PRIME) return false;
    bool aval = s->assignment[a];
    size_t sole = SIZE_MAX;
    for (size_t i = s->occ_off[a]; i < s->occ_off[a + 1]; i++) {
        Occ o = s->occ[i];
        if (o.positive == aval && s->sat[o.clause] == 1) { sole = o.clause; break; }
    }
    if (sole == SIZE_MAX) return false;
    const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, sole);
    size_t n = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, sole);
    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) {
        size_t b = cl[k].var;
        if (b == a || flipped[b]) continue;
        if (solver_refresh_var(s, b).state != VAR_PRIME) continue;
        solver_flip(s, a);
        solver_flip(s, b);
        bool clean = true;
        for (size_t i = s->occ_off[a]; i < s->occ_off[a + 1] && clean; i++)
            if (s->sat[s->occ[i].clause] == 0) clean = false;
        for (size_t i = s->occ_off[b]; i < s->occ_off[b + 1] && clean; i++)
            if (s->sat[s->occ[i].clause] == 0) clean = false;
        if (clean) {
            s->stats[a].state = VAR_TWIN;   /* phase-2 classification, reset on next refresh */
            s->stats[b].state = VAR_TWIN;
            *partner = b;
            return true;
        }
        solver_flip(s, b);
        solver_flip(s, a);
    }
    return false;
}

bool solver_likho(Solver *s) {
    solver_init_majority(s);
    size_t nv = s->cnf->n_vars, nc = s->cnf->n_clauses;
    unsigned char *flipped = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1);
    size_t *snap = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *snap);
    if (!flipped || !snap) { free(flipped); free(snap); return false; }
    while (s->n_rogue > 0) {
        size_t nr = s->n_rogue;
        memcpy(snap, s->rogue, nr * sizeof *snap);
        bool moved = false;
        /* Phase 2a: one neutral flip per rogue clause. A neutral flip breaks
         * nothing, so it can only remove clauses from the rogue set. */
        for (size_t i = 0; i < nr && s->n_rogue > 0; i++) {
            size_t c = snap[i];
            if (!solver_clause_is_rogue(s, c)) continue;
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, c);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, c);
            for (size_t k = 0; k < len; k++) {
                size_t v = cl[k].var;
                if (flipped[v]) continue;
                if (solver_refresh_var(s, v).state != VAR_NEUTRAL) continue;
                solver_flip(s, v);
                flipped[v] = 1;
                moved = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (moved) continue;  /* a neutral flip may have liberated a prime */
        /* Phase 2b: no neutral is left anywhere, so try twin pairs. One pair per
         * pass, because the flip changes the rogue set and the states. */
        for (size_t i = 0; i < nr && s->n_rogue > 0 && !moved; i++) {
            size_t c = snap[i];
            if (!solver_clause_is_rogue(s, c)) continue;
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, c);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, c);
            for (size_t k = 0; k < len; k++) {
                size_t v = cl[k].var, partner;
                if (flipped[v]) continue;
                if (likho_twin(s, v, flipped, &partner)) {
                    flipped[v] = 1;
                    flipped[partner] = 1;
                    moved = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        if (!moved) break;  /* stuck: no neutral, no twin */
    }
    free(flipped); free(snap);
    return true;
}

static void test_init_rarest_properties(void) {
    SolverConfig cfg = solver_config_default();
    cfg.init = INIT_RAREST;
    cfg.max_steps = 20000; cfg.restarts = 2;
    for (int i = 0; i < 25; i++) {
        Cnf c = random_cnf(60 + 20 * (i % 4), (int)((60 + 20 * (i % 4)) * (2.0 + 0.4 * (i % 5))), 500 + (uint64_t)i);
        Solver *a = must_solver(&c, 1), *b = must_solver(&c, 99);   /* different RNG seeds: no randomness used */
        CHECK(solver_init_rarest(a) && solver_init_rarest(b));
        CHECK(memcmp(solver_assignment(a), solver_assignment(b), c.n_vars) == 0);   /* deterministic */
        CHECK(solver_unsatisfied_count(a) == brute_unsat(&c, solver_assignment(a))); /* counters consistent */
        solver_free(a); solver_free(b);

        Solver *s = must_solver(&c, 5);                       /* plain solver started from the rarest-first state */
        ResultSolve r = solver_solve(s, &cfg);

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Random 3-CNF generator: gen_cnf.py N_VARS RATIO [SEED] > out.cnf
Each clause has 3 distinct variables with random polarity. The hard region for
random 3-SAT is around RATIO ~= 4.26."""
import random, sys

n = int(sys.argv[1]); ratio = float(sys.argv[2])
rng = random.Random(int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 0)
m = round(n * ratio)
print(f"c random 3-CNF n={n} m={m}")
print(f"p cnf {n} {m}")
for _ in range(m):
    vs = rng.sample(range(1, n + 1), 3)
    print(" ".join(str(v if rng.random() < 0.5 else -v) for v in vs), 0)

Default output: `./knowledge/c_3sat/results/latest.json` (relative to cwd), same
JSON shape as the Rust version. Exit codes: `0` SAT, `1` input/output/internal
error, `2` usage error, `3` budget exhausted (UNKNOWN), `4` structural UNSAT.

UNSAT output lists the conflicting clause indices (0-based):

```json
{
  "status": "UNSAT",
  "message": "UNSAT",
  "variables": 3,
  "clauses": 5,
  "contradictions": [{"i": 1, "j": 3}]
}
```

Here clause `j` is the negation of clause `i`; both must be unit clauses.
Non-unit relatives -- e.g. `(1 2)` and `(-1 -2)` -- are consistent even when the
formula has more clauses than variables, so they are not reported.

## Design

**Rust-like errors** (`src/result.h`). Fallible functions return a tagged
`Result` instead of using errno or sentinel values:

```c
typedef RESULT(Cnf) ResultCnf;                 // { bool ok; union { Cnf val; Error err; } }
Cnf cnf = TRY_CTX(ResultInt, cnf_from_dimacs_file(path), "Failed to load CNF");  // like `?` + .context()
return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_PARSE, "line %zu: ...", n);                           // like Err(...)
```

`TRY`, `TRY_CTX` (adds context) and `TRY0` (for `Result<()>`) early-return the
error from the enclosing function. Named typedefs are required per result type
(two anonymous structs are different types in C).

**Functions as variables.**

- `PickFn` chooses the variable to flip from the scored candidates. It is stored
  in `SolverConfig.pick`; built-ins are `ranked` (default, the original
  heuristic), `greedy`, `random`, selected by `--strategy` through the
  `STRATEGIES` name table.
- `ProgressFn` is an optional observer called every N flips (`--progress N`).
- CLI flags are a table of `{flag, handler}` function pointers (`OPTS` in `main.c`).

Adding a heuristic = write a `PickFn`, add one row to `STRATEGIES`.

**Speed / energy.**

- Flat CSR arrays for clauses and variable occurrences (no per-clause allocations).
- Variable states (prime/neutral, break/make counts) are derived *lazily*, only for
  the 2-3 variables of the clause actually examined, in one pass. A flip only
  updates clause counters and the rogue-clause index. On random 3-SAT this is
  ~10x faster than re-ranking every variable in every touched clause, with
  identical search decisions (same seed -> same steps).

## Initial assignment (`--init`)

Restart 0 starts from `--init majority` (default: every variable takes its majority
polarity) or `--init rarest`, a deterministic constructive start (no RNG, works in both
`plain` and `groups` mode; later restarts stay random):

1. Repeatedly set the currently **rarest** unassigned variable: the fewest clauses
   holding `x` or `!x`, whichever count is larger, and only clauses that are not yet
   satisfied count (ties by id). The counts are recomputed after every assignment, so
   satisfying a clause removes that overlap from every variable still unset.
2. The variable takes the value that satisfies more **forced**
   clauses (open clauses where it is the last unset variable); else more **open**
   (not yet satisfied) clauses; else the larger total polarity; else `false`.

Measured on random 3-SAT, 10 seeds per row (3 seeds for the 5000-var row), 20
restarts. "old" is the previous total-occurrence order, kept for comparison:

| instance | broken after init (majority / old / new) | solved (majority / old / new) | mean flips (majority / old / new) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 vars, ratio 2.0 | 76 / 15 / 27 | 10/10, 10/10, 10/10 | 85 / 32 / 42 |
| 1000 vars, ratio 3.5 | 187 / 77 / 98 | 10/10, 10/10, 10/10 | 11.1k / 16.1k / 12.0k |
| 20000 vars, ratio 3.5 | 3802 / 1527 / 2024 | 9/10, 9/10, 9/10 | 123k / 169k / 162k |
| 5000 vars, ratio 3.9 | 1098 / 482 / 631 | 2/3, 2/3, 2/3 | 3.06M / 0.76M / 1.84M |
| AIM yes-set, 48 instances | 44 / 18 / 21 | 27 / 31 / 31 | — |

The max-of-polarities order leaves 2-3x fewer broken clauses than majority, but
~30% more than the total-occurrence order. It is faster on 1000-var/3.5 and
20000-var/3.5, slower on 5000-var/3.9; on the AIM yes-set both rarest orders solve
the same 31/48 (identical failure sets) versus 27/48 for majority. It changes which
near-solutions are reachable more than it changes total coverage.

Rarest-first is still **worse** than majority at scale. Why: it satisfies each clause
with the first literal it can and never adds redundancy, so almost
every satisfied clause hangs on a single variable. On the 20000-var / ratio 3.5 instance
77% of variables are prime after rarest-first (62% after majority), only 23% are neutral
(38%), and 63% of the broken clauses contain no neutral variable at all, i.e. no free flip
(26% after majority) -- measured with the old ordering. Fewer problems, but most of the
remaining ones cannot be fixed
without breaking something. Group mode's merge, which only fires neutrals, is hit the same
way: its leftover barely changed (e.g. 105.7 -> 95.0 unmerged at ratio 4.2).
`majority` stays the default.

Reproduce with `make bench-rarest ARGS="1000 3.5 10 200000 9"` (or
`ARGS="file.cnf 100000 20"`); `steps = 0` measures init quality only. The harness
also reimplements the old total-occurrence order as a baseline, so all three starts
run the same search code.

## Group mode (`--mode groups`)

Sequential rogue groups with a neutral-driven merge, layered on the same solver
(`src/groups.c`). Ranking is unchanged: a variable is **neutral** iff flipping it
breaks no solved clause (`break_count == 0`), **prime** iff it is the sole

Likho description:
```
### Likho (`--init likho`)

Starts from `majority`, then repairs rogue clauses without accepting any move that
breaks a satisfied clause. Each variable is flipped at most once in this pass.

- A variable is **neutral** when flipping it breaks no satisfied clause. A neutral
  variable inside a rogue clause is flipped immediately; this always lowers the rogue
  count.
- Flipping a **prime** (sole support of some satisfied clause) normally trades one
  broken clause for another. Two primes are **twins** when flipping both together
  breaks nothing: the partner is taken from the clause the first prime's flip would
  break, and the pair is accepted only if every clause containing either variable is
  still satisfied afterwards.
- After a neutral flip, a prime it was propping up can become neutral; the next pass
  picks it up. When no neutral is left anywhere, twin pairs are tried.

The repair is deterministic for a fixed seed (the majority phase breaks polarity ties
with the solver RNG).
```

```
## Initial assignment (`--init`)

Restart 0 starts from one of three starts; later restarts are always random:

- `--init majority` (default): every variable takes its majority polarity.
- `--init rarest`: deterministic constructive start (no RNG).
- `--init likho`: majority, then a neutral/twin repair pass.

### Rarest

1. ...
2. ...

### Likho

`--init likho` starts from `majority`, then repairs rogue clauses. It only accepts
moves that break no satisfied clause, and each variable is flipped at most once:

- A **neutral** variable inside a rogue clause is flipped immediately; it breaks
  nothing and satisfies at least that clause.
- A **prime** is the sole support of some satisfied clause, so flipping it alone
  breaks that clause. Two primes are **twins** when flipping both together breaks
  nothing. The partner is taken from the clause the first prime's flip would break,
  and the pair is accepted only if every clause containing either variable is still
  satisfied afterwards.
- A neutral flip can liberate a prime (the clause it was propping up gets another
  true literal); the next pass sees it as neutral and can flip it. Twin pairs are
  tried only when no neutral is left anywhere.

For a fixed seed the repair is deterministic (the majority phase breaks polarity
ties with the solver RNG).

### Measurements

Measured on random 3-SAT, 10 seeds per row (3 seeds for the 5000-var row), 20
restarts, default solver seed. "old" is the previous total-occurrence rarest order,
kept for comparison; the four starts share the same search code:

| instance | broken after init (maj / old / new / likho) | solved | mean flips |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 vars, ratio 2.0 | 78 / 15 / 28 / 5 | 10/10 each | 88 / 47 / 67 / 25 |
| 1000 vars, ratio 3.5 | 187 / 77 / 98 / 51 | 10/10 each | 11.1k / 16.1k / 12.0k / 10.2k |
| 20000 vars, ratio 3.5 | 3802 / 1527 / 2024 / 1036 | 9/10, 9/10, 9/10, 10/10 | 123k / 169k / 162k / 118k |
| 5000 vars, ratio 3.9 | 1098 / 482 / 631 / 360 | 2/3 each | 3.06M / 0.76M / 1.84M / 3.24M |
| AIM yes-set, 48 instances | 46 / 18 / 21 / 26 | 27 / 31 / 31 / 27 | — |

Likho leaves the fewest broken clauses in every row. On random 3-SAT it is fastest
at 1000/2.0, 1000/3.5 and 20000/3.5 (and the only start that solves all ten
20000-var instances at this budget), but it is slower than both rarest orders at
5000/3.9. On the AIM yes-set it ties majority at 27/48 and fails the same 21
instances; rarest reaches 31/48. So the repair improves the starting assignment
much more reliably than it changes which hard instances the search can reach.

[keep the rarest "worse at scale" paragraph? It's still relevant for rarest, but
Likho addresses it. Let me adjust:]

Rarest-first is still **worse** than majority at scale. Why: it satisfies each clause
with the first literal it can and never adds redundancy, so almost every satisfied
clause hangs on a single variable. On the 20000-var / ratio 3.5 instance 77% of
variables are prime after rarest-first (62% after majority), only 23% are neutral
(38%), and 63% of the broken clauses contain no neutral variable at all, i.e. no free
flip (26% after majority) -- measured with the old ordering. Fewer problems, but most
of the remaining ones cannot be fixed without breaking something. Likho attacks
exactly that: it uses twin primes when no neutral is available. Group mode's merge,
which only fires neutrals, is hit the same way: its leftover barely changed (e.g.
105.7 -> 95.0 unmerged at ratio 4.2).
`majority` stays the default.

Reproduce with `make bench-rarest ARGS="1000 3.5 10 200000 9"` ...
The harness also reimplements the old total-occurrence order as a baseline, so all
four starts run the same search code.
```

```
## Initial assignment (`--init`)

Restart 0 starts from `--init majority` (default: every variable takes its majority
polarity) or `--init rarest`, a deterministic constructive start (no RNG, works in both
`plain` and `groups` mode; later restarts stay random):

1. Repeatedly set the currently **rarest** unassigned variable: the fewest clauses
   holding `x` or `!x`, whichever count is larger, and only clauses that are not yet
   satisfied count (ties by id). The counts are recomputed after every assignment, so
   satisfying a clause removes that overlap from every variable still unset.
2. The variable takes the value that satisfies more **forced**
   clauses (open clauses where it is the last unset variable); else more **open**
   (not yet satisfied) clauses; else the larger total polarity; else `false`.

Measured on random 3-SAT, 10 seeds per row (3 seeds for the 5000-var row), 20
restarts. "old" is the previous total-occurrence order, kept for comparison:

| instance | broken after init (majority / old / new) | solved (majority / old / new) | mean flips (majority / old / new) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 vars, ratio 2.0 | 76 / 15 / 27 | 10/10, 10/10, 10/10 | 85 / 32 / 42 |
| 1000 vars, ratio 3.5 | 187 / 77 / 98 | 10/10, 10/10, 10/10 | 11.1k / 16.1k / 12.0k |
| 20000 vars, ratio 3.5 | 3802 / 1527 / 2024 | 9/10, 9/10, 9/10 | 123k / 169k / 162k |
| 5000 vars, ratio 3.9 | 1098 / 482 / 631 | 2/3, 2/3, 2/3 | 3.06M / 0.76M / 1.84M |
| AIM yes-set, 48 instances | 44 / 18 / 21 | 27 / 31 / 31 | — |

The max-of-polarities order leaves 2-3x fewer broken clauses than majority, but
~30% more than the total-occurrence order. It is faster on 1000-var/3.5 and
20000-var/3.5, slower on 5000-var/3.9; on the AIM yes-set both rarest orders solve
the same 31/48 (identical failure sets) versus 27/48 for majority. It changes which
near-solutions are reachable more than it changes total coverage.

Rarest-first is still **worse** than majority at scale. Why: it satisfies each clause
with the first literal it can and never adds redundancy, so almost
every satisfied clause hangs on a single variable. On the 20000-var / ratio 3.5 instance
77% of variables are prime after rarest-first (62% after majority), only 23% are neutral
(38%), and 63% of the broken clauses contain no neutral variable at all, i.e. no free flip
(26% after majority) -- measured with the old ordering. Fewer problems, but most of the
remaining ones cannot be fixed
without breaking something. Group mode's merge, which only fires neutrals, is hit the same
way: its leftover barely changed (e.g. 105.7 -> 95.0 unmerged at ratio 4.2).
`majority` stays the default.

Reproduce with `make bench-rarest ARGS="1000 3.5 10 200000 9"` (or
`ARGS="file.cnf 100000 20"`); `steps = 0` measures init quality only. The harness
also reimplements the old total-occurrence order as a baseline, so all three starts
run the same search code.
```

So the repair improves the starting\nassignment much more reliably than it changes which hard instances the search can\nreach.\n\nThe max-of-polarities rarest order leaves 2-3x fewer broken clauses than majority,\nbut ~30% more than the total-occurrence order. It is faster on 1000-var/3.5 and\n20000-var/3.5, slower on 5000-var/3.9; on the AIM yes-set both rarest orders solve\nthe same 31/48 (identical failure sets) versus 27/48 for majority. It changes which\nnear-solutions are reachable more than it changes total coverage.\n\nRarest-first is still **worse** than majority at scale. Why: it satisfies each clause\nwith the first literal it can and never adds redundancy, so almost\nevery satisfied clause hangs on a single variable. On the 20000-var / ratio 3.5 instance\n77% of variables are prime after rarest-first (62% after majority), only 23% are neutral\n(38%), and 63% of the broken clauses contain no neutral variable at all, i.e. no free flip\n(26% after majority) -- measured with the old ordering. Fewer problems, but most of the\nremaining ones cannot be fixed\nwithout breaking something. Likho attacks exactly that: when no neutral is left it\nuses twin primes instead of giving up. Group mode's merge, which only fires neutrals,\nis hit the same way: its leftover barely changed (e.g. 105.7 -> 95.0 unmerged at ratio\n4.2). `majority` stays the default.\n\nReproduce with `make bench-rarest ARGS=\"1000 3.5 10 200000 9\"` (or\n`ARGS=\"file.cnf 100000 20\"`); `steps = 0` measures init quality only. The harness\nalso reimplements the old total-occurrence order as a baseline, so all four starts\nrun the same search code."
}

**Formation.** Start from the majority-polarity assignment `B`.
1. `G1` = *all* clauses rogue under `B`. Solve `G1` on its own (a sub-formula that
   sees only its clauses, started from `B`) -> snapshot `X1`. The same variable may
   hold different polarities in different snapshots.
2. Apply `X1`, inspect the **whole** formula, collect *all* clauses that are rogue
   now into `G2`, solve independently -> `X2`. Earlier snapshots are kept.
3. Repeat until nothing is rogue (formation alone solved it), or the group cap,
   a repeated rogue set, or an unsolvable group stops it.

**Merge** (only if formation did not close the formula).
- Start from the snapshot with the most neutral variables (the first anchor).
- Each step picks the *source* group with the most fireable neutrals: zero breaks
  under the merged assignment, not fired yet, inside a still-rogue clause of that
  group, and the group's snapshot wants the opposite polarity (**directed** flip).

## Differences from the Rust version

- Structural UNSAT: a unit clause and its negation are detected before search and
  returned as UNSAT with the conflicting clause pairs. The Rust version reports
  UNKNOWN.
- The DIMACS `%` end-of-file marker (used by SATLIB files) is accepted; the Rust
  parser rejects it.
- If the very last allowed flip satisfies the formula, C reports SAT. The Rust
  loop only checks at the top of a step, so it could report UNKNOWN with 0
  unsatisfied clauses.
- `make_count` equals `rogue_occurrences` (a rogue clause has no true literal),
  so both come from the same pass.
- Extra options: `--strategy`, `--progress`, `--mode`, `--max-groups`, `--merge`, `--diversify`,
  `--group-len` (also accepted as `-group-len`), `--init`.

## Layout

```
src/result.h   Result/Error/TRY macros
src/sat.h      public API
src/sat.c      DIMACS parser, strategies, solver
src/groups.h   group formation + merge API (and the algorithm spec)

/* ---- Likho: majority start + one-flip-per-variable repair pass ---------- */

/* a is a prime in a rogue clause. Flipping it breaks every clause where it is
 * the sole true literal; take the first such clause and try its other (false)
 * literals as partners. b is a twin iff b is an unflipped prime and flipping
 * both leaves every clause containing a or b satisfied. A flip toggles its
 * literal in each such clause, so a clause that is rogue after the pair flip
 * was satisfied before it -- exactly the breakage that rules the pair out. */
static bool likho_twin(Solver *s, size_t a, const unsigned char *flipped, size_t *partner) {
    if (flipped[a] || solver_refresh_var(s, a).state != VAR_PRIME) return false;
    bool aval = s->assignment[a];
    size_t sole = SIZE_MAX;
    for (size_t i = s->occ_off[a]; i < s->occ_off[a + 1]; i++) {
        Occ o = s->occ[i];
        if (o.positive == aval && s->sat[o.clause] == 1) { sole = o.clause; break; }
    }
    if (sole == SIZE_MAX) return false;
    const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, sole);
    size_t n = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, sole);
    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) {
        size_t b = cl[k].var;
        if (b == a || flipped[b]) continue;
        if (solver_refresh_var(s, b).state != VAR_PRIME) continue;
        solver_flip(s, a);
        solver_flip(s, b);
        bool clean = true;
        for (size_t i = s->occ_off[a]; i < s->occ_off[a + 1] && clean; i++)
            if (s->sat[s->occ[i].clause] == 0) clean = false;
        for (size_t i = s->occ_off[b]; i < s->occ_off[b + 1] && clean; i++)
            if (s->sat[s->occ[i].clause] == 0) clean = false;
        if (clean) {
            s->stats[a].state = VAR_TWIN;   /* phase-2 label; the next refresh re-derives it */
            s->stats[b].state = VAR_TWIN;
            *partner = b;
            return true;
        }
        solver_flip(s, b);
        solver_flip(s, a);
    }
    return false;
}

bool solver_likho(Solver *s) {
    solver_init_majority(s);
    size_t nv = s->cnf->n_vars, nc = s->cnf->n_clauses;
    unsigned char *flipped = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1);
    size_t *snap = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *snap);
    if (!flipped || !snap) { free(flipped); free(snap); return false; }
    while (s->n_rogue > 0) {
        size_t nr = s->n_rogue;
        memcpy(snap, s->rogue, nr * sizeof *snap);
        bool moved = false;
        /* Neutrals first: a neutral flip breaks nothing, so it only removes
         * clauses from the rogue set. Re-scanning next round also catches the
         * primes this pass liberated (they are neutral now). */
        for (size_t i = 0; i < nr; i++) {
            size_t c = snap[i];
            if (!solver_clause_is_rogue(s, c)) continue;
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, c);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, c);
            for (size_t k = 0; k < len; k++) {
                size_t v = cl[k].var;
                if (flipped[v]) continue;
                if (solver_refresh_var(s, v).state != VAR_NEUTRAL) continue;
                solver_flip(s, v);
                flipped[v] = 1;
                moved = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (moved) continue;   /* prefer neutrals, including freshly liberated primes */
        /* Twins: only reached when no rogue clause has a neutral left. A clean
         * pair flip also adds no new rogue clause, so this pass can keep going. */
        for (size_t i = 0; i < nr; i++) {
            size_t c = snap[i];
            if (!solver_clause_is_rogue(s, c)) continue;
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, c);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, c);
            for (size_t k = 0; k < len; k++) {
                size_t v = cl[k].var, partner;
                if (flipped[v]) continue;
                if (!likho_twin(s, v, flipped, &partner)) continue;
                flipped[v] = 1;
                flipped[partner] = 1;
                moved = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (!moved) break;   /* stuck: no neutral and no twin anywhere */
    }
    free(flipped); free(snap);
    return true;
}

static ResultSolve make_sat(const Solver *s, size_t steps, size_t restart) {
    size_t nv = s->cnf->n_vars;
    bool *a = malloc(nv ? nv : 1);
    if (!a) return ERRF(ResultSolve, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
    if (nv) memcpy(a, s->assignment, nv);
    return OK(ResultSolve, ((SolveResult){ SOLVE_SAT, a, nv, steps, restart, 0, NULL, 0 }));
}

## Initial assignment (`--init`)

Restart 0 starts from one of three starts (later restarts are always random):

- `--init majority` (default): every variable takes its majority polarity.
- `--init rarest`: deterministic constructive start (no RNG).
- `--init likho`: majority, then a neutral/twin repair pass.

All three work in both `plain` and `groups` mode.

### Rarest

1. Repeatedly set the currently **rarest** unassigned variable: the fewest clauses
   holding `x` or `!x`, whichever count is larger, and only clauses that are not yet
   satisfied count (ties by id). The counts are recomputed after every assignment, so
   satisfying a clause removes that overlap from every variable still unset.
2. The variable takes the value that satisfies more **forced**
   clauses (open clauses where it is the last unset variable); else more **open**
   (not yet satisfied) clauses; else the larger total polarity; else `false`.

### Likho

`--init likho` starts from `majority`, then repairs rogue clauses. It only accepts
moves that break no satisfied clause, and each variable is flipped at most once:

- A **neutral** variable inside a rogue clause is flipped immediately; it breaks
  nothing and satisfies at least that clause.
- A **prime** is the sole support of some satisfied clause, so flipping it alone
  breaks that clause. Two primes are **twins** when flipping both together breaks
  nothing. The partner is taken from the clause the first prime's flip would break,
  and the pair is accepted only if every clause containing either variable is still
  satisfied afterwards.
- A neutral flip can liberate a prime (the clause it was propping up gets another
  true literal); the next pass sees it as neutral and can flip it. Twin pairs are
  tried only when no neutral is left anywhere.

For a fixed seed the repair is deterministic (the majority phase breaks polarity
ties with the solver RNG).

### Measurements

Measured on random 3-SAT, 10 seeds per row (3 seeds for the 5000-var row), 20
restarts, default solver seed. "old" is the previous total-occurrence rarest order,
kept for comparison; all four starts share the same search code:

| instance | broken after init (maj / old / new / likho) | solved | mean flips over solved (maj / old / new / likho) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 vars, ratio 2.0 | 78 / 15 / 28 / 5 | 10/10 each | 88 / 47 / 67 / 25 |
| 1000 vars, ratio 3.5 | 187 / 77 / 98 / 52 | 10/10 each | 11.1k / 16.1k / 12.0k / 10.2k |
| 20000 vars, ratio 3.5 | 3802 / 1527 / 2024 / 1036 | 9/10, 9/10, 9/10, 10/10 | 123k / 169k / 162k / 118k |
| 5000 vars, ratio 3.9 | 1098 / 482 / 631 / 360 | 2/3 each | 3.06M / 0.76M / 1.84M / 3.24M |
| AIM yes-set, 48 instances | 46 / 18 / 21 / 26 | 27 / 31 / 31 / 27 | — |

Likho leaves the fewest broken clauses in every row. On random 3-SAT it is fastest
at 1000/2.0, 1000/3.5 and 20000/3.5, and the only start that solves all ten
20000-var instances at this budget; it is slower than both rarest orders at
5000/3.9. On the AIM yes-set it ties majority at 27/48 and fails the same 21
instances, while rarest reaches 31/48. So the repair improves the starting
assignment much more reliably than it changes which hard instances the search can
reach.

The max-of-polarities rarest order leaves 2-3x fewer broken clauses than majority,
but ~30% more than the total-occurrence order. It is faster on 1000-var/3.5 and
20000-var/3.5, slower on 5000-var/3.9; on the AIM yes-set both rarest orders solve
the same 31/48 (identical failure sets) versus 27/48 for majority. It changes which
near-solutions are reachable more than it changes total coverage.

Rarest-first is still **worse** than majority at scale. Why: it satisfies each clause
with the first literal it can and never adds redundancy, so almost
every satisfied clause hangs on a single variable. On the 20000-var / ratio 3.5 instance
77% of variables are prime after rarest-first (62% after majority), only 23% are neutral
(38%), and 63% of the broken clauses contain no neutral variable at all, i.e. no free flip
(26% after majority) -- measured with the old ordering. Fewer problems, but most of the
remaining ones cannot be fixed
without breaking something. Likho attacks exactly that: when no neutral is left it
uses twin primes instead of giving up. Group mode's merge, which only fires neutrals,
is hit the same way: its leftover barely changed (e.g. 105.7 -> 95.0 unmerged at ratio
4.2). `majority` stays the default.

Reproduce with `make bench-rarest ARGS="1000 3.5 10 200000 9"` (or
`ARGS="file.cnf 100000 20"`); `steps = 0` measures init quality only. The harness
also reimplements the old total-occurrence order as a baseline, so all four starts
run the same search code.

static bool likho_close(DomainSearch *d) {
    Solver *s = d->s;
    if (++d->nodes > LIKHO_SEARCH_NODES) return false;
    /* find a newly broken clause among the occurrences of domain vars */

            /* newly broken: branch on repair vars (false in c, unflipped, not in domain) */
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, c);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, c);

                if (d->in[u] || d->flipped[u]) continue;
                if (lit_value(cl[j], s->assignment[u])) continue;  /* must be false to help */
                d->in[u] = 1; d->dom[d->n++] = u;
                if (likho_close(d)) return true;
                d->n--; d->in[u] = 0;
            }
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

/* Re-derive one variable's state, break and make counts from the current
 * assignment in a single pass over its occurrences.
 *
 * Ranking invariant (relied on by the group merge):
 *   VAR_PRIME or VAR_TWIN <=> break_count >= 1  (sole support of a solved clause)
 *   VAR_NEUTRAL           <=> break_count == 0  (flipping can never un-solve a clause)
 * Neutrality is a property of the *current* assignment, not of the variable. */
static void refresh_var(Solver *s, size_t v) {
    size_t satisfied = 0, rogue_occ = 0, breaks = 0, min_support = SIZE_MAX;
    bool prime = false;
    bool val = s->assignment[v];
    for (size_t i = s->occ_off[v]; i < s->occ_off[v + 1]; i++) {
        Occ o = s->occ[i];
        uint32_t c = s->sat[o.clause];
        if (c == 0) { rogue_occ++; continue; }
        if (val == o.positive) {
            satisfied++;
            if (c < min_support) min_support = c;
            if (c == 1) { prime = true; breaks++; }
        }
    }
    VarStats *st = &s->stats[v];
    st->satisfied_occurrences = satisfied;
    st->rogue_occurrences = rogue_occ;
    st->break_count = breaks;
    st->make_count = rogue_occ;  /* a rogue clause has no true literal, so every incidence is a "make" */
    st->rank = SIZE_MAX;
    if (occ_count(s, v) == 0) { st->state = VAR_UNUSED; st->min_support = 0; }
    else if (prime) { st->state = VAR_PRIME; st->min_support = 1; }
    else { st->state = VAR_NEUTRAL; st->min_support = satisfied == 0 ? 0 : min_support; }
}

static void refresh_all(Solver *s) {
    for (size_t v = 0; v < s->cnf->n_vars; v++) refresh_var(s, v);
    s->stats_dirty = false;
}

void solver_flip(Solver *s, size_t var) {
    s->assignment[var] = !s->assignment[var];
    s->stats_dirty = true;  /* states are re-derived lazily, only for candidates actually examined */
    for (size_t i = s->occ_off[var]; i < s->occ_off[var + 1]; i++) {
        Occ o = s->occ[i];
        uint32_t old = s->sat[o.clause];
        bool now_true = s->assignment[var] == o.positive;
        uint32_t nw = now_true ? old + 1 : old - 1;
        s->sat[o.clause] = nw;
        if (old == 0 && nw > 0) remove_rogue(s, o.clause);
        else if (old > 0 && nw == 0) add_rogue(s, o.clause);
    }
}

static int cand_cmp(const Candidate *a, const Candidate *b) {
    if (a->cls != b->cls) return a->cls < b->cls ? -1 : 1;                 /* neutral before prime */
    if (a->support != b->support) return a->support > b->support ? -1 : 1; /* stronger support first */
    if (a->breaks != b->breaks) return a->breaks < b->breaks ? -1 : 1;     /* fewer breaks */
    if (a->makes != b->makes) return a->makes > b->makes ? -1 : 1;         /* more makes */
    return a->var < b->var ? -1 : (a->var > b->var);
}

/* Score the variables of one rogue clause and sort them best-first. */
static size_t rank_candidates(Solver *s, size_t clause) {
    const Lit *c = cnf_clause(s->cnf, clause);
    size_t n = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, clause);
    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) {
        size_t v = c[k].var;
        refresh_var(s, v);
        const VarStats *st = &s->stats[v];
        Candidate cd = { v, 0, 0, st->break_count, st->make_count };
        switch (st->state) {
            case VAR_NEUTRAL: cd.cls = 0; cd.support = st->min_support; break;
            case VAR_PRIME:
            case VAR_TWIN:    cd.cls = 1; cd.support = 1; break;   /* a twin is still a prime on its own */
            case VAR_UNUSED:  cd.cls = 2; cd.support = SIZE_MAX; break;
        }
        size_t j = k;  /* insertion sort: clauses are tiny */
        while (j > 0 && cand_cmp(&cd, &s->cands[j - 1]) < 0) { s->cands[j] = s->cands[j - 1]; j--; }
        s->cands[j] = cd;
    }
    for (size_t r = 0; r < n; r++) s->stats[s->cands[r].var].rank = r;
    return n;
}

        size_t neg = total - pos;
        s->assignment[v] = (majority && pos != neg) ? pos > neg : rng_bool(&s->rng);
    }
    rebuild_counts(s);
}

/* ---- Likho: majority start + one-flip-per-variable repair pass ---------- */

/* a is a prime in a rogue clause. Flipping it breaks every clause where it is
 * the sole true literal; take the first such clause and try its other (false)
 * literals as partners. b is a twin iff b is an unflipped prime or neutral and
 * flipping both leaves every clause containing a or b satisfied. (A neutral b
 * is flipped for free and gives the sole-support clause a second support, which
 * liberates a: the move a neutral-only scan never reaches, since b need not sit
 * in a rogue clause.) A flip toggles its
 * literal in each such clause, so a clause that is rogue after the pair flip
 * was satisfied before it -- exactly the breakage that rules the pair out.
 * shortcut: only the first sole-support clause is searched; a prime with
 * several sole supports rarely has one partner that fixes them all. */
static bool likho_twin(Solver *s, size_t a, const unsigned char *flipped, size_t *partner) {
    if (flipped[a] || solver_refresh_var(s, a).state != VAR_PRIME) return false;
    bool aval = s->assignment[a];
    size_t sole = SIZE_MAX;
    for (size_t i = s->occ_off[a]; i < s->occ_off[a + 1]; i++) {
        Occ o = s->occ[i];
        if (o.positive == aval && s->sat[o.clause] == 1) { sole = o.clause; break; }
    }
    if (sole == SIZE_MAX) return false;
    const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, sole);
    size_t n = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, sole);
    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) {
        size_t b = cl[k].var;
        if (b == a || flipped[b]) continue;
        VarState bs = solver_refresh_var(s, b).state;
        if (bs != VAR_PRIME && bs != VAR_NEUTRAL) continue;
        solver_flip(s, a);
        solver_flip(s, b);
        bool clean = true;
        for (size_t i = s->occ_off[a]; i < s->occ_off[a + 1] && clean; i++)
            if (s->sat[s->occ[i].clause] == 0) clean = false;
        for (size_t i = s->occ_off[b]; i < s->occ_off[b + 1] && clean; i++)
            if (s->sat[s->occ[i].clause] == 0) clean = false;
        if (clean) {
            s->stats[a].state = VAR_TWIN;   /* phase-2 label; the next refresh re-derives it */
            s->stats[b].state = VAR_TWIN;
            *partner = b;
            return true;
        }
        solver_flip(s, b);
        solver_flip(s, a);
    }
    return false;
}

bool solver_likho(Solver *s) {
    solver_init_majority(s);
    size_t nv = s->cnf->n_vars, nc = s->cnf->n_clauses;
    unsigned char *flipped = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1);
    size_t *snap = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *snap);
    if (!flipped || !snap) { free(flipped); free(snap); return false; }
    while (s->n_rogue > 0) {
        size_t nr = s->n_rogue;
        memcpy(snap, s->rogue, nr * sizeof *snap);
        bool moved = false;
        /* Neutrals first: a neutral flip breaks nothing, so it only removes
         * clauses from the rogue set. Re-scanning next round also catches the
         * primes this pass liberated (they are neutral now). */
        for (size_t i = 0; i < nr; i++) {
            size_t c = snap[i];
            if (!solver_clause_is_rogue(s, c)) continue;
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, c);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, c);
            for (size_t k = 0; k < len; k++) {
                size_t v = cl[k].var;
                if (flipped[v]) continue;
                if (solver_refresh_var(s, v).state != VAR_NEUTRAL) continue;
                solver_flip(s, v);
                flipped[v] = 1;
                moved = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (moved) continue;   /* prefer neutrals, including freshly liberated primes */
        /* Twins: only reached when no rogue clause has a neutral left. A clean
         * pair flip also adds no new rogue clause, so this pass can keep going. */
        for (size_t i = 0; i < nr; i++) {
            size_t c = snap[i];
            if (!solver_clause_is_rogue(s, c)) continue;
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, c);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, c);
            for (size_t k = 0; k < len; k++) {
                size_t v = cl[k].var, partner;
                if (flipped[v]) continue;
                if (!likho_twin(s, v, flipped, &partner)) continue;
                flipped[v] = 1;
                flipped[partner] = 1;
                moved = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (!moved) break;   /* stuck: no neutral and no twin anywhere */
    }
    free(flipped); free(snap);
    return true;
}

static ResultSolve make_sat(const Solver *s, size_t steps, size_t restart) {
    size_t nv = s->cnf->n_vars;
    bool *a = malloc(nv ? nv : 1);
    if (!a) return ERRF(ResultSolve, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
    if (nv) memcpy(a, s->assignment, nv);
    return OK(ResultSolve, ((SolveResult){ SOLVE_SAT, a, nv, steps, restart, 0, NULL, 0 }));

static bool likho_breaks_nothing(const Solver *s, size_t v) {
    bool val = s->assignment[v];
    for (size_t i = s->occ_off[v]; i < s->occ_off[v + 1]; i++) {
        Occ o = s->occ[i];
        if (o.positive == val && s->sat[o.clause] == 1) return false;
    }
    return true;
}
```
