bool solver_likho(Solver *s, const SolverConfig *cfg) {
    size_t nv = s->cnf->n_vars, nc = s->cnf->n_clauses;
    size_t max_vars = cfg && cfg->likho_domain_max ? cfg->likho_domain_max : LIKHO_DOMAIN_MAX;
    size_t max_nodes = cfg && cfg->likho_search_nodes ? cfg->likho_search_nodes : LIKHO_SEARCH_NODES;
    bool domains_first = cfg && cfg->likho_domains_first;
    if (max_vars > nv) max_vars = nv;   /* a domain cannot be larger than the formula */
    if (max_vars == 0) max_vars = 1;    /* domain of one: the prime alone, no repair */
    memset(s->assignment, 0, nv * sizeof *s->assignment);
    rebuild_counts(s);
    unsigned char *flipped = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1);
    unsigned char *in = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1);
    size_t *snap = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *snap);
    size_t *dom = malloc(max_vars * sizeof *dom);
    if (!flipped || !in || !snap || !dom) {
        free(flipped); free(in); free(snap); free(dom);
        return false;
    }
    while (s->n_rogue > 0) {
        size_t nr = s->n_rogue;
        memcpy(snap, s->rogue, nr * sizeof *snap);
        /* With -deep-dive the domain pass goes first; either way the other
         * pass runs only when this one found nothing, then the next round
         * re-snapshots so freshly liberated primes are seen as neutral. */
        bool moved = domains_first
            ? likho_domain_pass(s, snap, nr, flipped, in, dom, max_vars, max_nodes)
            : likho_neutral_pass(s, snap, nr, flipped);
        if (!moved)
            moved = domains_first
                ? likho_neutral_pass(s, snap, nr, flipped)
                : likho_domain_pass(s, snap, nr, flipped, in, dom, max_vars, max_nodes);
        if (!moved) break;   /* stuck: no neutral and no switch domain anywhere */
    }
    free(flipped); free(in); free(snap); free(dom);
    return true;
}

static ResultSolve make_sat(const Solver *s, size_t steps, size_t restart) {
    size_t nv = s->cnf->n_vars;
    bool *a = malloc(nv ? nv : 1);
    if (!a) return ERRF(ResultSolve, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
    if (nv) memcpy(a, s->assignment, nv);
    return OK(ResultSolve, ((SolveResult){ SOLVE_SAT, a, nv, steps, restart, 0, NULL, 0 }));
}

/* Sound UNSAT pre-check: only a unit clause and its negation are contradictory.
 * For length >= 2, a clause and its pointwise negation are satisfiable, e.g.
 * (1 2 3) and (-1 -2 -3) are both true at x1=1, x2=0, x3=0. */
bool cnf_find_contradictions(const Cnf *cnf, Contradiction **out, size_t *out_n) {
/* -deep-dive VARS NODES: cap switch domains, and fire them before neutrals. */
static ResultUnit opt_deep_dive(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *vars, const char *nodes) {
    TRY0(ResultUnit, parse_size(flag, vars, &cli->cfg.likho_domain_max));
    TRY0(ResultUnit, parse_size(flag, nodes, &cli->cfg.likho_search_nodes));
    if (cli->cfg.likho_domain_max < 1)
        return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "%s needs at least 1 variable per domain", flag);
    if (cli->cfg.likho_search_nodes < 1)
        return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "%s needs at least 1 search node", flag);
    cli->cfg.likho_domains_first = true;
    cli->cfg.init = INIT_LIKHO;   /* deep-dive is a Likho mode */
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
}
static ResultUnit opt_diversify(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    return parse_size(flag, value, &cli->gcfg.diversify);
}

static void print_progress(void *ctx, size_t steps, size_t unsat) {
    (void)ctx;
    fprintf(stderr, "[%zu steps] %zu unsatisfied\n", steps, unsat);
}
static ResultUnit opt_progress(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    TRY0(ResultUnit, parse_size(flag, value, &cli->cfg.progress_every));
    cli->cfg.on_progress = cli->cfg.progress_every ? print_progress : NULL;
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
}

typedef struct { const char *flag; OptApply apply; } OptSpec;
static const OptSpec OPTS[] = {
        "                      [--mode plain|groups] [--max-groups 1..1024] [--merge free|directed]\n"
        "                      [--diversify N] [--group-len N]\n"
        "                      [--init majority|rarest|likho] [-deep-dive VARS NODES]\n");
}

static ResultUnit parse_args(int argc, char **argv, Cli *cli) {
    if (argc < 2) return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Missing INPUT.cnf");
    cli->input = argv[1];
    for (int i = 2; i < argc; i += 2) {
        if (strcmp(argv[i], "-deep-dive") == 0 || strcmp(argv[i], "--deep-dive") == 0) {
            if (i + 2 >= argc) return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Missing values for %s", argv[i]);
            TRY0(ResultUnit, opt_deep_dive(cli, argv[i], argv[i + 1], argv[i + 2]));
            i += 1;   /* consumed two values; the loop's step lands on the next flag */
            continue;
        }
        const OptSpec *spec = NULL;
        for (size_t k = 0; k < sizeof OPTS / sizeof OPTS[0]; k++)
            if (strcmp(OPTS[k].flag, argv[i]) == 0) { spec = &OPTS[k]; break; }
        if (!spec) return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Unknown option: %s", argv[i]);
        if (i + 1 >= argc) return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Missing value for %s", argv[i]);
        TRY0(ResultUnit, spec->apply(cli, argv[i], argv[i + 1]));
    }
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
}

static void test_likho_properties(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 25; i++) {
        Cnf c = random_cnf(60 + 20 * (i % 4), (int)((60 + 20 * (i % 4)) * (2.0 + 0.4 * (i % 5))), 700 + (uint64_t)i);
        Solver *base = must_solver(&c, 7), *a = must_solver(&c, 7), *b = must_solver(&c, 7);
        init_zero(base, c.n_vars);
        size_t before = solver_unsatisfied_count(base);
        CHECK(solver_likho(a, NULL) && solver_likho(b, NULL));
        CHECK(memcmp(solver_assignment(a), solver_assignment(b), c.n_vars) == 0);   /* same seed => same repair */
        CHECK(solver_unsatisfied_count(a) <= before);                               /* never worse than the zero start */
        CHECK(solver_unsatisfied_count(a) == brute_unsat(&c, solver_assignment(a)));/* counters consistent */
        solver_free(base); solver_free(a); solver_free(b);

        SolverConfig cfg = solver_config_default();
        cfg.init = INIT_LIKHO;
        cfg.max_steps = 20000; cfg.restarts = 2;
        Solver *s = must_solver(&c, 5);
        ResultSolve r = solver_solve(s, &cfg);
        CHECK(r.ok);
        if (r.ok && r.val.status == SOLVE_SAT) CHECK(verify(&c, r.val.assignment, r.val.n_vars));
        if (r.ok) solve_result_free(&r.val);
        solver_free(s);
        cnf_free(&c);
    }
}

static void test_likho_pre_cook(void) {
    /* The pre-cook assignment is Likho's phase 1. On this formula both
     * majority and rarest already solve it, so the repair must leave the
     * pre-cooked assignment untouched. */
    Cnf c = must_parse("p cnf 5 3\n"
                       "1 2 3 0\n"
                       "-1 4 5 0\n"
                       "-2 -4 3 0\n");
    SolverConfig cfg = solver_config_default();
    cfg.likho_pre_cook = INIT_MAJORITY;
    Solver *m = must_solver(&c, 1), *s = must_solver(&c, 1);
    solver_init_majority(m);
    CHECK(solver_unsatisfied_count(m) == 0);
    CHECK(solver_likho(s, &cfg));
    CHECK(memcmp(solver_assignment(s), solver_assignment(m), c.n_vars) == 0);
    solver_free(m); solver_free(s);

    cfg.likho_pre_cook = INIT_RAREST;
    m = must_solver(&c, 1); s = must_solver(&c, 1);
    CHECK(solver_init_rarest(m));
    CHECK(solver_unsatisfied_count(m) == 0);
    CHECK(solver_likho(s, &cfg));
    CHECK(memcmp(solver_assignment(s), solver_assignment(m), c.n_vars) == 0);
    solver_free(m); solver_free(s); cnf_free(&c);
}

130: - A neutral flip can liberate a prime (the clause it was propping up gets another
131:   true literal); the next pass sees it as neutral and can flip it. By default
132:   domains are tried only when no neutral is left anywhere; `-deep-dive` reverses
133:   that order and tries a closed domain first.
134: 
135: A domain is capped at 8 variables and its closure search at 64 backtracking nodes,
136: so a prime with an unusually large or conflicting domain is skipped rather than
137: solved. `-deep-dive VARS NODES` raises or lowers both bounds. With the default
138: zero start the repair is deterministic for a given formula; `-pre-cook majority`
139: inherits the majority phase's RNG tie-breaking.
140: 
141: ### Measurements
142: 
143: Measured on random 3-SAT, 10 seeds per row (3 seeds for the 5000-var row), 20
144: restarts, default solver seed. "old" is the previous total-occurrence rarest order,
145: kept for comparison; "likho-dd" is `-deep-dive 32 128`, "likho-pc" is
146: `-pre-cook majority`. All six starts share the same search code:
147: 
148: | instance | broken after init (maj / old / new / likho / dd / pc) | solved | mean flips over solved (maj / old / new / likho / dd / pc) |
149: |---|---|---|---|
150: | 1000 vars, ratio 2.0 | 78 / 15 / 28 / 0 / 0.2 / 0 | 10/10 each | 88 / 47 / 67 / 0 / 1 / 0 |
151: | 1000 vars, ratio 3.5 | 187 / 77 / 98 / 34 / 32 / 10 | 10/10 each | 11.1k / 16.1k / 12.0k / 18.1k / 17.6k / 9.8k |
152: | 20000 vars, ratio 3.5 | 3802 / 1527 / 2024 / 742 / 637 / 209 | 9/10, 9/10, 9/10, 0/10, 0/10, 9/10 | 123k / 169k / 162k / — / — / 129k |
153: | 5000 vars, ratio 3.9 | 1098 / 482 / 631 / 385 / 337 / 126 | 2/3 each | 3.06M / 0.76M / 1.84M / 4.40M / 4.40M / 5.68M |
154: | AIM yes-set, 48 instances | 46 / 18 / 21 / 23 / 22 / 22 | 27 / 31 / 31 / 31 / 31 / 27 | — |
155: 
156: The zero start still leaves 3-5x fewer broken clauses than majority, and it solves
157: 1000/2.0 outright at init (zero flips), but it is a much deeper local minimum. At
158: 20000/3.5 it solves **0/10** at this budget, where majority and both rarest orders
159: solve 9/10; fewer broken clauses does not mean an easier search. `-pre-cook
160: majority` restores the previous majority-start repair exactly (209 broken, 9/10,
161: 129k flips), so pre-cooking is the escape from the zero-start basin. On the AIM
162: yes-set the zero start matches both rarest orders at 31/48 (majority and the
163: majority pre-cook stay at 27/48), so the constructive start pays off there.
164: `-deep-dive 32 128` trims the zero-start init count (637 at 20000, 337 at 5000) but
165: changes no solved count. From a majority pre-cook, domains-first makes 20000/3.5
166: much worse (1/10 at 32 128, 0/3 at the default bounds), so deep-dive is not the
167: escape route; pre-cook without it is. `majority` stays the default start for the
168: plain search.
169: 
170: The max-of-polarities rarest order leaves 2-3x fewer broken clauses than majority,
171: but ~30% more than the total-occurrence order. It is faster on 1000-var/3.5 and
172: 20000-var/3.5, slower on 5000-var/3.9; on the AIM yes-set both rarest orders solve
173: the same 31/48 (identical failure sets) versus 27/48 for majority. It changes which
174: near-solutions are reachable more than it changes total coverage.
175: 
176: Rarest-first is still **worse** than majority at scale. Why: it satisfies each clause
177: with the first literal it can and never adds redundancy, so almost
178: every satisfied clause hangs on a single variable. On the 20000-var / ratio 3.5 instance
179: 77% of variables are prime after rarest-first (62% after majority), only 23% are neutral
180: (38%), and 63% of the broken clauses contain no neutral variable at all, i.e. no free flip
181: (26% after majority) -- measured with the old ordering. Fewer problems, but most of the
182: remaining ones cannot be fixed
183: without breaking something. Likho attacks exactly that: a prime's switch domain
184: chains through other primes until it reaches a neutral, instead of giving up at the
185: first broken clause. Group mode's merge, which only fires neutrals,
186: is hit the same way: its leftover barely changed (e.g. 105.7 -> 95.0 unmerged at ratio
187: 4.2).
188: 
189: Reproduce with `make bench-rarest ARGS="1000 3.5 10 200000 9"` (or
190: `ARGS="file.cnf 100000 20"`); `steps = 0` measures init quality only. The harness
191: also reimplements the old total-occurrence order as a baseline, so all six starts
192: run the same search code; its deep-dive row uses `-deep-dive 32 128` and its
193: pre-cook row uses `-pre-cook majority`.
194: 
195: ## Group mode (`--mode groups`)
196: 
197: Sequential rogue groups with a neutral-driven merge, layered on the same solver
198: (`src/groups.c`). Ranking is unchanged: a variable is **neutral** iff flipping it
199: breaks no solved clause (`break_count == 0`), **prime** iff it is the sole
200: support of at least one (`break_count >= 1`). Neutrality belongs to the *current*
201: assignment, so it changes as flips happen. This invariant is pinned by a test.
202: 
203: ```sh
204: build/3sat input.cnf --mode groups                      # defaults: 16 groups, free merge
205: build/3sat input.cnf --mode groups --max-groups 64 --merge directed --diversify 20
206: build/3sat input.cnf --mode groups --group-len 10 --max-groups 400   # at most 10 clauses per group
207: ```
208: 
209: **Formation.** Start from the `--init` assignment `B` (majority by default).

/* ---- Likho: zero start + switch-domain repair pass --------------------- */

/* A switch domain of a prime is the set of unflipped variables that must flip
 * with it so that no currently satisfied clause becomes rogue. A neutral is
 * its own domain; a prime needs a repair for every clause it solely supports,
 * and a repair may itself be a prime, so domains can chain. Domains are
 * recomputed after each firing and `flipped` enforces the gold rule (every
 * variable fires once): two primes whose domains share a variable share that
 * single flip, and a prime whose domain conflicts with an already fired one is
 * simply not fired. */
/* shortcut: a prime whose domain needs more than either bound is skipped, not
 * solved; -deep-dive raises the bounds. */

typedef struct {
    Solver *s;
    const unsigned char *flipped;
    unsigned char *in;   /* membership of the domain under construction */
    size_t *dom;         /* dom[0] is the prime the domain is for */
    size_t n, nodes, max_vars, max_nodes;
} LikhoSearch;

/* Support of `clause` after flipping every variable of the domain once.
 * Clauses with no domain variable keep their count and are never examined. */
static uint32_t likho_sat_after(const LikhoSearch *d, size_t clause) {
    const Lit *c = cnf_clause(d->s->cnf, clause);
    size_t n = cnf_clause_len(d->s->cnf, clause);
    uint32_t cnt = 0;
    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++)
        cnt += lit_value(c[k], d->s->assignment[c[k].var]) != d->in[c[k].var];
    return cnt;
}

/* true when flipping v alone cannot un-satisfy a clause; those "free" repairs
 * are tried first because they add no new breakage to the domain. */
static bool likho_breaks_nothing(const Solver *s, size_t v) {
    bool val = s->assignment[v];
    for (size_t i = s->occ_off[v]; i < s->occ_off[v + 1]; i++) {
        Occ o = s->occ[i];
        if (o.positive == val && s->sat[o.clause] == 1) return false;
    }
    return true;
}

/* Close the domain: every clause it broke needs a repair from one of its own
 * false literals, recursively. A clause with no free false literal backtracks. */
static bool likho_close(LikhoSearch *d) {
    if (++d->nodes > d->max_nodes) return false;
    Solver *s = d->s;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < d->n; i++) {
        size_t v = d->dom[i];
        for (size_t j = s->occ_off[v]; j < s->occ_off[v + 1]; j++) {
            size_t c = s->occ[j].clause;
            if (likho_sat_after(d, c) != 0) continue;
            if (d->n >= d->max_vars) return false;
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, c);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, c);
            for (int pass = 0; pass < 2; pass++)
                for (size_t k = 0; k < len; k++) {
                    size_t u = cl[k].var;
                    if (d->in[u] || d->flipped[u]) continue;
                    if (lit_value(cl[k], s->assignment[u])) continue;   /* must be false to help */
                    if ((pass == 0) != likho_breaks_nothing(s, u)) continue;
                    d->in[u] = 1; d->dom[d->n++] = u;
                    if (likho_close(d)) return true;
                    d->n--; d->in[u] = 0;
                }
            return false;   /* this clause cannot be repaired: backtrack */
        }
    }
    return true;   /* nothing broke */
}

/* Switch domain of v, or 0 when none fits the size/node bounds. On success the
 * membership flags are cleared again; the caller applies dom[0..n). */
static size_t likho_domain(Solver *s, size_t v, const unsigned char *flipped,
                           unsigned char *in, size_t *dom,
                           size_t max_vars, size_t max_nodes) {
    LikhoSearch d = { s, flipped, in, dom, 1, 0, max_vars, max_nodes };
    dom[0] = v;
    in[v] = 1;
    bool ok = likho_close(&d);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < d.n; i++) in[dom[i]] = 0;  /* failed search leaves n == 1 */
    return ok ? d.n : 0;
}

/* One neutral flip per rogue clause: it breaks nothing, so it only removes
 * clauses from the rogue set. Returns true if anything fired. */
static bool likho_neutral_pass(Solver *s, const size_t *snap, size_t nr,
                               unsigned char *flipped) {
    bool moved = false;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < nr; i++) {
        size_t c = snap[i];
        if (!solver_clause_is_rogue(s, c)) continue;
        const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, c);
        size_t len = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, c);
        for (size_t k = 0; k < len; k++) {
            size_t v = cl[k].var;
            if (flipped[v]) continue;
            if (solver_refresh_var(s, v).state != VAR_NEUTRAL) continue;
            solver_flip(s, v);
            flipped[v] = 1;
            moved = true;
            break;
        }
    }
    return moved;
}

/* One closed switch domain per rogue clause. A closed domain adds no rogue
 * clause, so this pass can keep going and the next round re-derives the states
 * it changed. Returns true if anything fired. */
static bool likho_domain_pass(Solver *s, const size_t *snap, size_t nr,
                              unsigned char *flipped, unsigned char *in, size_t *dom,
                              size_t max_vars, size_t max_nodes) {
    bool moved = false;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < nr; i++) {
        size_t c = snap[i];
        if (!solver_clause_is_rogue(s, c)) continue;
        const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(s->cnf, c);
        size_t len = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, c);
        for (size_t k = 0; k < len; k++) {
            size_t v = cl[k].var;
            if (flipped[v]) continue;
            size_t n = likho_domain(s, v, flipped, in, dom, max_vars, max_nodes);
            if (n == 0) continue;
            for (size_t j = 0; j < n; j++) { solver_flip(s, dom[j]); flipped[dom[j]] = 1; }
            moved = true;
            break;
        }
    }
    return moved;
}

bool solver_likho(Solver *s, const SolverConfig *cfg) {
    size_t nv = s->cnf->n_vars, nc = s->cnf->n_clauses;
    size_t max_vars = cfg && cfg->likho_domain_max ? cfg->likho_domain_max : LIKHO_DOMAIN_MAX;
    size_t max_nodes = cfg && cfg->likho_search_nodes ? cfg->likho_search_nodes : LIKHO_SEARCH_NODES;
    bool domains_first = cfg && cfg->likho_domains_first;
    InitMode pre = cfg ? cfg->likho_pre_cook : INIT_ZERO;
    if (max_vars > nv) max_vars = nv;   /* a domain cannot be larger than the formula */
    if (max_vars == 0) max_vars = 1;    /* domain of one: the prime alone, no repair */
    if (pre == INIT_MAJORITY) solver_init_majority(s);
    else if (pre == INIT_RAREST) { if (!solver_init_rarest(s)) return false; }
    else {
        memset(s->assignment, 0, nv * sizeof *s->assignment);
        rebuild_counts(s);
    }
    unsigned char *flipped = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1);
    unsigned char *in = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1);
    size_t *snap = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *snap);
    size_t *dom = malloc(max_vars * sizeof *dom);
    if (!flipped || !in || !snap || !dom) {
        free(flipped); free(in); free(snap); free(dom);
        return false;
    }
    while (s->n_rogue > 0) {
        size_t nr = s->n_rogue;
        memcpy(snap, s->rogue, nr * sizeof *snap);
        /* With -deep-dive the domain pass goes first; either way the other
         * pass runs only when this one found nothing, then the next round
         * re-snapshots so freshly liberated primes are seen as neutral. */
        bool moved = domains_first
            ? likho_domain_pass(s, snap, nr, flipped, in, dom, max_vars, max_nodes)
            : likho_neutral_pass(s, snap, nr, flipped);
        if (!moved)
            moved = domains_first
                ? likho_neutral_pass(s, snap, nr, flipped)
                : likho_domain_pass(s, snap, nr, flipped, in, dom, max_vars, max_nodes);
        if (!moved) break;   /* stuck: no neutral and no switch domain anywhere */
    }
    free(flipped); free(in); free(snap); free(dom);
    return true;
}

static ResultSolve make_sat(const Solver *s, size_t steps, size_t restart) {
    size_t nv = s->cnf->n_vars;
    bool *a = malloc(nv ? nv : 1);
    if (!a) return ERRF(ResultSolve, ERR_NOMEM, "out of memory");
    if (nv) memcpy(a, s->assignment, nv);
    return OK(ResultSolve, ((SolveResult){ SOLVE_SAT, a, nv, steps, restart, 0, NULL, 0 }));
}

A "node" is one call to `likho_close()` — one state in the depth-first search that builds a prime's switch domain (`src/sat.c`):

```c
static bool likho_close(LikhoSearch *d) {
    if (++d->nodes > d->max_nodes) return false;
    ...
    d->in[u] = 1; d->dom[d->n++] = u;
    if (likho_close(d)) return true;   // <- next node
    d->n--; d->in[u] = 0;              // backtrack
```

So `-deep-dive VARS NODES` gives each prime at most **NODES closure attempts**:

- Node 1 is the root check: the prime alone, i.e. "which satisfied clauses does flipping it break?"
- Every candidate repair variable added to the domain and re-checked is one more node; failed branches that backtrack still consume nodes, so it is a total work budget, not a depth limit.
- It is **not** a clause count, variable count, or time limit. One node scans all clauses touched by the current domain, so cost per node grows with domain size.
- When the budget runs out, `likho_domain()` returns 0: that prime is skipped (the pass then tries the next variable, or falls back to a neutral), it does not abort the whole repair.

Consequences: `NODES 1` permits only size-1 domains, i.e. no prime repairs at all (only neutrals); the unit test uses exactly that to force the fallback. The default 64 is plenty for the common 2–5 variable domains — measured on 20000/3.5, only 1,270 of 10,594 prime searches hit the node cap, while 8,470 hit the 8-variable cap. /* Score the variables of one rogue clause and sort them best-first. */
static size_t rank_candidates(Solver *s, size_t clause) {
    const Lit *c = cnf_clause(s->cnf, clause);
    size_t n = cnf_clause_len(s->cnf, clause);
    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) {
        size_t v = c[k].var;
        refresh_var(s, v);
        const VarStats *st = &s->stats[v];
        Candidate cd = { v, 0, 0, st->break_count, st->make_count };
        switch (st->state) {
            case VAR_NEUTRAL: cd.cls = 0; cd.support = st->min_support; break;
            case VAR_PRIME:   cd.cls = 1; cd.support = 1; break;
            case VAR_UNUSED:  cd.cls = 2; cd.support = SIZE_MAX; break;
        }
        size_t j = k;  /* insertion sort: clauses are tiny */
        while (j > 0 && cand_cmp(&cd, &s->cands[j - 1]) < 0) { s->cands[j] = s->cands[j - 1]; j--; }
        s->cands[j] = cd;
    }
    for (size_t r = 0; r < n; r++) s->stats[s->cands[r].var].rank = r;
    return n;
}

static void random_assignment(Solver *s, bool majority) {
    for (size_t v = 0; v < s->cnf->n_vars; v++) {
        size_t pos = 0, total = occ_count(s, v);
        for (size_t i = s->occ_off[v]; i < s->occ_off[v + 1]; i++) pos += s->occ[i].positive;
        size_t neg = total - pos;
        s->assignment[v] = (majority && pos != neg) ? pos > neg : rng_bool(&s->rng);
    }
    rebuild_counts(s);
}

typedef struct { size_t key, var; } Rare;

static bool rare_before(Rare a, Rare b) {
    if (a.key != b.key) return a.key < b.key;
    return a.var < b.var;
}

static void rare_push(Rare *h, size_t *n, Rare x) {
    size_t i = (*n)++;
    while (i > 0) {
        size_t p = (i - 1) / 2;
        if (!rare_before(x, h[p])) break;
        h[i] = h[p];
        i = p;
    }
    h[i] = x;
}

static void rare_sift_down(Rare *h, size_t n, size_t i, Rare x) {
    for (;;) {
        size_t l = 2 * i + 1;
        if (l >= n) break;
        size_t c = l;
        if (l + 1 < n && rare_before(h[l + 1], h[l])) c = l + 1;
        if (!rare_before(h[c], x)) break;
        h[i] = h[c];
        i = c;
    }
    h[i] = x;
}

static Rare rare_pop(Rare *h, size_t *n) {
    Rare top = h[0], last = h[--(*n)];
    if (*n) rare_sift_down(h, *n, 0, last);
    return top;
}

/* Rarest = fewest clauses holding x or !x, whichever is larger. Only clauses
 * that are still unsatisfied count, so satisfying a clause removes the
 * overlapping occurrences of every variable it contains. */
static size_t rare_key(const uint32_t *pos, const uint32_t *neg, size_t v) {
    return pos[v] > neg[v] ? pos[v] : neg[v];
}

bool solver_init_rarest(Solver *s) {
    const Cnf *cnf = s->cnf;
    size_t nv = cnf->n_vars, nc = cnf->n_clauses;
    uint32_t *unset = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *unset);   /* unassigned variables left in each clause */

        free(unset); free(done); free(pos); free(neg); free(assigned); free(heap);
        return false;
    }
    for (size_t c = 0; c < nc; c++) unset[c] = (uint32_t)cnf_clause_len(cnf, c);
    size_t hn = 0;
    for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) {
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++)
            if (s->occ[k].positive) pos[v]++; else neg[v]++;
        rare_push(heap, &hn, (Rare){ rare_key(pos, neg, v), v });

        size_t v = top.var;
        size_t fp = 0, fn = 0, op = 0, on = 0, tp = 0, tn = 0;
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++) {
            Occ o = s->occ[k];
            if (o.positive) tp++; else tn++;
            if (done[o.clause]) continue;
            if (unset[o.clause] == 1) { if (o.positive) fp++; else fn++; }
            else                      { if (o.positive) op++; else on++; }
        }
        bool val;
        if (fp != fn) val = fp > fn;
        else if (op != on) val = op > on;
        else if (tp != tn) val = tp > tn;
        else val = false;
        s->assignment[v] = val;
        assigned[v] = 1;
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++) {
            Occ o = s->occ[k];
            unset[o.clause]--;
            if (done[o.clause] || o.positive != val) continue;
            done[o.clause] = 1;

            for (size_t j = 0; j < len; j++) {
                size_t u = cl[j].var;
                if (assigned[u]) continue;
                if (cl[j].positive) pos[u]--; else neg[u]--;
                rare_push(heap, &hn, (Rare){ rare_key(pos, neg, u), u });
            }
        }

static ResultUnit opt_merge(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    if (strcmp(value, "free") == 0) cli->gcfg.directed_only = false;
    else if (strcmp(value, "directed") == 0) cli->gcfg.directed_only = true;
    else return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Invalid value for %s: `%s` (expected free|directed)", flag, value);
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
}

static ResultUnit opt_init(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    if (strcmp(value, "majority") == 0) cli->cfg.init = INIT_MAJORITY;
    else if (strcmp(value, "rarest") == 0) cli->cfg.init = INIT_RAREST;
    else if (strcmp(value, "likho") == 0) cli->cfg.init = INIT_LIKHO;
    else return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Invalid value for %s: `%s` (expected majority|rarest|likho)", flag, value);
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
}
static ResultUnit opt_pre_cook(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    if (strcmp(value, "zero") == 0) cli->cfg.likho_pre_cook = INIT_ZERO;
    else if (strcmp(value, "majority") == 0) cli->cfg.likho_pre_cook = INIT_MAJORITY;
    else if (strcmp(value, "rarest") == 0) cli->cfg.likho_pre_cook = INIT_RAREST;
    else return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Invalid value for %s: `%s` (expected zero|majority|rarest)", flag, value);
    cli->cfg.init = INIT_LIKHO;   /* pre-cook is a Likho mode */
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
}
static ResultUnit opt_group_len(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    return parse_size(flag, value, &cli->gcfg.group_len);
}
/* -deep-dive VARS NODES: cap switch domains, and fire them before neutrals. */
static ResultUnit opt_deep_dive(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *vars, const char *nodes) {
    TRY0(ResultUnit, parse_size(flag, vars, &cli->cfg.likho_domain_max));
    TRY0(ResultUnit, parse_size(flag, nodes, &cli->cfg.likho_search_nodes));
    if (cli->cfg.likho_domain_max < 1)
        return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "%s needs at least 1 variable per domain", flag);
    if (cli->cfg.likho_search_nodes < 1)
        return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "%s needs at least 1 search node", flag);
    cli->cfg.likho_domains_first = true;
    cli->cfg.init = INIT_LIKHO;   /* deep-dive is a Likho mode */
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
}

static ResultUnit opt_diversify(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    return parse_size(flag, value, &cli->gcfg.diversify);
}

/* ---- rarest-first constructive start ------------------------------------ */

static size_t brute_unsat(const Cnf *c, const bool *a) {
    size_t n = 0;
    for (size_t ci = 0; ci < c->n_clauses; ci++) {
        bool any = false;
        for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(c, ci); k++) any |= lit_value(cnf_clause(c, ci)[k], a[cnf_clause(c, ci)[k].var]);
        n += !any;
    }
    return n;
}

static void test_init_rarest_hand_checked(void) {
    /* Rarest by max(#x,#!x): x2 and x3 have 1, x1 has 2, so x2 goes first.
     * x2 false satisfies (-2 -3), which drops x3's negative occurrence; x3 then
     * takes (1 3) as an open clause and goes true. x1 last: both clauses forced. */
    Cnf c = must_parse("p cnf 3 3\n1 2 0\n1 3 0\n-2 -3 0\n");
    Solver *s = must_solver(&c, 1);
    CHECK(solver_init_rarest(s));
    const bool *a = solver_assignment(s);
    CHECK(a[0] && !a[1] && a[2]);
    CHECK(solver_unsatisfied_count(s) == 0);
    solver_free(s); cnf_free(&c);

    /* x2 occurs once, x1 twice. x2 goes first: (-1 2) open -> true. x1: unit (1) is forced -> true. */
    Cnf d = must_parse("p cnf 2 2\n1 0\n-1 2 0\n");
    s = must_solver(&d, 1);
    CHECK(solver_init_rarest(s));
    a = solver_assignment(s);
    CHECK(a[0] && a[1] && solver_unsatisfied_count(s) == 0);
    solver_free(s); cnf_free(&d);

    /* variable that occurs nowhere is set false */
    Cnf e = must_parse("p cnf 3 1\n1 2 0\n");
    s = must_solver(&e, 1);
    CHECK(solver_init_rarest(s));
    CHECK(!solver_assignment(s)[2]);
    solver_free(s); cnf_free(&e);
}

static void test_init_rarest_properties(void) {
    SolverConfig cfg = solver_config_default();
    cfg.init = INIT_RAREST;
    cfg.max_steps = 20000; cfg.restarts = 2;
    for (int i = 0; i < 25; i++) {
        Cnf c = random_cnf(60 + 20 * (i % 4), (int)((60 + 20 * (i % 4)) * (2.0 + 0.4 * (i % 5))), 500 + (uint64_t)i);
        Solver *a = must_solver(&c, 1), *b = must_solver(&c, 99);   /* different RNG seeds: no randomness used */
        CHECK(solver_init_rarest(a) && solver_init_rarest(b));
        CHECK(memcmp(solver_assignment(a), solver_assignment(b), c.n_vars) == 0);   /* deterministic */
        CHECK(solver_unsatisfied_count(a) == brute_unsat(&c, solver_assignment(a))); /* counters consistent */
        solver_free(a); solver_free(b);

        gc.max_groups = 64;

        if (g.ok) { check_group_result(&c, &g.val); group_result_free(&g.val); }

/* Naive spec of --init rarest: every step recomputes, for each unset variable, max(#x, #!x) over the
 * clauses not yet satisfied, takes the smallest (ties: lowest id), then applies forced > open > total
 * polarity > false. No heap, no incremental counters. */
static void rarest_reference(const Cnf *c, bool *out) {
    size_t nv = c->n_vars, nc = c->n_clauses;

    for (size_t step = 0; step < nv; step++) {
        size_t best = SIZE_MAX, best_key = 0;
        for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) {
            if (set[v]) continue;
            size_t p = 0, n = 0;
            for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++) {
                if (done[ci]) continue;
                for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(c, ci); k++) {
                    Lit l = cnf_clause(c, ci)[k];
                    if (l.var == v) { if (l.positive) p++; else n++; }
                }
            }
            size_t key = p > n ? p : n;
            if (best == SIZE_MAX || key < best_key) { best = v; best_key = key; }
        }
        size_t v = best, fp = 0, fn = 0, op = 0, on = 0, tp = 0, tn = 0;
        for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++) {
            size_t unset_here = 0;
            bool has = false, pos = false;
            for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(c, ci); k++) {
                Lit l = cnf_clause(c, ci)[k];
                if (!set[l.var]) unset_here++;
                if (l.var == v) { has = true; pos = l.positive; }
            }
            if (!has) continue;
            if (pos) tp++; else tn++;
            if (done[ci]) continue;
            if (unset_here == 1) { if (pos) fp++; else fn++; }
            else                 { if (pos) op++; else on++; }
        }
        bool val = (fp != fn) ? fp > fn : (op != on) ? op > on : (tp != tn) ? tp > tn : false;
        out[v] = val; set[v] = true;
        for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++)
            for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(c, ci); k++) {
                Lit l = cnf_clause(c, ci)[k];
                if (l.var == v && l.positive == val) done[ci] = true;
            }
    }
    free(set); free(done);
}

static void check_rarest_matches_reference(const Cnf *c) {
    Solver *s = must_solver(c, 1);
    bool *ref = malloc(c->n_vars ? c->n_vars : 1);
    CHECK(solver_init_rarest(s));
    rarest_reference(c, ref);
    CHECK(c->n_vars == 0 || memcmp(solver_assignment(s), ref, c->n_vars) == 0);
    CHECK(solver_unsatisfied_count(s) == brute_unsat(c, ref));
    free(ref);
    solver_free(s);
}

static void test_init_rarest_matches_reference(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 150; i++) {                           /* random 3-SAT, easy to hard */
        int n = 8 + (i % 7) * 9;
        Cnf c = random_cnf(n, (int)(n * (1.0 + 0.5 * (i % 9))), 9000 + (uint64_t)i);
        check_rarest_matches_reference(&c);
        cnf_free(&c);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < 150; i++) {                           /* general CNF: units, long clauses, unused vars */
        int n = 5 + (i % 6) * 7;
        Cnf c = random_general_cnf(n * 2, n + (i % 5) * 6, 1 + (i % 6), 4000 + (uint64_t)i);
        check_rarest_matches_reference(&c);
        cnf_free(&c);
    }
    Cnf e = must_parse("p cnf 0 0\n");
    check_rarest_matches_reference(&e);
    cnf_free(&e);
    Cnf one = must_parse("p cnf 1 1\n-1 0\n");
    check_rarest_matches_reference(&one);
    cnf_free(&one);
}

static ResultUnit opt_init(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    if (strcmp(value, "majority") == 0) cli->cfg.init = INIT_MAJORITY;
    else if (strcmp(value, "rarest") == 0) cli->cfg.init = INIT_RAREST;
    else if (strcmp(value, "glowest") == 0) cli->cfg.init = INIT_GLOWEST;
    else if (strcmp(value, "likho") == 0) cli->cfg.init = INIT_LIKHO;
    else return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Invalid value for %s: `%s` (expected majority|rarest|glowest|likho)", flag, value);
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
}
static ResultUnit opt_pre_cook(Cli *cli, const char *flag, const char *value) {
    if (strcmp(value, "zero") == 0) cli->cfg.likho_pre_cook = INIT_ZERO;
    else if (strcmp(value, "majority") == 0) cli->cfg.likho_pre_cook = INIT_MAJORITY;
    else if (strcmp(value, "rarest") == 0) cli->cfg.likho_pre_cook = INIT_RAREST;
    else if (strcmp(value, "glowest") == 0) cli->cfg.likho_pre_cook = INIT_GLOWEST;
    else return ERRF(ResultUnit, ERR_USAGE, "Invalid value for %s: `%s` (expected zero|majority|rarest|glowest)", flag, value);
    cli->cfg.init = INIT_LIKHO;   /* pre-cook is a Likho mode */
    return OK_UNIT(ResultUnit);
}

static void test_init_glowest_hand_checked(void) {
    /* Glowest by max(#x,#!x): x1 has 2, x2 and x3 have 1, so x1 goes first.
     * Both clauses are open and positive for x1, so it goes true and satisfies
     * them; x2 and x3 then have no open clause and tie on total polarity, so
     * both go false. */
    Cnf c = must_parse("p cnf 3 3\n1 2 0\n1 3 0\n-2 -3 0\n");

86: ## Initial assignment (`--init`)
87: 
88: Restart 0 starts from one of three starts (later restarts are always random):

90: - `--init majority` (default): every variable takes its majority polarity.

99: The three starts work in both `plain` and `groups` mode; `-deep-dive` is a variant

102: ### Rarest
103: 
104: 1. Repeatedly set the currently **rarest** unassigned variable: the fewest clauses
105:    holding `x` or `!x`, whichever count is larger, and only clauses that are not yet
106:    satisfied count (ties by id). The counts are recomputed after every assignment, so
107:    satisfying a clause removes that overlap from every variable still unset.
108: 2. The variable takes the value that satisfies more **forced**
109:    clauses (open clauses where it is the last unset variable); else more **open**
110:    (not yet satisfied) clauses; else the larger total polarity; else `false`.
111: 
112: ### Likho
113: 
114: `--init likho` starts from `-pre-cook` (`zero`, the default: every variable
115: `false`), then repairs rogue clauses. It only accepts moves that break no
116: satisfied clause, and each variable is flipped at most once:
117: 
118: - A **neutral** variable inside a rogue clause is flipped immediately; it breaks
119:   nothing and satisfies at least that clause.
120: - A **prime** is the sole support of some satisfied clause, so flipping it alone
121:   breaks that clause. Its **switch domain** is the set of other unflipped variables
122:   that must flip with it so every clause it breaks gains a new true literal. A
123:   repair may itself be a prime, so a domain chains: prime -> prime -> ... -> neutral.
124:   The domain is accepted only if the joint flip leaves every touched clause
125:   satisfied. A twin pair is the special case of a domain with one partner.
126: - Domains are recomputed after every firing, and the gold rule (every variable
127:   fires once) means two primes whose domains share a variable share that single
128:   flip, while a prime whose domain conflicts with an already fired one is simply

Answer with the algorithm precisely as implemented:

1. Maintain for each unset variable v: pos[v], neg[v] = number of not-yet-satisfied clauses containing v positively / negatively. A clause is dropped from these counts once it has a true literal.
2. Repeat until all variables set:
   a. Pick the unset variable with the largest key = max(pos[v], neg[v]); ties by lowest id. (Lazy min-heap over inverted key.)
   b. Set v by: forced clauses first (open clauses where v is the last unset variable): count positive vs negative, take the polarity with more; else open clauses: more positive/negative occurrences; else total polarity; else false.
   c. Assign, then for every clause where v's literal is true: mark done, and decrement the matching polarity count of every still-unset variable in that clause. Push updated keys.
3. Unused variables: key 0, all tie → lowest id order, value false.

Also mention complexity: O(total occurrences × log n) with the lazy heap; deterministic, no RNG.

And contrast to rarest: only step 2a differs (largest vs smallest key).

No tools needed. Ponytail closing: skipped restating Likho/rarest internals; the code path is `init_frequency(s, true)` in src/sat.c.

Glowest = rarest's constructive pass with the pick order reversed. Exact algorithm (`init_frequency(s, /*most=*/true)` in `src/sat.c`):

**State.** For every unset variable `v`: `pos[v]`, `neg[v]` = how many **not-yet-satisfied** clauses contain `v` positively / negatively. A clause is removed from these counts the moment it gets a true literal.

**Loop, `n_vars` times:**

1. **Pick** the unset variable with the largest `key(v) = max(pos[v], neg[v])`; ties by lowest variable id. (Implementation: min-heap over `SIZE_MAX - key`, so ties still resolve by id; counts only shrink, and the current key is re-pushed whenever it changes, so stale heap entries are discarded when popped.)
2. **Value** for `v`:
   1. more **forced** clauses: open clauses where `v` is the last unset variable — pick the polarity appearing in more of them;
   2. else more **open** (not-yet-satisfied) clauses;
   3. else the larger total polarity over all its occurrences;
   4. else `false`.
3. **Assign**, then for each clause where that literal is true: mark the clause satisfied and decrement the matching count of every still-unset variable in it, pushing their new keys.
4. Variables with no occurrences have key 0, sort last, and take `false`.

Deterministic, no RNG; O(total occurrences × log n_vars).

The only difference from rarest is step 1: rarest takes the **smallest** key, so glowest front-loads the highest-overlap variables (and their clauses) and rarest front-loads the lowest-overlap ones. That is why glowest ends with fewer broken clauses: satisfying high-overlap variables early removes more clauses from everyone else's counts, leaving fewer clauses supported by a single literal.

```c
/* Value for v given the current partial assignment: forced > open > total > false. */
static bool start_value(const Solver *s, size_t v, const unsigned char *done, const uint32_t *unset) {
    size_t fp = 0, fn = 0, op = 0, on = 0, tp = 0, tn = 0;
    for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++) {
        Occ o = s->occ[k];
        if (o.positive) tp++; else tn++;
        if (done[o.clause]) continue;
        if (unset[o.clause] == 1) { if (o.positive) fp++; else fn++; }
        else                      { if (o.positive) op++; else on++; }
    }
    if (fp != fn) return fp > fn;
    if (op != on) return op > on;
    if (tp != tn) return tp > tn;
    return false;
}
```

Let me write it:

```c
/* ---- min-overlapping constructive start -------------------------------- */

typedef struct { size_t num, den, var; } Overlap;   /* key = num/den; den 0 sorts last */

static bool overlap_before(Overlap a, Overlap b) {
    if (a.den == 0 || b.den == 0) {
        if (a.den != b.den) return b.den == 0;   /* the one with a denominator first */
        return a.var < b.var;
    }
    size_t l = a.num * b.den, r = b.num * a.den;
    if (l != r) return l < r;
    return a.var < b.var;
}

```c
/* Value for v: forced > open > total polarity > false. `done`/`unset` describe
 * the clauses of the partial assignment. */
static bool start_value(const Solver *s, size_t v, const unsigned char *done, const uint32_t *unset) {
    size_t fp = 0, fn = 0, op = 0, on = 0, tp = 0, tn = 0;
    for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++) {
        Occ o = s->occ[k];
        if (o.positive) tp++; else tn++;
        if (done[o.clause]) continue;
        if (unset[o.clause] == 1) { if (o.positive) fp++; else fn++; }
        else                      { if (o.positive) op++; else on++; }
    }
    if (fp != fn) return fp > fn;
    if (op != on) return op > on;
    if (tp != tn) return tp > tn;
    return false;
}
```

Let me write the whole function carefully.

```c
/* ---- min-overlapping constructive start -------------------------------- */

/* Key of a variable for the min-overlapping order: overlap / occurrences.
 * Both terms only move one way (overlap grows, the effective occurrence count
 * shrinks), so the ratio never decreases and the lazy min-heap below can
 * discard stale entries exactly like the rarest heap. A variable with no
 * occurrence left sorts last. */
typedef struct { size_t num, den, var; } Overlap;

static bool overlap_before(Overlap a, Overlap b) {
    if (a.den == 0 || b.den == 0) {
        if (a.den != b.den) return b.den == 0;   /* den == 0 sorts last */
        return a.var < b.var;
    }
    size_t l = a.num * b.den, r = b.num * a.den;
    if (l != r) return l < r;
    return a.var < b.var;
}

static void overlap_push(Overlap *h, size_t *n, Overlap x) {
    size_t i = (*n)++;
    while (i > 0) {
        size_t p = (i - 1) / 2;
        if (!overlap_before(x, h[p])) break;
        h[i] = h[p];
        i = p;
    }
    h[i] = x;
}

static void overlap_sift_down(Overlap *h, size_t n, size_t i, Overlap x) {
    for (;;) {
        size_t l = 2 * i + 1;
        if (l >= n) break;
        size_t c = l;
        if (l + 1 < n && overlap_before(h[l + 1], h[l])) c = l + 1;
        if (!overlap_before(h[c], x)) break;
        h[i] = h[c];
        i = c;
    }
    h[i] = x;
}

static Overlap overlap_pop(Overlap *h, size_t *n) {
    Overlap top = h[0], last = h[--(*n)];
    if (*n) overlap_sift_down(h, *n, 0, last);
    return top;
}
```

```c
bool solver_init_min_overlapping(Solver *s) {
    const Cnf *cnf = s->cnf;
    size_t nv = cnf->n_vars, nc = cnf->n_clauses, tot = s->occ_off[nv];
    uint32_t *unset = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *unset);
    unsigned char *done = calloc(nc ? nc : 1, 1);
    uint32_t *pos = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *pos);
    uint32_t *neg = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *neg);
    unsigned char *assigned = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1);
    size_t *overlap = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *overlap);
    uint32_t *hits = calloc(nc ? nc : 1, sizeof *hits);   /* assigned variables per clause */
    Overlap *heap = malloc((nv + tot + 1) * sizeof *heap);
    if (!unset || !done || !pos || !neg || !assigned || !overlap || !hits || !heap) {
        free(unset); free(done); free(pos); free(neg); free(assigned); free(overlap); free(hits); free(heap);
        return false;
    }
    for (size_t c = 0; c < nc; c++) unset[c] = (uint32_t)cnf_clause_len(cnf, c);
    for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++)
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++)
            if (s->occ[k].positive) pos[v]++; else neg[v]++;

    /* step 1 is glowest's pick: the largest single-polarity count, ties by id */
    size_t first = SIZE_MAX, first_key = 0;
    for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) {
        size_t key = pos[v] > neg[v] ? pos[v] : neg[v];
        if (first == SIZE_MAX || key > first_key) { first = v; first_key = key; }
    }
    size_t hn = 0;
    for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++)
        overlap_push(heap, &hn, (Overlap){ 0, pos[v] + neg[v], v });

    for (size_t step = 0; step < nv; step++) {
        size_t v;
        if (step == 0) {
            v = first;
        } else {
            Overlap top;
            do {
                top = overlap_pop(heap, &hn);
            } while (assigned[top.var] || top.num != overlap[top.var]
                     || top.den != pos[top.var] + neg[top.var]);
            v = top.var;
        }
        bool val = start_value(s, v, done, unset);
        s->assignment[v] = val;
        assigned[v] = 1;
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++) {
            Occ o = s->occ[k];
            size_t c = o.clause;
            unset[c]--;
            bool becomes_done = !done[c] && o.positive == val;
            if (becomes_done) done[c] = 1;
            bool first_hit = hits[c]++ == 0;
            if (!becomes_done && !first_hit) continue;
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(cnf, c);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(cnf, c);
            for (size_t j = 0; j < len; j++) {
                size_t u = cl[j].var;
                if (assigned[u]) continue;
                if (first_hit) overlap[u]++;
                if (becomes_done) { if (cl[j].positive) pos[u]--; else neg[u]--; }
                overlap_push(heap, &hn, (Overlap){ overlap[u], pos[u] + neg[u], u });
            }
        }
    }
    free(unset); free(done); free(pos); free(neg); free(assigned); free(overlap); free(hits); free(heap);
    rebuild_counts(s);
    return true;
}

/* Naive spec of --init min_overlapping: first set the variable with the largest
 * max(#x, #!x); then repeatedly set the unset variable with the smallest
 * (#clauses it shares with an already-set variable) / (#not-yet-satisfied
 * clauses holding it), 0/0 last, ties by id. Values follow the rarest rule. */
static void min_overlap_reference(const Cnf *c, bool *out) {
    size_t nv = c->n_vars, nc = c->n_clauses;
    bool *set = calloc(nv?nv:1,1), *done = calloc(nc?nc:1,1);
    for (size_t step = 0; step < nv; step++) {
        size_t v = SIZE_MAX;
        if (step == 0) {
            size_t best = 0;
            for (size_t x = 0; x < nv; x++) {
                if (set[x]) continue;
                size_t p=0,n=0;
                for (ci...) for(k...) if (var==x) pos?p++:n++;
                size_t key = p>n?p:n;
                if (v == SIZE_MAX || key > best) { v=x; best=key; }
            }
        } else {
            size_t best_num=0, best_den=1; bool have=false;
            for (x unset) {
                size_t den=0, num=0;
                for (ci) {
                    if (done[ci]) continue;
                    bool has=false; 
                    for (k) if (var==x) has=true;
                    if (has) den++;
                }
                // overlap over all clauses
                for (ci) {
                    bool hasx=false, has_set=false;
                    for (k) { if (var==x) hasx=true; if (set[var]) has_set=true; }
                    if (hasx && has_set) num++;
                }
                if (den == 0) { /* last */ if (!have) { v=x; have=true; best_num=0; best_den=0; } else if (best_den != 0) {} continue; }
                if (!have || best_den == 0 || num*best_den < best_num*den) { v=x; best_num=num; best_den=den; have=true; }
            }
        }
        // value rule same as rarest_reference
        ...
    }
}
```
Tie handling: iterate ascending, use strict < to keep lowest id. den==0: pick the first den==0 only if no den>0 candidate exists (i.e., treat den==0 as worst). If have with den==0 and new den>0 → replace ✓. If have with den>0 and new den==0 → skip ✓. If both den==0 → keep first (lowest id) ✓. If both >0 → compare ✓. Good.

/* Where restart 0 starts from (later restarts are random). */
typedef enum {
    INIT_MAJORITY,  /* every variable takes its majority polarity (default) */
    INIT_RAREST,    /* constructive: rarest variables first, see solver_init_rarest() */
    INIT_GLOWEST,   /* constructive: most frequent variables first, see solver_init_glowest() */
    INIT_LIKHO,     /* pre-cooked start (all false by default), then a one-flip-per-variable repair pass */
    INIT_ZERO       /* all false; Likho's phase 1, not selectable via --init */
} InitMode;

typedef struct {
const VarStats *solver_var_stats(Solver *s);  /* refreshes lazily if stale */
void solver_set_assignment(Solver *s, const bool *assignment);
void solver_flip(Solver *s, size_t var);
/* Deterministic constructive start (no RNG). Repeatedly takes the rarest unset
 * variable: fewest clauses holding x or !x (the larger of the two polarity counts,
 * satisfied clauses excluded, ties by id), recomputed after each assignment so a
 * satisfied clause drops its overlap from every remaining variable. A variable takes the value that
 *   1. satisfies more *forced* clauses (open clauses where it is the last unset variable),
 *   2. else satisfies more open (not yet satisfied) clauses,
 *   3. else has the larger total polarity, else false.
 * false only on allocation failure. */
bool solver_init_rarest(Solver *s);
/* Same constructive start as solver_init_rarest(), but takes the most frequent
 * unset variable first (most clauses holding x or !x, the larger of the two
 * counts, satisfied clauses excluded, ties by id). Deterministic, no RNG.
 * false only on allocation failure. */
bool solver_init_glowest(Solver *s);
void solver_init_majority(Solver *s);                  /* majority-polarity start (ties use the solver RNG) */

static Rare rare_pop(Rare *h, size_t *n) {
    Rare top = h[0], last = h[--(*n)];
    if (*n) rare_sift_down(h, *n, 0, last);
    return top;
}

/* Rarest = fewest clauses holding x or !x, whichever is larger; glowest = most.
 * Only clauses that are still unsatisfied count, so satisfying a clause removes
 * the overlapping occurrences of every variable it contains. The heap is a
 * min-heap in both modes: glowest inverts the key. A count only shrinks, so the
 * current key is re-pushed whenever it changes and a stale entry is simply
 * discarded when it pops. */
static size_t rare_key(const uint32_t *pos, const uint32_t *neg, size_t v, bool most) {
    size_t m = pos[v] > neg[v] ? pos[v] : neg[v];
    return most ? SIZE_MAX - m : m;
}

static bool init_frequency(Solver *s, bool most) {
    const Cnf *cnf = s->cnf;
    size_t nv = cnf->n_vars, nc = cnf->n_clauses;
    uint32_t *unset = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *unset);   /* unassigned variables left in each clause */
    unsigned char *done = calloc(nc ? nc : 1, 1);              /* clause already has a true literal */
    uint32_t *pos = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *pos);          /* effective: satisfied clauses dropped */
    uint32_t *neg = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *neg);
    unsigned char *assigned = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1);
    Rare *heap = malloc((nv + s->occ_off[nv] + 1) * sizeof *heap);
    if (!unset || !done || !pos || !neg || !assigned || !heap) {
        free(unset); free(done); free(pos); free(neg); free(assigned); free(heap);
        return false;
    }
    for (size_t c = 0; c < nc; c++) unset[c] = (uint32_t)cnf_clause_len(cnf, c);
    size_t hn = 0;
    for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) {
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++)
            if (s->occ[k].positive) pos[v]++; else neg[v]++;
        rare_push(heap, &hn, (Rare){ rare_key(pos, neg, v, most), v });
    }

    for (size_t step = 0; step < nv; step++) {
        Rare top;
        do {
            top = rare_pop(heap, &hn);
        } while (assigned[top.var] || top.key != rare_key(pos, neg, top.var, most));
        size_t v = top.var;
        size_t fp = 0, fn = 0, op = 0, on = 0, tp = 0, tn = 0;
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++) {
            Occ o = s->occ[k];
            if (o.positive) tp++; else tn++;
            if (done[o.clause]) continue;
            if (unset[o.clause] == 1) { if (o.positive) fp++; else fn++; }
            else                      { if (o.positive) op++; else on++; }
        }
        bool val;
        if (fp != fn) val = fp > fn;
        else if (op != on) val = op > on;
        else if (tp != tn) val = tp > tn;
        else val = false;
        s->assignment[v] = val;
        assigned[v] = 1;
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++) {
            Occ o = s->occ[k];
            unset[o.clause]--;
            if (done[o.clause] || o.positive != val) continue;
            done[o.clause] = 1;
            const Lit *cl = cnf_clause(cnf, o.clause);
            size_t len = cnf_clause_len(cnf, o.clause);
            for (size_t j = 0; j < len; j++) {
                size_t u = cl[j].var;
                if (assigned[u]) continue;
                if (cl[j].positive) pos[u]--; else neg[u]--;
                rare_push(heap, &hn, (Rare){ rare_key(pos, neg, u, most), u });
            }
        }
    }
    free(unset); free(done); free(pos); free(neg); free(assigned); free(heap);
    rebuild_counts(s);
    return true;
}

bool solver_init_rarest(Solver *s) { return init_frequency(s, false); }
bool solver_init_glowest(Solver *s) { return init_frequency(s, true); }

static bool vec_reserve(void **data, size_t *cap, size_t elem, size_t need) {
    if (need <= *cap) return true;
    size_t ncap = *cap ? *cap : 16;
    while (ncap < need) {
        if (ncap > SIZE_MAX / 2) return false;
        ncap *= 2;
    }
    if (ncap > SIZE_MAX / elem) return false;
    void *p = realloc(*data, ncap * elem);
    if (!p) return false;
    *data = p;
    *cap = ncap;
    return true;
}

static bool is_ws(char c) {
    return c == ' ' || c == '\t' || c == '\r' || c == '\n' || c == '\v' || c == '\f';
}

/* Strict integer parsing (optional sign, digits only), like Rust's parse(). */
static bool parse_u64(const char *s, size_t len, uint64_t *out, bool allow_sign, bool *neg) {
    size_t i = 0;
    *neg = false;
    if (allow_sign && i < len && (s[i] == '+' || s[i] == '-')) { *neg = s[i] == '-'; i++; }
    else if (!allow_sign && i < len && s[i] == '+') i++;
    if (i == len) return false;
    uint64_t acc = 0;
    for (; i < len; i++) {
        if (s[i] < '0' || s[i] > '9') return false;
        unsigned d = (unsigned)(s[i] - '0');
        if (acc > (UINT64_MAX - d) / 10) return false;
        acc = acc * 10 + d;
    }
    *out = acc;
    return true;
}

static bool parse_i64(const char *s, size_t len, int64_t *out) {
    uint64_t mag; bool neg;
    if (!parse_u64(s, len, &mag, true, &neg)) return false;
    if (neg) {
        if (mag > (uint64_t)INT64_MAX + 1) return false;
        *out = (int64_t)(0 - mag);
    } else {
        if (mag > (uint64_t)INT64_MAX) return false;
        *out = (int64_t)mag;
    }

typedef struct { size_t key, var; } Rare;

static bool rare_before(Rare a, Rare b) {
    if (a.key != b.key) return a.key < b.key;
    return a.var < b.var;
}

static void rare_push(Rare *h, size_t *n, Rare x) {
    size_t i = (*n)++;
    while (i > 0) {
        size_t p = (i - 1) / 2;
        if (!rare_before(x, h[p])) break;
        h[i] = h[p];
        i = p;
    }
    h[i] = x;
}

static void rare_sift_down(Rare *h, size_t n, size_t i, Rare x) {
    for (;;) {
        size_t l = 2 * i + 1;
        if (l >= n) break;
        size_t c = l;
        if (l + 1 < n && rare_before(h[l + 1], h[l])) c = l + 1;
        if (!rare_before(h[c], x)) break;
        h[i] = h[c];
        i = c;
    }
    h[i] = x;
}

static Rare rare_pop(Rare *h, size_t *n) {
    Rare top = h[0], last = h[--(*n)];
    if (*n) rare_sift_down(h, *n, 0, last);
    return top;
}

/* Rarest = fewest clauses holding x or !x, whichever is larger; glowest = most.
 * Only clauses that are still unsatisfied count, so satisfying a clause removes
 * the overlapping occurrences of every variable it contains. The heap is a
 * min-heap in both modes: glowest inverts the key. A count only shrinks, so the
 * current key is re-pushed whenever it changes and a stale entry is simply
 * discarded when it pops. */
static size_t rare_key(const uint32_t *pos, const uint32_t *neg, size_t v, bool most) {
    size_t m = pos[v] > neg[v] ? pos[v] : neg[v];
    return most ? SIZE_MAX - m : m;
}

typedef enum { FREQ_RAREST, FREQ_GLOWEST, OVERLAP_MIN } InitOrder;

typedef struct { size_t key, den, var; } Rare;

static bool rare_before(Rare a, Rare b) {
    /* key/den ascending; cross-multiplied so the ratio is exact. den is 1 for
     * the frequency orders. */
    if (a.key != b.key || a.den != b.den) {
        unsigned __int128 l = (unsigned __int128)a.key * b.den;
        unsigned __int128 r = (unsigned __int128)b.key * a.den;
        if (l != r) return l < r;
    }
    return a.var < b.var;
}

static bool rare_before(Rare a, Rare b) {

     * the two frequency orders. */

    unsigned __int128 r = (unsigned __int128)b.key * a.den;

    return a.var < b.var;
}

static void order_key(InitOrder mode, const uint32_t *pos, const uint32_t *neg,
                      const uint32_t *overlap, const size_t *total,
                      size_t v, size_t *key, size_t *den) {

}

/* Naive spec of --init rarest/glowest: every step recomputes, for each unset variable,
 * max(#x, #!x) over the clauses not yet satisfied, takes the smallest (rarest) or the
 * largest (glowest) key (ties: lowest id), then applies forced > open > total
 * polarity > false. No heap, no incremental counters. */
static void order_reference(const Cnf *c, bool *out, bool most) {
    size_t nv = c->n_vars, nc = c->n_clauses;
    bool *set = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1), *done = calloc(nc ? nc : 1, 1);
    for (size_t step = 0; step < nv; step++) {
        size_t best = SIZE_MAX, best_key = 0;
        for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) {
            if (set[v]) continue;
            size_t p = 0, n = 0;
            for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++) {
                if (done[ci]) continue;
                for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(c, ci); k++) {
                    Lit l = cnf_clause(c, ci)[k];
                    if (l.var == v) { if (l.positive) p++; else n++; }
                }
            }
            size_t key = p > n ? p : n;
            if (best == SIZE_MAX || (most ? key > best_key : key < best_key)) { best = v; best_key = key; }
        }
        size_t v = best, fp = 0, fn = 0, op = 0, on = 0, tp = 0, tn = 0;
        for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++) {
            size_t unset_here = 0;
            bool has = false, pos = false;
            for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(c, ci); k++) {
                Lit l = cnf_clause(c, ci)[k];
                if (!set[l.var]) unset_here++;
                if (l.var == v) { has = true; pos = l.positive; }
            }
            if (!has) continue;
            if (pos) tp++; else tn++;
            if (done[ci]) continue;
            if (unset_here == 1) { if (pos) fp++; else fn++; }
            else                 { if (pos) op++; else on++; }
        }
        bool val = (fp != fn) ? fp > fn : (op != on) ? op > on : (tp != tn) ? tp > tn : false;
        out[v] = val; set[v] = true;
        for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++)
            for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(c, ci); k++) {
                Lit l = cnf_clause(c, ci)[k];
                if (l.var == v && l.positive == val) done[ci] = true;
            }
    }
    free(set); free(done);
}

```c
typedef struct { size_t key, den, var; } Rare;

/* Ascending key/den, ties by variable id. den is 1 for the frequency orders
 * and the variable's occurrence count for the overlap order; ratios are compared
 * by cross-multiplication so the order is exact. A zero denominator (variable
 * with no occurrences) sorts last. */
static bool rare_before(Rare a, Rare b) {
    if ((a.den == 0) != (b.den == 0)) return b.den == 0;
    unsigned __int128 l = (unsigned __int128)a.key * b.den;
    unsigned __int128 r = (unsigned __int128)b.key * a.den;
    if (l != r) return l < r;
    return a.var < b.var;
}
```

Then push/sift/pop unchanged (they use rare_before).

```c
/* Rarest = fewest clauses holding x or !x, whichever is larger; glowest = most.
 * Only clauses that are still unsatisfied count, so satisfying a clause removes
 * the overlapping occurrences of every variable it contains. */
static size_t rare_key(const uint32_t *pos, const uint32_t *neg, size_t v, bool most) {
    size_t m = pos[v] > neg[v] ? pos[v] : neg[v];
    return most ? SIZE_MAX - m : m;
}

typedef enum { ORDER_RAREST, ORDER_GLOWEST, ORDER_MIN_OVERLAP } InitOrder;

/* Current key and denominator of v. min-overlap ranks a variable by the share
 * of its clauses already satisfied: satisfied occurrences / total occurrences. */
static void order_key(InitOrder mode, const uint32_t *pos, const uint32_t *neg,
                      const uint32_t *overlap, const size_t *total,
                      size_t v, size_t *key, size_t *den) {
    if (mode == ORDER_MIN_OVERLAP) { *key = overlap[v]; *den = total[v]; }
    else { *key = rare_key(pos, neg, v, mode == ORDER_GLOWEST); *den = 1; }
}

static void order_push(Rare *h, size_t *hn, InitOrder mode, const uint32_t *pos,
                       const uint32_t *neg, const uint32_t *overlap,
                       const size_t *total, size_t v) {
    size_t key, den;
    order_key(mode, pos, neg, overlap, total, v, &key, &den);
    rare_push(h, hn, (Rare){ key, den, v });
}

/* Constructive start. rarest/glowest take, at every step, the unset variable
 * with the fewest/most open clauses holding x or !x (the larger polarity count,
 * ties by id). min-overlap takes the most frequent variable first (glowest's
 * pick, ties by id) and then the one with the smallest share of its clauses
 * already satisfied, ties by id. A key only moves one way (frequency down,
 * overlap up), so the current entry is re-pushed whenever it changes and a stale
 * entry is discarded when it pops. */
static bool init_order(Solver *s, InitOrder mode) {
    const Cnf *cnf = s->cnf;
    size_t nv = cnf->n_vars, nc = cnf->n_clauses;
    uint32_t *unset = malloc((nc ? nc : 1) * sizeof *unset);
    unsigned char *done = calloc(nc ? nc : 1, 1);
    uint32_t *pos = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *pos);
    uint32_t *neg = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *neg);
    uint32_t *overlap = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *overlap);
    size_t *total = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, sizeof *total);
    unsigned char *assigned = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1);
    Rare *heap = malloc((nv + s->occ_off[nv] + 1) * sizeof *heap);
    if (!unset || !done || !pos || !neg || !overlap || !total || !assigned || !heap) {
        free(unset); free(done); free(pos); free(neg); free(overlap); free(total);
        free(assigned); free(heap);
        return false;
    }
    for (size_t c = 0; c < nc; c++) unset[c] = (uint32_t)cnf_clause_len(cnf, c);
    size_t hn = 0;
    for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) {
        total[v] = occ_count(s, v);
        for (size_t k = s->occ_off[v]; k < s->occ_off[v + 1]; k++)
            if (s->occ[k].positive) pos[v]++; else neg[v]++;
    }
    /* min-overlap's first pick is glowest's, so its heap starts after step 0. */
    if (mode != ORDER_MIN_OVERLAP)
        for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) order_push(heap, &hn, mode, pos, neg, overlap, total, v);

    for (size_t step = 0; step < nv; step++) {
        size_t v;
        if (mode == ORDER_MIN_OVERLAP && step == 0) {
            size_t best = 0;
            for (size_t u = 0; u < nv; u++) {
                size_t m = pos[u] > neg[u] ? pos[u] : neg[u];
                if (m > (pos[best] > neg[best] ? pos[best] : neg[best])) best = u;
            }
            v = best;
        } else {
            Rare top;
            size_t key, den;

                order_key(mode, pos, neg, overlap, total, top.var, &key, &den);
            } while (assigned[top.var] || top.key != key || top.den != den);
            v = top.var;

typedef struct { size_t key, den, var; } Rare;

/* Ascending key/den, ties by variable id. den is 1 for the frequency orders and
 * the variable's occurrence count for the overlap order; ratios are compared by
 * cross-multiplication so the order stays exact. A zero denominator (variable
 * with no occurrences) sorts last. */
static bool rare_before(Rare a, Rare b) {
    if ((a.den == 0) != (b.den == 0)) return b.den == 0;
    unsigned __int128 l = (unsigned __int128)a.key * b.den;
    unsigned __int128 r = (unsigned __int128)b.key * a.den;
    if (l != r) return l < r;
    return a.var < b.var;
}
```

 * current key is re-pushed whenever it changes and a stale entry is simply
 * discarded when it pops. */
static size_t rare_key(const uint32_t *pos, const uint32_t *neg, size_t v, bool most) {

/* Rarest = fewest clauses holding x or !x, whichever is larger; glowest = most.
 * Only clauses that are still unsatisfied count, so satisfying a clause removes
 * the overlapping occurrences of every variable it contains. */
static size_t rare_key(const uint32_t *pos, const uint32_t *neg, size_t v, bool most) {
    size_t m = pos[v] > neg[v] ? pos[v] : neg[v];
    return most ? SIZE_MAX - m : m;
}

typedef enum { ORDER_RAREST, ORDER_GLOWEST, ORDER_MIN_OVERLAP } InitOrder;

/* Current key and denominator of v. min-overlap ranks a variable by the share of
 * its occurrences that sit in already satisfied clauses. */
static void order_key(InitOrder mode, const uint32_t *pos, const uint32_t *neg,
                      const uint32_t *overlap, const size_t *total,
                      size_t v, size_t *key, size_t *den) {
    if (mode == ORDER_MIN_OVERLAP) { *key = overlap[v]; *den = total[v]; }
    else { *key = rare_key(pos, neg, v, mode == ORDER_GLOWEST); *den = 1; }
}

static void order_push(Rare *h, size_t *hn, InitOrder mode, const uint32_t *pos,
                       const uint32_t *neg, const uint32_t *overlap,
                       const size_t *total, size_t v) {
    size_t key, den;
    order_key(mode, pos, neg, overlap, total, v, &key, &den);
    rare_push(h, hn, (Rare){ key, den, v });
}

/* Constructive start. rarest/glowest take at every step the unset variable with
 * the fewest/most open clauses holding x or !x (the larger polarity count, ties
 * by id). min-overlap takes the most frequent variable first (glowest's pick,
 * ties by id), then the one with the smallest share of its occurrences already
 * in satisfied clauses, ties by id. A key only moves one way, so the current
 * entry is re-pushed whenever it changes and a stale entry is discarded when it
 * pops. */
static bool init_order(Solver *s, InitOrder mode) {

}

/* Naive spec of --init rarest/glowest: every step recomputes, for each unset variable,
 * max(#x, #!x) over the clauses not yet satisfied, takes the smallest (rarest) or the
 * largest (glowest) key (ties: lowest id), then applies forced > open > total
 * polarity > false. No heap, no incremental counters. */
static void order_reference(const Cnf *c, bool *out, bool most) {
    size_t nv = c->n_vars, nc = c->n_clauses;
    bool *set = calloc(nv ? nv : 1, 1), *done = calloc(nc ? nc : 1, 1);
    for (size_t step = 0; step < nv; step++) {
        size_t best = SIZE_MAX, best_key = 0;
        for (size_t v = 0; v < nv; v++) {
            if (set[v]) continue;
            size_t p = 0, n = 0;
            for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++) {
                if (done[ci]) continue;
                for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(c, ci); k++) {
                    Lit l = cnf_clause(c, ci)[k];
                    if (l.var == v) { if (l.positive) p++; else n++; }
                }
            }
            size_t key = p > n ? p : n;
            if (best == SIZE_MAX || (most ? key > best_key : key < best_key)) { best = v; best_key = key; }
        }
        size_t v = best, fp = 0, fn = 0, op = 0, on = 0, tp = 0, tn = 0;
        for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++) {
            size_t unset_here = 0;
            bool has = false, pos = false;
            for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(c, ci); k++) {
                Lit l = cnf_clause(c, ci)[k];
                if (!set[l.var]) unset_here++;
                if (l.var == v) { has = true; pos = l.positive; }
            }
            if (!has) continue;
            if (pos) tp++; else tn++;
            if (done[ci]) continue;
            if (unset_here == 1) { if (pos) fp++; else fn++; }
            else                 { if (pos) op++; else on++; }
        }
        bool val = (fp != fn) ? fp > fn : (op != on) ? op > on : (tp != tn) ? tp > tn : false;
        out[v] = val; set[v] = true;
        for (size_t ci = 0; ci < nc; ci++)
            for (size_t k = 0; k < cnf_clause_len(c, ci); k++) {
                Lit l = cnf_clause(c, ci)[k];
                if (l.var == v && l.positive == val) done[ci] = true;
            }
    }
    free(set); free(done);
}

static void check_order_matches_reference(const Cnf *c, bool most) {
    Solver *s = must_solver(c, 1);
    bool *ref = malloc(c->n_vars ? c->n_vars : 1);
    CHECK(most ? solver_init_glowest(s) : solver_init_rarest(s));
    order_reference(c, ref, most);
    CHECK(c->n_vars == 0 || memcmp(solver_assignment(s), ref, c->n_vars) == 0);
    CHECK(solver_unsatisfied_count(s) == brute_unsat(c, ref));
    free(ref);
    solver_free(s);
}

static void check_order_corpus(bool most) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 150; i++) {                           /* random 3-SAT, easy to hard */
        int n = 8 + (i % 7) * 9;
        Cnf c = random_cnf(n, (int)(n * (1.0 + 0.5 * (i % 9))), 9000 + (uint64_t)i);
        check_order_matches_reference(&c, most);
        cnf_free(&c);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < 150; i++) {                           /* general CNF: units, long clauses, unused vars */
        int n = 5 + (i % 6) * 7;
        Cnf c = random_general_cnf(n * 2, n + (i % 5) * 6, 1 + (i % 6), 4000 + (uint64_t)i);
        check_order_matches_reference(&c, most);
        cnf_free(&c);
    }
    Cnf e = must_parse("p cnf 0 0\n");
    check_order_matches_reference(&e, most);
    cnf_free(&e);
    Cnf one = must_parse("p cnf 1 1\n-1 0\n");
    check_order_matches_reference(&one, most);
    cnf_free(&one);
}

static void test_init_rarest_matches_reference(void) { check_order_corpus(false); }
static void test_init_glowest_matches_reference(void) { check_order_corpus(true); }

                       "-2 4 1 0\n-2 4 1 0\n-2 4 1 0\n-3 4 1 0\n-3 4 1 0\n-3 4 1 0\n");

            random_assignment(s, restart == 0);
        }
        for (size_t step = 0; step < cfg->max_steps; step++) {
            if (s->n_rogue == 0) return make_sat(s, total, restart);
            if (s->n_rogue < best) best = s->n_rogue;
            size_t clause = s->rogue[rng_index(&s->rng, s->n_rogue)];
            size_t n = rank_candidates(s, clause);
            if (n == 0) break;
            solver_flip(s, pick(&s->rng, s->cands, n, cfg->noise));
            total++;
            if (cfg->on_progress && cfg->progress_every && total % cfg->progress_every == 0)
                cfg->on_progress(cfg->progress_ctx, total, s->n_rogue);
        }
        if (s->n_rogue == 0) return make_sat(s, total, restart);  /* last flip solved it */
    }

static void test_init_glowest_hand_checked(void) {
    /* Glowest by max(#x,#!x): x1 has 2, x2 and x3 have 1, so x1 goes first.
     * Both clauses are open and positive for x1, so it goes true and satisfies
     * them; x2 and x3 then have no open clause and tie on total polarity, so
     * both go false. */
    Cnf c = must_parse("p cnf 3 3\n1 2 0\n1 3 0\n-2 -3 0\n");
    Solver *s = must_solver(&c, 1);
    CHECK(solver_init_glowest(s));
    const bool *a = solver_assignment(s);
    CHECK(a[0] && !a[1] && !a[2]);
    CHECK(solver_unsatisfied_count(s) == 0);
    solver_free(s);

    /* solver_solve's restart-0 dispatch must take the same start. */
    Solver *d = must_solver(&c, 1);
    SolverConfig sc = solver_config_default();
    sc.init = INIT_GLOWEST;
    sc.max_steps = 0;
    sc.restarts = 0;
    ResultSolve r = solver_solve(d, &sc);
    const bool *da = solver_assignment(d);
    CHECK(r.ok && da[0] && !da[1] && !da[2]);
    if (r.ok) solve_result_free(&r.val);
    solver_free(d);

    SolverConfig cfg = solver_config_default();          /* and the group solver */
    cfg.init = INIT_GLOWEST;
    GroupConfig gc = group_config_default();
    gc.max_groups = 8;
    ResultGroup g = group_solve(&c, &cfg, &gc);
    CHECK(g.ok);
    if (g.ok) { check_group_result(&c, &g.val); group_result_free(&g.val); }
    cnf_free(&c);

    /* variable that occurs nowhere is set false */
    Cnf e = must_parse("p cnf 3 1\n1 2 0\n");
    s = must_solver(&e, 1);
    CHECK(solver_init_glowest(s));
    CHECK(!solver_assignment(s)[2]);
    solver_free(s); cnf_free(&e);
}

static void test_init_min_overlap_hand_checked(void) {
    /* Step 0 is glowest's pick: x4 and x5 both have max(#x,#!x)=3, so x4 (lower
     * id) goes first and, all-negative, goes false. That satisfies clauses 1, 4,
     * 5. Then the least-overlapping variable is x1 (0 of 1 occurrences already
     * satisfied), not x5 (3 of 5), so x1 goes true. Next x2 and x6 tie at 1 of 2
     * and x2 wins by id; x2 goes true. x5 (5/5) and x6 (2/2) follow, both false.
     * Glowest instead takes x5 at step 1 and ends with x2 false, so this pins
     * the order. */
    Cnf c = must_parse("p cnf 6 5\n"
                       "5 -4 -2 0\n"
                       "-5 2 6 0\n"
                       "-5 1 0\n"
                       "-4 -5 0\n"
                       "-6 5 -4 0\n");
    Solver *s = must_solver(&c, 1);
    CHECK(solver_init_min_overlap(s));
    const bool *a = solver_assignment(s);
    CHECK(a[0] && a[1] && !a[2] && !a[3] && !a[4] && !a[5]);
    CHECK(solver_unsatisfied_count(s) == 0);
    solver_free(s);

    Solver *g = must_solver(&c, 1);          /* glowest's order differs */
    CHECK(solver_init_glowest(g));
    CHECK(!solver_assignment(g)[1]);
    solver_free(g);

    /* solver_solve's restart-0 dispatch must take the same start. */
    Solver *d = must_solver(&c, 1);
    SolverConfig sc = solver_config_default();
    sc.init = INIT_MIN_OVERLAP;
    sc.max_steps = 0;
    sc.restarts = 0;
    ResultSolve r = solver_solve(d, &sc);
    const bool *da = solver_assignment(d);
    CHECK(r.ok && da[0] && da[1] && !da[2] && !da[3] && !da[4] && !da[5]);
    if (r.ok) solve_result_free(&r.val);
    solver_free(d);

    SolverConfig cfg = solver_config_default();          /* and the group solver */
    cfg.init = INIT_MIN_OVERLAP;
    GroupConfig gc = group_config_default();
    gc.max_groups = 8;
    ResultGroup gr = group_solve(&c, &cfg, &gc);
    CHECK(gr.ok);
    if (gr.ok) { check_group_result(&c, &gr.val); group_result_free(&gr.val); }
    cnf_free(&c);
}
